title: Recreation Specialist III - Special Events ($26.06/hour - $35.16/hour)
description:
Do you have a passion for Special Events and building community connections? Are you experienced in supporting and coordinating events that bring people together?

The Hayward Area Recreation and Park District (H.A.R.D.) is currently hiring a part-time Recreation Specialist III to join our Special Events Team! This position will work under the direction of a Recreation Coordinator II, helping to plan, lead and execute a wide variety of community-focused events throughout the year.

As a Recreation Specialist III, you will assist in the coordination, logistics, and support of community events for all ages including programming, volunteer coordination, enrichment preparation, supply purchasing and other support functions. This position will also assist with vendor outreach, volunteer communication, and scheduling.

We are looking for someone who is organized, creative, and passionate about recreation and community building. Previous special event experience highly desired.

Here are the details about the positions:

  • Available Positions: 1
  • Hourly Rate: $26.06/hour - $35.16/hour
  • Work Location: Multiple Parks and Sites within the District
  • Typical Work hours: 18 hours/week, Friday – Monday as needed – Schedule based on program needs
  • Part-Time, Year-Round, Hourly, Non-Exempt Position
  • Anticipated Start Date: ASAP
  • Not to exceed 960 hours per fiscal year. (July 1 – June 30)

POSITION SUMMARY

Under direction, performs difficult, complex and specialized recreation program work; oversees recreational programs for specific age groups and interests; develops recreation program/course content; conducts classes and trains subordinates within a specialized service area including, but not limited to: officiating; Class B driving; unique instructional classes or workshops; security; special projects, and/or graphic design; performs special project and graphic design work; and performs related work as required.

DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS

This is a highly specialized class that is separate from the Program Aide class. Incumbents in this class typically perform complex and difficult work within one or more specific program areas.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Incumbents may not perform all duties. Duties include but are not limited to the following:
  • Plans, organizes and conducts classes in specialty fields for groups of various ages and interests; develops course content and designs course materials
  • Provides oversight for specific projects, programs and special events; and
  • Coordinates programs with City staff and commissions.
  • Serves as a subject matter expert and trains subordinates within a specialty field
  • Stimulates interest and appreciation for the specialty field
  • Maintains and operates specialized equipment; procures supplies for classes
  • Provides technical guidance to students by demonstrating methods and conducting training in an area of specialty
  • Maintains control of classes or groups
  • Addresses participant complaints; communicates with parents and/or participants regarding the complaint; takes action to resolve the complaint based on policy and procedure and within limits of authority
  • Maintains records of participation and collects participant fees
  • Implements and monitors District procedures regarding the safety of participants
  • Performs administrative duties such as attending/scheduling staff meetings, preparing reports, and monitoring expenditures; administers program budgets and contracts
  • At all times, demonstrates cooperative behavior with colleagues, supervisors and the public
  • Performs other duties as assigned

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential duties and responsibilities of this position. The functions of this position may be performed in both indoor and outdoor locations, alone or as part of a team. In an indoor environment, the setting may be consistent with an office environment or a specialized recreational venue. In an outdoor environment, incumbents may occasionally be exposed inclement weather conditions. Specialized aspects of the work environment may also include high noise levels, exposure to equipment with moving parts, and exposure to dust. Incumbents may be assigned an irregular working schedule, including weekends, evenings and holidays and may frequently have to travel between various locations.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential duties and responsibilities of this position. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to have: hearing and speech adequate to communicate in person, by telephone, by PA system and by radio; vision adequate to read fine print and computer screens; bodily movement adequate to sit, walk, and stand frequently, and to reach, turn, bend, kneel, push and pull occasionally; manual dexterity adequate to grasp objects, use fine manipulation, write and operate office machines and equipment; and strength to safely perform lifting and carrying of items up to 50 pounds.

title: ASSISTANT DIRECTOR OF THE AMBASSADOR CHORALE (5031)
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

POSITION/ JOB FAMILY: Assistant Director of the Ambassador Chorale

DIVISION/DEPARTMENT: Visual and Performing Arts | School of Arts & Sciences

FLSA STATUS: Full-Time Staff | Exempt

REPORTS TO: Director of the Ambassador Chorale

The Assistant Director of the Ambassador Chorale shall have the primary responsibility of assisting the Director in providing musical instruction, rehearsal leadership, and artistic support for the Ambassador Chorale. This position requires the ability to create meaningful experiences with students that are inspiring, engaging, exciting, and transformative while fostering artistic growth, discipline, and confidence through the study, practice, and performance of music in both academic and social settings. This position also requires participation in weekend rehearsals, performances, tours, and university-related travel. The candidate must possess the ability and flexibility to travel and perform on weekday evenings, weekends, and as required by the performance schedule and operational needs of the Ambassador Chorale.

Essential Functions

  • Assist and support in fostering an environment and culture that inspires students to grow and supports the educational focus and institutional objectives of the chorale program and university.
  • Create an environment of active and genuine learning by employing a range of teaching strategies that meet the needs of all students.
  • Provide musical instruction and rehearsal leadership for undergraduate students enrolled in the Ambassador Chorale.
  • Support the Director of the Ambassador Chorale in advancing student learning outcomes, vocal development, musical excellence, and ensemble performance standards.
  • Assist students in developing healthy vocal techniques, musicianship skills, stage presence, and ensemble awareness.
  • Demonstrate the ability to work effectively with students from diverse musical, cultural, and educational backgrounds.
  • Teach vocal parts accurately and efficiently, with strong aural skills and the ability to hear, identify, and instruct individual vocal lines within ensemble settings.
  • Demonstrate proficiency in teaching and rehearsing music in various idioms. i.e. gospel, classical chorale literature, and jazz vocal styles.
  • Assist with sectional rehearsals, performance preparation, repertoire instruction, and ensemble coordination.
  • Manage, prioritize, and successfully complete multiple tasks and projects simultaneously within a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
  • Assist in promoting the mission, visibility, and artistic excellence of the Ambassador Chorale through performances, outreach activities, and recruitment initiatives.
  • Skills and abilities required: Previous conducting/directing skills are desirable.
  • The omission of specific duties does not preclude the supervisor from assigning duties that logically relate to the position.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Previous conducting and chorale directive experience is required.
  • Knowledge of chorale rehearsal techniques, vocal pedagogy, ensemble development, and performance preparation.
  • Strong musicianship skills, including sight-reading, score study, ear training, and vocal part instruction.
  • Advanced piano proficiency with the ability to accompany the choir during rehearsals, performances, and instructional settings.
  • Ability to accompany vocal ensembles effectively while simultaneously providing music direction and instruction to the rhythm section.
  • Ability to teach and rehearse music in multiple styles, including gospel, classical chorale literature, jazz choir, and vocal jazz idioms.
  • Strong oral, written, interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to motivate, mentor, and develop undergraduate students.
  • Maintain professionalism, collaboration, and effective communication with students, faculty, staff, and community partners.
  • Skilled multitasker. Detail-oriented skill set needed.
  • Ability to work effectively with students of varying musical backgrounds, skill levels, and experiences.
  • Demonstrated organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple assignments and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Proficiency in MS Office Suite, music software, as well as knowledge and understanding of the organizational structure, workflow, and operating procedures. Familiarity with Jenzabar technology suite for higher education.
  • A record showing commitment to customer service and the application of appropriate flexibility in response to issues and opposing points of view.
  • Proficiency in basic administrative tasks, music organization, scheduling, and ensemble coordination.
  • Commitment to fostering a positive, inclusive, and student-centered learning environment that promotes respect, accountability, confidence, professionalism, punctuality, and artistic excellence.
  • Ability to handle information of a sensitive and confidential nature in the utmost professional manner.
  • Demonstrate a high level of professionalism, initiative, resourcefulness, and personal accountability.
  • Moderate physical activity. Requires handling objects of average weight up to fifty (50) pounds or standing and/or walking for more than four (4) hours per day.

Minimum Requirements

  • The position requires a bachelor's degree.
  • Chorale Music/Conducting Master's Degree is preferred. Grade 5/6 level performance and sight-reading skills.
  • Preferred qualifications: Experience directing groups.
  • Demonstrated skill on instrument or voice.
  • Demonstrated sensitivity to and desire to promote diversity.
  • An active passion for music and the local and international scene.
  • Ability to maintain a flexible work schedule that may include working nights and weekends (if applicable).

Pre-Employment Requirements

  • Criminal background check

Florida Memorial University is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. In compliance with the American Disabilities Act (ADA), those functions of the job that are identified as essential are required to be performed with or without reasonable accommodations. Requests to facilitate the performance of essential functions will be given careful consideration.

About this role:

Wells Fargo is seeking a Senior Lead Control Management Officer. The Senior Lead Control Management Officer will serve as a key member of the Technology Control Management organization, responsible for strengthening the control environment within the Cloud Platform organization. This role will provide strategic control oversight and risk leadership for enterprise infrastructure services, cloud platform adoption, platform engineering, and control modernization initiatives focused on Control-as-Code, automated governance, and continuous control monitoring.


The individual will partner closely with Infrastructure Engineering leaders, Cloud Platform Engineering, Information Security, Technology Risk, Cloud GRC, Audit, and Control Management teams to establish and maintain a strong control environment that enables secure technology transformation while ensuring regulatory compliance and operational resilience.


In This Role, You Will

  • Act as a trusted advisor to senior technology and control management leaders in developing risk mitigation strategies for complex infrastructure and cloud-related risks.
  • Lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of control frameworks supporting:
    • Infrastructure Engineering
    • Cloud Platforms (Azure, AWS, GCP, OpenShift, Kubernetes)
    • Storage, Compute, Network, Database, and Middleware Services
    • Platform Engineering initiatives
  • Lead the adoption of Control-as-Code principles across Infrastructure Engineering and Cloud Platforms, including continuous compliance monitoring and automated evidence collection.
  • Propose governance standards and operating models for automated preventive, detective, and corrective controls.
  • Provide strategic oversight of enterprise technology risk, operational risk, resiliency risk, and regulatory compliance requirements.
  • Proactively identify and assess emerging risks related to cloud adoption, hybrid cloud architectures, automation, AI-enabled infrastructure operations, platform engineering, and infrastructure modernization.
  • Monitor, measure, evaluate, and report on the effectiveness of controls and risk mitigation strategies, analyzing Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), issues, control testing, and operational loss data to identify systemic risk trends.
  • Lead complex risk and control governance activities, including preparation of executive-level reporting, risk committee materials, and regulatory updates.
  • Provide risk and control expertise in engagement with Audit, Compliance, Independent Risk Management, and regulators.
  • Coordinate issue management activities, including root-cause analysis and sustainable corrective action plans.
  • Serve as the control management lead for major infrastructure and cloud transformation programs.
  • Mentor and guide control officers and virtual teams supporting technology control execution.

Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years of Risk Management or Financial Services Industry experience, or equivalent experience demonstrated through one or a combination of the following: work experience, training, military experience, or education.
  • 7+ years of Control Management, Technology Risk, Information Security experience.

Desired Qualifications

  • Knowledge of IT, information security, and cloud management and control frameworks (e.g., NIST Cybersecurity Framework and 800-53, CIS Critical Security Controls, FFIEC IT Examination Handbooks, COBIT, FedRAMP, ISO 2700x, ITIL).
  • Strong control evaluation, testing, and/or audit experience, including assessing risk, drafting and executing test scripts, identifying gaps in controls and control execution, assessing issues and trends, and influencing change.
  • Strong risk and control fundamentals, including a comprehensive understanding of risk types, methodologies, and frameworks for evaluating or testing controls, assessing results, conducting research, and identifying control deficiencies.
  • Technology risk acumen and a clear understanding of policies and standards associated with Technology and Cyber Security Risk.
  • Experience leading audit engagements and providing feedback to staff.
  • Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Experience supporting large-scale infrastructure or cloud modernization programs.

    • CRISC / CISA
    • CISSP / CCSP

title: Salesforce Business Analyst
description:
About the role

We’re looking for a Salesforce Business Analyst to join our delivery team and play a central role on client engagements. You’ll work closely with business stakeholders and technical teams to translate requirements into actionable Salesforce solutions. You will lead discovery sessions, capture and synthesize requirements, write user stories, and produce documentation that keeps complex workstreams moving. This is a hands-on BA role where organization, precision, and structured thinking matter as much as Salesforce knowledge. If you’re the person who leaves every meeting with clean notes, tight action items, and a ticket ready to write, we want to talk.

Employment Type: Full-Time 1099 Contractor
Compensation Range: $60-$85 per hour

Key Responsibilities:

  • Plan and facilitate discovery sessions with client stakeholders. Prepare agendas, ask the right questions, and ensure every session has a clear output.
  • Capture and synthesize session notes in real time: document decisions, open questions, and action items while the conversation is still happening, and distribute clean summaries promptly.
  • Write clear, developer-ready user stories and acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then format) for Salesforce configuration, automation, and integration work. Provide enough detail that a developer can build and a tester can verify without a follow-up meeting.
  • Own your documentation end to end. Maintain well-organized Confluence pages, Jira backlogs, and project artifacts that are current, navigable, and useful to the whole team.
  • Serve as the connective tissue between business stakeholders and technical teams. Translate needs in both directions and keep track of what was agreed.
  • Support UAT by writing test scripts, coordinating testers, and tracking defects through resolution.
  • Identify scope risks, open questions, and dependencies early. Escalate with context, not just flags.
  • Contribute to internal process improvement and knowledge-sharing as part of a growing consulting team.

Required Qualifications

  • 2–5 years of experience as a Salesforce Business Analyst, ideally in a consulting or SI environment.
  • 1–2 years of hands-on experience in a Salesforce Administrator role — required. This foundation is non-negotiable: we expect you to understand how the platform works, not just how to document it.
  • Salesforce Administrator Certification
  • Solid working knowledge of Sales Cloud and Service Cloud. You understand the objects, the relationships, and how configuration choices affect end users.
  • Demonstrated experience facilitating discovery and requirements sessions with non-technical stakeholders. This includes preparation, facilitation, and post-session documentation.
  • Strong note-taking and synthesis skills: you can walk out of a 90-minute session with a clean summary, open question log, and decision record that everyone can rely on.
  • Demonstrated ability to write user stories and structured acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then) that developers and QA can act on without follow-up.
  • Exceptional organizational skills. You manage your own backlog, maintain your documentation proactively, and don’t let things fall through the cracks across multiple workstreams.
  • Strong written communication skills. Your tickets, session notes, and project docs are precise, well-structured, and easy for others to navigate.
  • Proficiency with Jira and/or Confluence (or equivalent project tracking and documentation tools).
  • 1+ Years of consulting experience.

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience with Health Cloud or working in a healthcare client environment.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce org migration or consolidation projects.
  • Exposure to integration-adjacent BA work (e.g., API-based integrations, middleware, EHR/Epic touchpoints).
  • Salesforce Business Analyst Certification
  • Experience writing or contributing to UAT scripts and supporting formal test cycles.

What Success Looks Like

In the first 90 days, you’re oriented on client context and actively contributing to at least one engagement. You are facilitating or co-facilitating discovery sessions, producing clean session notes and summaries, writing stories, and managing your ticket backlog with minimal hand-holding. Within six months, stakeholders trust your documentation, developers rarely need to come back for clarification, and your Confluence pages are the team’s source of truth. You make the work legible.

Why Join Us?

  • Work on substantive, complex Salesforce engagements — not cookie-cutter implementations.
  • A tight-knit team where your work is visible and your voice matters.
  • Opportunities to grow into senior BA, PM, or solution architecture tracks.
  • Remote-first culture with collaborative, structured delivery practices.
  • Exposure to healthcare and enterprise Salesforce at scale.

    To ensure a fair and accurate evaluation process, candidates are expected to complete interviews independently without the use of AI-assisted tools, external coaching, or unauthorized assistance. Please note that interviews may be recorded with your consent for evaluation and quality purposes. If we determine the interview process is not being completed independently, the interview may be discontinued.

title: Trade Surveillance Analyst
description:
About the Company

Sei Labs is a unicorn startup based in NYC building Sei, the fastest EVM blockchain in the world designed for trading. We’re building a decentralized Wall Street. We’re a lean, remote-first team that ships fast, takes full ownership of outcomes and builds from first principles.

Sei Labs is incubating a new US regulated exchange from zero to one. You’d be the first hire in your function, with the speed and ownership of a startup and the backing of an established company and an S-tier team (Robinhood, Coinbase, Google, etc.)

About the role

As our first trading Surveillance Analyst, you will be a founding member of the DCM’s market regulation function. You will monitor trading activity on the exchange, investigate alerts, and help build the surveillance program, procedures and tooling we launch with. This role starts hands-on and detail-heavy. As the exchange goes live and the team grows, there is a clear path to more complex investigations and team leadership.

What you’ll do

  • Monitor real-time and post-trade activity for potential manipulation, fraud and disruptive trading practices (spoofing, layering, wash trading, pre-arranged trading, position-limit breaches and similar).

  • Triage and investigate alerts in our surveillance platform: reconstruct orders and trades, decide whether an alert is an error, a false positive or a potential violation, and document the reasoning clearly.

  • Run participant inquiry workflows, including broker explanation requests, and work directly with FCMs and clearing members to gather information and resolve cases.

  • Escalate potential rule violations and prepare well-documented case files for review, enforcement and regulatory inquiries, under the direction of the head of trade surveillance and/or market regulation.

  • Help design our case-management flow, alert tuning and automation so the program scales as volume grows.

  • Contribute to written surveillance procedures and DCM Core Principle readiness ahead of launch.

  • Ownhigh-volume first-line alert review, and earn broader investigative ownership as the function grows.

  • Participate in coverage for a 24/7 market, which may include scheduled weekend or off-hours rotations.

What you bring

  • 2–5+ years in trade or market surveillance at an exchange or regulator (e.g., DCM, national securities exchage, CFTC, SEC, NFA, or FINRA) strongly preferred; trading compliance experience at an FCM, broker-dealer, or trading firm strongly considered.

  • Hands-on experience investigating surveillance alerts, ideally in Nasdaq SMARTS or a comparable platform (Eventus Validus, TT Score, NICE Actimize, Solidus, b-next).

  • Working knowledge of manipulative and disruptive trading patterns and how to evidence them.

  • Experience with digital assets and digital assets investigations, as well as traditional financial instruments and futures or other derivatives, including on-chain analysis and forensic tracing of wallets and fund flows using tools such as Chainalysis, TRM Labs, or Elliptic..

  • Clear, professional written and verbal communication. You will deal directly with external FCMs and clearing members.

  • Strong attention to detail and disciplined documentation habits.

  • Comfort with ambiguity, shifting priorities and building process where none exists yet.

  • Ability to work from approved security devices and environments, and to comply with information barrier, conflict-of-interest, and personal trading policies, including restrictions on trading in markets we surveil.

Nice to have

  • SQL, Python or other data tooling for analysis and automating repetitive surveillance work.

  • Experience with 24/7 markets, or crypto derivatives.

  • Exposure to CFTC/NFA regulation, DCM Core Principles or rule-enforcement reviews.

  • Interest in growing into a team lead or manager role as the function scales.

Michelin is hiring! We are looking for a top candidate with a passion for Materials and Supplier Relations to be a part of our Research & Development Engineering team.


The Opportunity

For 130 years, Michelin has innovated to improve the mobility of people and goods. Today, we are setting the benchmark across tire and related services markets, while leading a global strategy to drive sustainable, profitable growth.

We have an immediate opening for a Senior Pipeline Materials Engineer with a focus on reinforcing fillers or colloidal science, who is the technical interface between Michelin and external raw material suppliers. The Senior Pipeline Materials Engineer will learn and develop an understanding of the processes and products of the raw material suppliers and how those can impact Michelin’s manufactured products and processes. Come join our team of Materials scientists and engineers in a collaborative environment to develop the next generation of tire lines and deliver future technologies to markets around the world.

Situated in Greenville, South Carolina, the sprawling Michelin Americas Research Center (MARC) campus is home to approximately 650 talented employees, including materials researchers, product designers, scientists, engineers, test technicians and individuals in a variety of support roles.

Our team contributes to designing, testing, and industrializing the innovative products that earn Michelin’s deserving place as one of the world’s leading tire manufacturers.

Greenville, SC is conveniently located within driving distance to east coast beaches, the Blue Ridge Mountains and large cities like Atlanta and Charlotte. The mild climate, charming downtown, and impressive culinary scene are just a few of the perks of living here.


What you will do

  • Complete a training program on both raw materials and composite material design. This training consists of both formal classes and project-style training while being mentored by an experienced area expert.
  • Manage technical relationships with the raw material suppliers of a specific raw materials domain (examples: reinforcing fillers, chemicals, petrochemicals, elastomers, natural rubber, etc.).
  • Support internal and external innovation through the industrialization of new raw materials.
  • Understand raw material supplier processes and product characteristics and how they impact Michelin’s products, processes, and costs.
  • Ensure technical approvals of raw materials based on the needs of our partners in industry, purchasing, supply chain, and design. This includes risk analyses and project management.
  • Conduct Supplier Quality Assurance Audits and Technical Visits, assess supplier processes, define progress actions, and follow-up on quality results.
  • Manage technical issues pertaining to raw materials coming from Michelin factories and work to define action plans for progress and/or improvement.
  • Ensure integrity of technical data in the information systems relative to raw materials.

What you will bring

  • PhD or Master’s with equivalent experience in Chemistry, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, or a related engineering field (ex. Polymer Science, etc.).
  • Desired background in colloidal science, reinforcing fillers, and/or soft flexible composites.
  • Intellectual curiosity and a spirit of continuous learning and adaptability.
  • The ability to collaborate and communicate in a professional manner with external partners, suppliers, customers, and colleagues (domestic and global) – to be receptive to their needs and provide solutions accordingly.
  • Ability to represent the supplier at Michelin and Michelin at the supplier by demonstrating both professionalism and ethics.
  • Self-motivation with a high degree of integrity and able to perform job duties with minimal direction on a timely basis. Able to prioritize and handle multiple projects simultaneously in an organized manner.
  • Leadership, communication, organizational, and technical skills.

#LI-RG1

Ready to Shape the Future of Innovation?

Michelin is building a world-leading manufacturer of life-changing composites and experiences. Pioneering engineered materials for more than 130 years, Michelin is uniquely positioned to make decisive contributions to human progress and a more sustainable world. Drawing on its deep know-how in polymer composite materials, Michelin is constantly innovating to manufacture high-quality tires and components for critical applications in demanding fields as varied as mobility, construction, aeronautics, low-carbon energies and healthcare.

The care placed in its products and deep customer knowledge inspire Michelin to offer the finest experiences. This spans from providing data- and AI-based connected solutions for professional fleets to recommending outstanding restaurants and hotels curated by the MICHELIN Guide.

  • Innovation-Driven: Work on projects that matter—from sustainable materials to digital transformation.

  • Community Impact: Be part of a company that does what's right. We use sustainable business practices while balancing the needs of our customers and communities.

description:
Keeper Security is hiring an experienced QA Analyst to join our Console team and help ensure the quality, reliability and usability of Keeper’s enterprise Admin Console applications. This is a 100% remote position, with an opportunity to work a hybrid schedule for candidates based in the El Dorado Hills, CA or Chicago, IL metro areas.

Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organizations globally. Keeper is published in 23 languages and sold in over 150 countries. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and help deliver secure, reliable administrative experiences to enterprise customers worldwide.

About Keeper

Keeper Security is one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity software companies that protects thousands of organizations and millions of people in over 150 countries. Keeper is a pioneer of zero-knowledge and zero-trust security built for any IT environment. Its core offering, KeeperPAM®, is an AI-enabled, cloud-native platform that protects all users, devices and infrastructure from cyber attacks. Recognized for its innovation in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management (PAM), Keeper secures passwords and passkeys, infrastructure secrets, remote connections and endpoints with role-based enforcement policies, least privilege and just-in-time access. Learn why Keeper is trusted by leading organizations to defend against modern adversaries at KeeperSecurity.com.

About the Role

As a QA Analyst on the Admin Console team, you will test Keeper’s web-based administrative experiences and the backend APIs that support our enterprise solutions. You will work closely with Engineering, Product and other QA professionals to validate new features, identify defects and ensure console functionality remains secure, reliable and intuitive.

This role requires strong attention to detail, experience testing enterprise web applications and familiarity with modern web and API testing practices. You will help maintain comprehensive test coverage across frontend functionality, administrative workflows, access controls and backend integrations.

Responsibilities

  • Test Keeper’s web-based Admin Console applications for functionality, reliability, usability and regression issues
  • Validate backend APIs that support console functionality using tools such as Postman or similar platforms
  • Create, execute and maintain test cases based on product requirements, technical specifications and user stories
  • Test enterprise administrative workflows including authentication, authorization, permissions and role-based access controls
  • Perform cross-browser testing to ensure consistent behavior across supported desktop browsers
  • Reproduce, document and track defects with clear technical detail and steps to reproduce
  • Maintain test coverage and execution results using tools such as TestRail, Jira and Confluence
  • Collaborate closely with developers, Product and other QA team members to identify issues and validate fixes
  • Participate in requirement reviews, release validation and regression testing activities
  • Identify gaps in test coverage and recommend improvements to QA processes and test strategy
  • Use AI-assisted tools such as Claude, ChatGPT or similar platforms to support test design, defect analysis, troubleshooting and documentation

Requirements

  • 3+ years of experience in software quality assurance, web application testing or a related QA role
  • Hands-on experience testing enterprise web applications, administrative consoles or SaaS platforms
  • Familiarity with web technologies including HTML, CSS, JavaScript and modern browser behavior
  • Experience validating backend APIs using Postman or similar API testing tools
  • Strong understanding of authentication, authorization, permissions and role-based access control concepts
  • Ability to create clear, detailed and reproducible test cases and defect reports
  • Experience with Jira, TestRail, Confluence or similar test and defect management platforms
  • Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to collaborate across Engineering, Product and QA teams
  • Familiarity with enterprise identity technologies such as Active Directory, LDAP or similar platforms
  • Ability and willingness to use AI-assisted tools effectively to improve testing, troubleshooting, analysis and documentation
  • Due to this role’s involvement in GovCloud environments, qualified candidates must be a U.S. Person, defined as a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident

Preferred Requirements

  • Experience testing identity, cybersecurity or other security-sensitive enterprise applications
  • Familiarity with cloud environments such as AWS or Azure
  • Exposure to identity and access management protocols such as SAML, SCIM or SSO
  • Familiarity with virtualization or containerization tools such as Docker or VMware
  • Experience with automated web or API testing tools

Benefits

  • Medical, Dental & Vision (inclusive of domestic partnerships)
  • Employer Paid Life Insurance & Employee/Spouse/Child Supplemental life
  • Voluntary Short/Long Term Disability Insurance
  • 401K (Roth/Traditional)

title: Sr Eng, Design Quality

This is where your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Your Role at Baxter

This is where my hands make life-sustaining products

As a Senior Engineer, Design Quality, you will serve as the quality partner for New Product Development and Sustaining Engineering projects. You will provide quality oversight throughout the product lifecycle, ensuring design controls, regulatory requirements, and quality standards are met. You will join a collaborative Quality team that partners with R&D, Regulatory Affairs, Manufacturing, and Supplier Quality to bring innovative healthcare products to market.   • 401K match

What you’ll bring

  • Experience with structured methods such as 5 Why, fault tree analysis, design or process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis, DMAIC, or equivalent approaches is preferred.

Knowledge of applicable IECand ISO product standards (ex: IEC 62304, IEC 60601-1, ISO 62366-1, etc…) is expected for the assigned product scope
  • Ability to review technical documentation and determine whether requirements, methods, results, conclusions, and traceability are scientifically and objectively supported

  • Self-motivated, organized, detail oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities while maintaining accurate and complete records.
  • Ability to challenge constructively, make decisions, and escalate concerns when evidence is insufficient or patient safety, product quality, or compliance may be affected. · Experience supporting audits or regulatory inspections is preferred.
  • Professional certification in quality engineering, reliability, software quality, Lean, or Six Sigma is preferred.
  • Experience with working in an environment subject to compliance with 21 CFR Parts 820, and FDA Inspection experience preferred.

Company Culture

We have two shifts available – (All times are listed in Sydney local time)

Tuesday through Saturday 4:00 AM – 12:00 PM

Tuesday through Saturday 4:00 PM – 12:00 AM

What you’ll Bring:

  • Five (5+) years of experience in an information security role. Progressive relevant training and/or certification may be substituted for one (1) year of the experience requirement

  • Experience working in a Security Operations Center (SOC)

  • Two (2+) years of experience with triaging endpoint events from EDR, NGAV, and supporting the Incident Response (IR) process

  • Deep knowledge on assessing threat indicators in a Windows Environment (e.g. Malware/Malicious Anomalies/Abnormal network Activity/Root Level Compromise, Forensic Artifacts, etc.)

  • Robust understanding of at least two of the following: Windows, Linux or OSX;

  • Familiarity with ELK stack (Dashboards, Logstash Config, Searching) Scripting / Programming with Powershell, Python, and Go

  • Familiarity with AWS services such as EC2, S3 and IAM and Azure/M365

  • Experience in developing, refining, and performing leadless threat hunting analysis to uncover new or potential incidents and report on results

  • Excellent problem solving, critical thinking, and analytical skills with the ability to deconstruct issues (hunting anomalous pattern detection)

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills to effectively summarize and present technical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences

Bonus:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science or related technical discipline

  • Network/System Administration and/or Engineering

  • Deep forensic knowledge of Windows, Mac OS and/or Linux

  • Experience in Digital Forensics and Incident Response a plus

  • Malware Analysis (Behavioral and/or Static analysis- IDA, Cuckoo Sandbox, x86/x64 Debugging) Pentesting/Red/Blue Team

  • Capture The Flag (CTF) Development

Blackpoint Cyber welcomes and encourages applications from qualified individuals of all races, colors, religions, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, marital status, or any other legally protected status. We are committed to equality of opportunity in all aspects of employment.

For eligible employees in the US, Blackpoint offers competitive Health, Vision, Dental, and Life Insurance plans, a robust 401k plan, Discretionary Time Off, and other minor perks. Blackpoint believes all employees should share in the company’s success – equity participation is available to employees globally, with program details varying by location and employment structure.

Citizenship: U.S. Citizenship Required


Help Secure the U.S. Army's Global Network!

Leidos is seeking a Mid-Level Cryptography & Security Infrastructure Engineer to support the Army Global Unified Network (AGUN) Migration team.

In this remote role, you'll help secure and modernize the Army's global network infrastructure through Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), digital certificate management, cryptographic security, and enterprise infrastructure support.

You'll work with engineering and cybersecurity teams to maintain secure systems, troubleshoot technical issues, and support network modernization.

  • Support Linux systems, virtualization, and container infrastructure.
  • Maintain enterprise network monitoring and management applications.
  • Perform infrastructure patching, upgrades, configuration changes, and security hardening.
  • Support DoD cybersecurity requirements and STIGs.
  • Assist with network migrations, systems integration, testing, and validation.
  • Develop technical documentation, certificate reports, and configuration records.
  • Collaborate with engineering, cybersecurity, and operations teams.

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • Active DoD Secret clearance and U.S. citizenship.
  • Bachelor's degree in a related technical field with 4–8 years of relevant experience, or a master's degree with 2–6 years. Additional applicable experience may be considered in place of a degree.
  • DoD IAT Level II certification (Security+ or equivalent) and an approved Computing Environment (CE) certification.
  • Experience supporting enterprise infrastructure, network management, or systems engineering.
  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaborate with technical teams.
  • Flexibility to work nonstandard shifts and travel up to 10%.

Required Technologies & Technical Skills

  • PKI & Certificates: Experience with PKI administration, digital certificates, and certificate lifecycle management.
  • Linux: Administration, configuration, and troubleshooting.
  • Networking: LAN/WAN, TCP/IP, routing, and switching fundamentals.
  • Virtualization: VMware, KVM, or comparable technologies.
  • Containers: Familiarity with Docker or Kubernetes.
  • Network Monitoring: Familiarity with ELK or comparable monitoring platforms.
  • Network Management: Experience with at least one of Palo Alto Panorama, Cisco Prime, Cisco DNA, or Junos Space.
  • Security: DoD STIGs, system hardening, and infrastructure security.

Preferred Qualifications & Technologies

  • Experience supporting Army, DISA, or other DoD networks.
  • Network+, CCNA, Red Hat certification, or equivalent.
  • Hands-on experience with Certificate Authorities, HSMs, and cryptographic security.
  • Experience with RHEL, Red Hat Satellite, VMware, vSAN, or Kubernetes.
  • Knowledge of InfoVista, ELK, or SIEM platforms.
  • Experience with Git, GitLab, Ansible, Terraform, Puppet, or Salt.
  • Python scripting and infrastructure automation.
  • Experience supporting Windows Server, Dell servers, or enterprise infrastructure.
  • Experience with network migration, systems integration, and modernization.

Why Join Leidos?

At Leidos, you'll have the opportunity to work with advanced security technologies while supporting the modernization of the U.S. Army's global communications infrastructure.

If you're a cleared infrastructure engineer with PKI, certificate management, and Linux experience who enjoys solving technical challenges, apply today!

If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. title: ICAM Policy Analyst
description:
About Easy Dynamics Corporation

Easy Dynamics is a leading IT service provider specializing in cybersecurity, cloud computing, and risk management for federal agencies. Since 2006, we have partnered with our customers to design, build, and secure the systems that protect our people, places, and way of life. Our work is grounded in deep technical expertise, thoughtful problem-solving, and a clear understanding of the complex environments our customers operate in.

Our world-class team of engineers, consultants, and subject-matter experts are builders, problem-solvers, and trusted advisors who thrive on solving unique and ever-evolving digital challenges. We bring a hands-on, mission-focused approach to every engagement, delivering solutions that are built to last.

About the role

We are seeking a mid-level Identity Policy Analyst to support a federal government client’s identity, credential, and access management (ICAM) program. This role assesses the current identity and access environment, identifies gaps against federal policy and target-state architectures, and delivers actionable recommendations and support that advance the agency’s Zero Trust and ICAM modernization goals.

What you’ll do

  • Assess the current-state identity, credential, and access management (ICAM) environment, including systems, processes, and governance, to establish a clear baseline of existing capabilities.
  • Identify gaps between current-state ICAM capabilities and target-state requirements, including alignment with Zero Trust principles and maturity models (e.g., CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, NIST SP 800-207).
  • Develop findings, risk-informed recommendations, and prioritized roadmaps to close identified gaps and advance ICAM and Zero Trust maturity.
  • Interpret and apply relevant federal policy, guidance, and frameworks, including GSA’s Federal Identity, Credential, and Access Management (FICAM) Playbook, NIST SP 800-63 (Digital Identity Guidelines), NIST SP 800-207 (Zero Trust Architecture), OMB M-22-09 (Federal Zero Trust Strategy), HSPD-12, and FISMA.
  • Translate policy and framework requirements into practical, actionable guidance for technical teams, program leadership, and agency stakeholders.
  • Support development of ICAM strategy documents, implementation plans, and governance artifacts, such as policy briefs, assessment reports, and roadmaps.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including engineering, cybersecurity, and program management, to ensure recommendations are technically sound and operationally feasible.
  • Prepare clear, well-organized written products and briefings for both technical and executive audiences.
  • Monitor evolving federal identity and Zero Trust policy, guidance, and standards, and assess their impact on the program.
  • Support governance and compliance activities related to identity, such as control assessments, audits, and reporting.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Public Policy, or a related field, and 4+ years of relevant experience; or 6+ years of relevant experience in lieu of a degree.
  • Demonstrated experience with identity, credential, and access management (ICAM) programs, cybersecurity policy, or federal IT policy and compliance.
  • Working knowledge of GSA’s FICAM Playbook and its application to agency ICAM programs.
  • Familiarity with Zero Trust principles and frameworks, including NIST SP 800-207 and OMB’s Federal Zero Trust Strategy (M-22-09).
  • Understanding of federal identity and security guidance, including NIST SP 800-63, HSPD-12, and FISMA.
  • Experience assessing current-state environments, performing gap analyses, and developing practical recommendations and roadmaps.
  • Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize policy and technical information.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience briefing both technical staff and program/agency leadership.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with technical, policy, and program stakeholders across a government engagement.
  • Must be eligible to obtain a Public Trust government security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience directly supporting a federal ICAM, Zero Trust, or identity governance program.
  • Relevant certification such as CAP, CISSP, or CISA.
  • Familiarity with NIST SP 800-53 security controls and their intersection with identity and access management.

The salary range for this role is $120,000 to $135,000 annually.

The Office of Risk Management & Insurance supports the University's efforts to identify, assess, finance, and mitigate risk across academic, administrative, research, and healthcare operations.

  • Identify trends, and emerging risks through quantitative analysis.

Collaboration

  • Participate in other initiatives and other duties as assigned.

  • Experience gathering, analyzing, and interpreting complex datasets.
  • Experience developing reports and presenting findings to stakeholders.

About Visio Lending

Visio Lending is the nation’s leader in rental home financing. Headquartered in fantastic Austin, Texas, since late 2015, Visio has financed more than $1 billion in Rental360 loans. We offer a collaborative culture, growth opportunities, and flexibility with remote work options.

How to Apply?

To be considered for employment, please submit your application online. While we appreciate all the interest we receive, only candidates selected for phone screening, or an interview will be contacted directly. You will receive application status alerts via email so make sure your email address is accurate.

Note: Incomplete applications will not be considered. Unanswered application questions or responses indicating “see resume” will be considered incomplete and you will be removed from consideration.

Visio Financial Services, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer

The Opportunity:

As a Business Systems Analyst / UAT Lead, you will lead the planning, coordination, and execution of user acceptance testing (UAT) for Visio Lending’s software solutions, while also independently owning business analysis for assigned initiatives. Working closely with other Business Systems Analysts, business stakeholders, and Engineering teams, you’ll organize testing cycles, guide business users through the UAT process, track defects and approvals, and communicate testing progress and release readiness. On smaller initiatives, you’ll also lead requirements discovery, documentation, and stakeholder facilitation from intake through business validation.

If you are an organized, analytical professional who enjoys coordinating cross-functional teams, translating business needs into clear requirements, and ensuring nothing falls through the cracks, this role is for you. You’ll thrive if you’re a strong communicator with exceptional attention to detail, comfortable owning ambiguous work, and passionate about delivering high-quality solutions that support the business.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the planning, coordination, and execution of UAT across assigned releases and projects
  • Independently lead business analysis for assigned small to moderate initiatives, from requirements discovery through implementation and validation, filling remaining capacity around UAT priorities
  • Facilitate requirements workshops, discovery sessions, and cross-functional meetings with business, technology, and vendor stakeholders
  • Elicit, document, and drive approval of clear, complete, and testable requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria
  • Partner with Business Systems Analysts and stakeholders to translate requirements into UAT test plans and scenarios
  • Develop and maintain UAT plans, entry/exit criteria, readiness checklists, and schedules
  • Recruit, prepare, and guide business users who serve as UAT testers
  • Maintain traceability between requirements, acceptance criteria, UAT scenarios, defects, and business validation
  • Track UAT execution, defects, and resolution status, and report regularly on UAT health
  • Facilitate defect triage and communication between business testers, BSAs, and engineering
  • Manager UAT sign-off, approvals, and go/no-go recommendations
  • Coordinate test environment and test data readiness with technical teams
  • Demonstrate completed solutions to stakeholders and confirm delivered functionality meets business intent
  • Maintain UAT and requirements documentation, templates, and standards, driving continuous improvement
  • Contribute to agile ceremonies such as sprint planning, standups, and retrospectives
  • Other responsibilities and duties as assigned based on business needs
  • Authorized Remote Locations: AL, AR, AZ, FL, GA, IL, IN, KS, KY, LA, MI, NC, SC, TX, UT
  • Salary Range: $85,000 – $115,000 (Exempt level position)

What We Are Looking For:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, information systems, technology, or a related field, or equivalent experience
  • 3- 5 years of experience in a Business Systems Analyst, Business Analyst, Systems Analyst, or similar technology delivery role
  • Demonstrated experience independently leading requirements discovery and analysis for technology initiatives
  • Experience facilitating requirements workshops with cross-functional stakeholders
  • Strong experience translating business needs into clear, testable requirements and acceptance criteria
  • Experience supporting or coordinating User Acceptance Testing as part of the software development lifecycle
  • Strong understanding of the SDLC and the relationship between requirements, development, testing, UAT, and implementation
  • Experience working with requirements, test management, or defect tracking tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, TestRail
  • Strong meeting facilitation, stakeholder management, and communication skills
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent initiatives, priorities, and deadlines
  • Ability to independently own assigned work and drive activities and decisions to resolution
  • Ability to use standard office equipment, printer, scanner, copier, fax, telephone, personal computer, and other peripheral devices

What We Prefer to Find:

  • Experience in mortgage lending, financial services, or another regulated industry
  • Knowledge of mortgage lending processes including origination, processing, underwriting, closing/funding, and post-closing
  • Experience with DSCR or other business-purpose lending
  • Experience with Loan Origination Systems or similar lending technology, including product and pricing eligibility, rules engines, workflow design, or underwriting conditions
  • Experience coordinating formal UAT cycles involving multiple business stakeholders or non-technical testers
  • Familiarity with Agile/Scrum delivery methodologies
  • Ability to write basic SQL queries or otherwise perform data validation

title: Senior AI Agent Runtime Engineer (Remote/Hybrid)
description:
HS Financial Technologies is seeking an experienced AI Engineer to design, build, and operate production AI agents for financial operations and enterprise workflows. You will own the agent runtime, orchestration, memory, tool execution, and safety controls in a production environment.

You will bring strong software engineering skills, hands-on production LLM experience, and architecture judgment, establishing reusable patterns for HSFT engineering teams and ensuring secure, auditable deployments.

Runtime: Design, deploy, and support reliable production runtimes for AI agents serving financial operations and enterprise workflows. Controls: Enforce authorization, human approvals, policy checks, validation, checkpoints, idempotency, retries, and exception handling throughout agent workflows. Enterprise integration: Build validated, auditable tool and system interfaces with least-privilege permissions, prompt-injection defenses, and controls outside the model that isolate reasoning from deterministic execution. Evaluation: Build repeatable tests and regression suites for agent outcomes, supporting evidence, and tool-execution paths; diagnose quality, safety, failures, latency, and cost. Observability: Monitor and troubleshoot production agents, maintain audit evidence, and turn operational findings into reusable engineering standards. Bachelor’s degree in a relevant technical field or equivalent practical experience. 5+ years of software engineering experience, including 1+ year delivering LLM/agent-based applications in production. Strong Python, API design, asynchronous processing, automated testing, source control, and AWS engineering skills. Hands-on experience implementing agent loops, context assembly, retrieval, memory, tool selection and limits, durable state, checkpoints, retries, and idempotency. title: Senior Intelligence Analyst
description:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM’s platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

About the role

The Senior Intelligence Analyst owns TRM’s blockchain intelligence for a priority coverage area. You turn on-chain tracing, OSINT, and diverse intel signals into finished intelligence across scam/fraud, counter-narcotics, and facilitation and money laundering. You lead industry-leading work against professional money laundering organizations, illicit gambling networks, and related actors.

What is unique here: you build the AI-driven pipelines that turn many signals into attribution, making one of TRM’s highest-priority coverage areas a strength.

The impact you will have

  • Deepen TRM’s coverage by owning your area end-to-end and delivering finished, source-cited intelligence products across multiple threat categories.

  • Build end-to-end AI capability that processes a wide variety of intel signals and augments target selection, so you generate leads faster and at greater scale.

  • Trace funds across chains and through obfuscation, and correlate on-chain activity with OSINT, including Mandarin-language sources, to attribute money laundering organizations, threat actors, and gambling networks.

  • Drive attribution and leads that improve delivery in Mission (scam/fraud), Counter Narcotics, Nation States, and Facilitation and Money Laundering.

  • Set ambitious, industry-leading targets for your coverage area and raise the bar on tradecraft.

  • Build reusable AI pipelines and methods the broader Intelligence team adopts.

What we’re looking for

  • 5 to 8+ years in blockchain intelligence, crypto investigations, threat intelligence, or financial-crime investigations.

  • Strong OSINT and off-chain investigative tradecraft: you connect on-chain activity to real-world people, companies, and networks. Hands-on blockchain tracing experience is a plus, not a requirement; we train strong investigators on our tooling.

  • Domain expertise in professional money laundering organizations, illicit gambling networks, and underground banking.

  • Mandarin Chinese fluency is a strong plus.

  • Production AI fluency: you build end-to-end pipelines that process diverse intel signals and augment target selection, and you critically evaluate the output.

  • A track record of independently running complex investigations and producing clear, source-cited written intelligence.

  • US-based preferred, not required.

About the Team

  • You will join TRM’s Blockchain Intelligence (Primary Intelligence) organization, a distributed team producing finished intelligence across threat categories.

  • The work is intellectually demanding: you keep real investigative proficiency across on-chain and OSINT tradecraft while owning a priority coverage area.

  • Mission-first, high-autonomy, execution-oriented culture with rigorous analytical standards.

  • AI-native team: analysts build reusable pipelines the whole team adopts.

Team Operating Rhythms

  • Distributed, not distant: a US-based analyst collaborating across time zones with regular overlap for syncs.

  • Slack-first, async communication; @mention for timely responses.

  • Weekly 1:1s and team syncs, plus case and category rhythms.

  • Regular cross-category coordination with other Intelligence pods and Global Investigations.

  • Required online and collaboration hours: standard business hours in your timezone, with 3-4 hours overlap across US time zones (EST preferred) for internal syncs.

Travel Requirements:

  • Schedule: Occasional travel for team engagements.

  • Frequency: Low.

Onsite Requirements:

  • Schedule: None required; distributed/remote role.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position

  • Within your first 30 days, take ownership of an active case in your coverage area and deliver a finished, source-cited intelligence product.

  • Within 60 days, build an end-to-end AI pipeline that processes diverse intel signals for augmented target selection and that another analyst can reuse.

  • Within 90 days, measurably deepen coverage against money laundering organizations or gambling networks, with attribution and leads that support cross-category delivery.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We’re excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

Privacy Policy and Additional Information

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy.

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at ** Redacted **.

To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form.

Recruitment agencies

TRM Labs does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to TRM employees. TRM Labs is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company without a signed agreement.

About Keeper

Keeper Security is transforming cybersecurity for organizations globally with zero-trust privileged access management built with end-to-end encryption. Keeper’s cybersecurity solutions are FedRAMP and StateRAMP Authorized, SOC 2 compliant, FIPS 140-2 validated, as well as ISO 27001, 27017 and 27018 certified. About the Role

As a Senior QA Analyst focused on Privileged Access Management, you will validate complex workflows that span cloud infrastructure, identity providers, CI/CD systems, and enterprise operating environments. This role emphasizes integration testing, security-focused validation, and system-level quality across PAM and KSM capabilities, rather than isolated feature testing.   • Experience testing integrations with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) and CI/CD systems

  • Working knowledge of Windows and Linux operating systems

  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and communication skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in Agile development environments

title: Internship – Data Analyst
description:
DATA ANALYST INTERNSHIP

WHO WE ARE:

Passion for Life is a non-profit organization that operates with the power of dedicated interns like you. We help under-resourced youth transform their passions into rewarding careers. Our mission is to provide forward-thinking career coaching and immersion opportunities driven by the students’ passions and talents in a fun, structured, and high-energy environment. Passion for Life was created to be a high-energy and engaging process that helps students identify their passions and gain clarity on how to utilize their core strengths and talents to select a career.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Data Analyst Intern plays a critical role in advancing the organization’s mission by transforming raw program and operational data into clear, actionable insights. Working collaboratively across program, development, and leadership teams, this position supports data-driven decision-making by designing and maintaining evaluation frameworks, producing compelling reports and dashboards, and ensuring data integrity throughout the organization. The ideal candidate is both analytically rigorous and mission-passionate, with the ability to communicate complex findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.

While this is an unpaid internship position, there are many exciting internal and external rewards to consider.

What you gain

  • Gain valuable hands on experience in nonprofit educational sector
  • Make a meaningful impact on the lives of underserved communities
  • Increase your networking opportunities and collaborate with knowledgeable teams
  • Boost your untapped potential and master new skills
  • Flexible scheduling and potential for recommendation letters

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Data Analysis & Program Evaluation: Conduct regular impact assessments, needs analyses, and program evaluations using both quantitative and qualitative methodologies to measure effectiveness and inform continuous improvement.
  • Data Management & Governance: Oversee data collection, cleaning, storage, and management in compliance with organizational standards, confidentiality policies, and applicable data governance requirements.
  • Reporting & Data Visualization: Create user-friendly, visually engaging reports and dashboards for both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including program teams, leadership, and funders.
  • Evaluation Framework & Strategy: Design and maintain robust evaluation frameworks that measure program outcomes, align with organizational goals, and inform strategic decision-making.
  • Collaboration & Capacity Building: Partner with program, development, and leadership teams to deliver data insights that support program enhancement and assist staff in building data literacy for day-to-day use.

Technical Skills:

  • Leadership and Delegation: Ability to lead research initiatives and delegate tasks effectively to team members or collaborators.
  • Research Platforms: Proficiency in research platforms and tools, including Python, Qualtrics, Microsoft Office Suite, and Java.
  • Analytics: Skilled in statistical and data analytics software (e.g., SPSS, SAS, R), with a strong foundation in analyzing complex datasets.
  • Data Collection and Cleaning: Experienced in data collection methods and techniques, ensuring clean, accurate, and reliable data for analysis.
  • Qualitative and Quantitative Data: Competent in both qualitative and quantitative research methodologies, applying each effectively to capture comprehensive insights.
  • Evaluation Design: Ability to design robust evaluation frameworks that measure outcomes and inform strategic decisions.
  • Creating Reports and Sharing Data: Skilled in creating clear, compelling reports and dashboards to communicate findings effectively to stakeholders, including program teams and funders.
  • Editing and Proofreading: Strong attention to detail in reviewing reports, ensuring clarity, coherence, and accuracy in documentation.
  • Research and Evaluation Planning: Skilled in planning and executing research projects aligned with organizational goals.
  • Instructional Design Principles and Learning Theory: Knowledgeable in instructional design (ID) principles, learning theory, and educational frameworks to support effective program evaluation.
  • Graphic Design and Multimedia: Familiar with tools such as Articulate, Captivate, and other eLearning and multimedia platforms, capable of creating engaging visuals and interactive reports.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Social Sciences, Public Policy, Human Services, or a related field required.
  • Master’s degree or certifications in research methods, program evaluation, or data analytics (e.g., SAS, SPSS, Google Data Analytics, or equivalent) preferred.
  • Students with relevant majors and coursework aligned to the above are encouraged to apply for the intern role.

Experience

  • 1–5 years of experience in data analysis, program evaluation, or research, ideally within a nonprofit or mission-driven organization.
  • Proven experience conducting impact assessments, needs analyses, and program evaluations; community-based program familiarity strongly preferred.
  • Experience working across cross-functional teams and communicating findings to non-technical audiences.

Additional Information

Estimated time commitment: 9-10 hours/ week depending on needs, in addition to weekly meetings and occasional conference calls.

Term limit: 4-month unpaid intern position (Can be extendable on mutual agreement).

title: Service Operations Supervisor
description:
This is where your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

As a Service Operations Supervisor, you will lead the daily operations of an assigned service location, ensuring the safe, compliant, and efficient delivery of service while driving operational performance, customer satisfaction, and revenue growth.

You will oversee service center performance, lead continuous improvement initiatives, and manage a team responsible for servicing critical healthcare equipment that impacts patient care every day. Schedule: Tuesday-Saturday or Wednesday-Sunday, 7:00 AM-3:30 PM, based on business needs. Flexibility to work outside regular hours and on scheduled days off is required to support operational needs and special events.

What You'll Do

  • Drive safety initiatives, maintain a clean and compliant work environment, and ensure completion of required safety training and medical testing requirements.
  • Maintain accountability for site inventory accuracy and the timely, accurate completion of service work orders.
  • Monitor and drive key operational metrics, continuous improvement initiatives, and overall service center performance.
  • Manage service revenue objectives, support service contract compliance, and oversee local expense controls and resource utilization.
  • Partner with sales teams and customers to support business reviews, contract performance, and customer satisfaction goals.
  • Evaluate staffing, equipment, and operational needs; prepare business cases to support resource planning and site requirements.

What You'll Bring

We understand compensation is an important factor as you consider the next step in your career.
