title: Frontline Services Technician I
description:
FRONTLINE SERVICES TECHNICIAN I

Department: Frontline Services

Reports to: Manager of Frontline Services


Job Summary

The Frontline Services Technician I is a technical role responsible for providing professional end-user support, monitoring IT infrastructure, resolving routine incidents, and escalating complex or high-risk issues.

This is a combined Service Desk, Network Operations, and Security Operations position. Technicians are expected to maintain broad foundational competency across all three areas while developing a primary focus in either End User Support or Network & Security Operations.

The role operates primarily through established procedures, knowledge articles, runbooks, and escalation processes.

This is an in-office position.


Essential Functions

  • Provide technical support for end users, applications, endpoints, network connectivity, and common IT services, resolving routine issues using established troubleshooting procedures, knowledge articles, and runbooks.
  • Provide responsive user support by answering service desk queue calls, responding to email and portal-generated tickets, and communicating clearly and professionally with users by phone and email throughout the lifecycle of incidents and service requests.
  • Monitor and respond to service, infrastructure, network, endpoint, backup, and security alerts, performing approved first-response actions and escalating issues that require additional expertise.
  • Troubleshoot common hardware, software, operating system, Microsoft 365, identity, access, VPN, Wi-Fi, printing, and application issues while maintaining a professional customer-service experience.
  • Perform approved service requests and operational tasks such as user onboarding, account and MFA support, device provisioning, software installation, patching, and equipment configuration.
  • Perform initial security-event and phishing triage, following established procedures for investigation, containment, remediation, and escalation.
  • Accurately document incidents, service requests, troubleshooting steps, resolutions, alert activity, and user communications in accordance with service-management requirements.
  • Follow established SLAs, escalation procedures, security controls, change restrictions, and operational runbooks to ensure consistent and reliable service.
  • Recognize issues that exceed Tier 1 authority or capability and provide complete, actionable escalations to Tier 2 or other specialized teams.
  • Participate in shift handoffs and operational continuity by clearly communicating outstanding issues, service impacts, active alerts, and required follow-up.
  • Contribute to knowledge articles, runbooks, and process improvements by identifying recurring issues, documenting solutions, and communicating opportunities for improved efficiency or service quality.
  • Work collaboratively with users, Tier 2 technicians, vendors, and other IT teams to support timely resolution of incidents and service requests.


Specialization Tracks


End User Support Focus

  • Primary emphasis on:
  • Endpoint, desktop, mobile, and application support.
  • Microsoft 365 and productivity applications.
  • Software, hardware, printing, and remote support issues.
  • Customer communication and service delivery.


Maintains working knowledge of: network monitoring, VPN, endpoint security, phishing/security triage, backup/infrastructure alerts, and NOC/SOC escalation.


Network & Security Operations Focus

Primary emphasis on:

  • Infrastructure and network outage alert triage and outage resolution.
  • User, endpoint, and systems security monitoring and triage.
  • User connectivity, VPN, and access issue resolution.
  • Veeam backup and SQL software job triage.


Maintains working knowledge of: Windows and endpoint troubleshooting, Microsoft 365, account/MFA support, hardware, applications, customer service, and service-desk procedures.

title: Sr Manager Medical Affairs
description:
This is where your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your Role at Baxter


At Baxter, we are deeply connected by our mission. No matter your role at Baxter, your work makes a positive impact on people around the world. You'll feel a sense of purpose throughout the organization, as we know our work improves outcomes for millions of patients.


The Senior Manager – Medical Affairs serves as the clinical voice within Research & Development (R&D), partnering with cross-functional teams to ensure Baxter's Patient Support Systems (PSS) and Global Surgical Solutions (GSS) portfolio addresses real-world clinical needs, digital integration, and workflow efficiency. This role provides clinical leadership to influence product design, clinical validation, evidence generation, and innovation strategy, enabling differentiated, outcome-oriented solutions for modern healthcare environments.


What You'll Be Doing


Clinical Strategy & R&D Partnership

  • Provide clinical leadership throughout the product development lifecycle, including design controls and product development processes.
  • Translate unmet clinical needs into product requirements, design inputs, and innovation opportunities.
  • Partner closely with Engineering, Product Management, Human Factors, and Regulatory teams to optimize product usability and workflow efficiency.
  • Support risk assessments, clinical evaluations, validation activities, and regulatory submissions.

Digital Health & Connected Care

  • Provide expertise related to Electronic Medical Record (EMR) platforms, including Epic and Cerner, and their integration within clinical workflows.
  • Advise teams on device connectivity, interoperability, and data flow across connected healthcare ecosystems.
  • Support the development of connected medical devices, clinical dashboards, and Operating Room (OR) integration solutions.
  • Ensure product designs align with evolving digital health standards and healthcare interoperability requirements.

Voice of Customer (VoC) & Clinical Insights

  • Engage with clinicians globally, including surgeons, nurses, anesthesia professionals, and biomedical engineers.
  • Conduct field observations, workflow assessments, interviews, and usability studies.
  • Translate customer insights into:
    • Clinical requirements
    • Workflow optimization opportunities
    • Product differentiation strategies
    • Innovation roadmaps

Clinical Evidence & Medical Affairs

  • Support clinical evidence generation and evaluation strategies for new and existing products.
  • Perform literature reviews and synthesize clinical data into actionable recommendations.
  • Contribute to clinical value messaging, publications, educational content, and internal training materials.
  • Provide expert clinical perspectives during product development and commercialization activities.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Influence decision making within a complex global matrix environment.
  • Serve as the bridge between clinical practice, engineering, product management, and digital health teams.
  • Present clinical insights, recommendations, and strategic guidance to senior leaders and stakeholders.



What You'll Bring


Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or advanced degree in Clinical Informatics, Medicine (MBBS/MD), Nursing (RN), or a related clinical field, with 8+ years of relevant clinical experience.
  • Strong clinical background in:
    • Medical-Surgical Nursing
    • Intensive Care Unit (ICU) / Critical Care
  • Experience working with EMR systems, preferably Epic and/or Cerner.
  • Knowledge of connected devices, clinical dashboards, and data-driven healthcare workflows.
  • Professional clinical experience in one or more of the following regions:
    • United States
    • Europe
    • United Kingdom / Ireland
    • Singapore
    • Middle East
  • Demonstrated ability to translate clinical needs into product and technology solutions.
  • Excellent communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience within Operating Room (OR) settings.
  • Prior experience in the medical device industry.
  • Experience supporting products such as:
    • Surgical Tables
    • Patient Support Surfaces
    • OR Integration Systems
  • Working knowledge of healthcare interoperability standards including HL7 and FHIR.
  • Experience in Medical Affairs, Clinical Development, Clinical Research, or Clinical Product Management roles.
  • Advanced clinical, healthcare, or business-related degree preferred.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Baxter is an equal opportunity employer. Baxter evaluates qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, protected veteran status, disability/handicap status or any other legally protected characteristic.

Reasonable Accommodations

Baxter is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities globally. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or interview process, please click on the link here and let us know the nature of your request along with your contact information.

Recruitment Fraud Notice

Baxter has discovered incidents of employment scams, where fraudulent parties pose as Baxter employees, recruiters, or other agents, and engage with online job seekers in an attempt to steal personal and/or financial information. To learn how you can protect yourself, review our Recruitment Fraud Notice.

AI Disclaimer

Baxter may use AI-enabled technologies to support portions of the hiring process, such as scheduling or skills matching. Final decisions regarding candidate applications and selection are made by our hiring teams, who review any AI-assisted outputs before decisions are made, and we remain committed to fairness, inclusion, and thoughtful decision-making led by our hiring teams throughout the selection process. Our AI-enabled technologies do not automatically disqualify candidates or make hiring decisions.

title: Senior Analyst, Market Research & CX
description:
Job description

OGC is a boutique research and consulting agency specializing in data driven strategy, quantitative analytics, and Customer Experience (CX) program design and optimization. We partner with some of the world’s leading organizations across Financial Services, Specialty Retail, Telecommunications, Hospitality, and Software, helping them gain a deeper understanding of their customers, translate research into actionable insights, and improve business processes and customer experiences.

One of our telecommunications clients is seeking an analytical, detail oriented Senior Analyst to join their team. In this role, you will support the analysis and measurement of customer experience, with a particular focus on NPS and other CX metrics. You will work across multiple data sources to identify trends, uncover key drivers, and translate findings into clear, actionable insights for stakeholders.

This position is ideal for a strong analytical thinker who is equally comfortable working with data and communicating what that data means. The successful candidate will be able to move beyond reporting numbers to develop clear narratives around customer experience trends, support dashboards and reporting, and work collaboratively with stakeholders to answer complex business questions. This position is based in Philadelphia 4 days a week.

  • CX & NPS Analysis: Analyze NPS and other customer experience data to identify trends, drivers, and opportunities for improvement.

  • Data Synthesis: Pull together data and signals from multiple sources to develop a clear understanding of customer experience performance and trends.

  • Reporting & Dashboards: Create, maintain, and manage CX dashboards and recurring reporting, ensuring data is accurate, relevant, and easy to interpret.

  • Insight Development: Translate analytical findings into clear narratives and actionable insights that explain the “why” behind customer experience trends.

  • Stakeholder Support: Partner with CX, Research, Analytics, and business stakeholders to understand key questions and provide data-driven answers and recommendations.

  • Research & Measurement: Support ongoing CX measurement initiatives and pilots as the client evolves its approach to understanding customer journeys and experiences.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work across teams and data sources to connect information, identify patterns, and support broader CX strategy and decision-making.

Job requirements

  • Experience: 3-6 years of experience in an analyst role within Customer Experience, Market Research, Consumer Insights, Business Analytics, or a related field.

  • Strong Analytical Skills: Demonstrated ability to analyze large or complex datasets, identify meaningful trends, and draw clear conclusions from data.

  • CX / NPS Experience: Experience working with NPS, customer satisfaction, survey data, CX metrics, or similar customer-focused measurement.

  • Reporting & Visualization: Strong experience with Excel and/or data visualization and dashboarding tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or similar platforms.

  • Data Storytelling: Ability to turn data into a compelling, easy-to-understand narrative and communicate the key implications to stakeholders.

  • Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with confidence presenting findings and insights to cross-functional teams.

  • Research Knowledge: Understanding of quantitative research and survey methodologies; experience with qualitative research or journey research is a plus.

  • Problem Solving: Ability to work with multiple data sources, investigate unexpected findings, and independently identify the information needed to answer business questions.

  • Organization & Adaptability: Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

  • Location: Must be based in Philadelphia, PA.

title: Claims Business Process Analyst (Remote)
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Claims Business Process Analyst optimizes and modernizes claims processes to improve efficiency, accuracy, and alignment. This role analyzes workflows, identifies bottlenecks, and drives improvements by partnering with stakeholders and consultants to document gaps, define future processes, and implement solutions aligned with strategic priorities.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Evaluate claims business processes and identify opportunities to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and customer satisfaction.
  • Conduct root cause analyses to uncover operational gaps, data inconsistencies, or process bottlenecks.
  • Define and document “as-is” and “to-be” workflows using process mapping and related methodologies.

  • Support Single Source of Truth initiatives ensuring consistent data usage, definitions, and reporting across systems.
  • Define and track key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure process effectiveness and turnaround times.
  • Prepare and present insights, findings, and process improvement recommendations to leadership.
  • Support internal and external audits with accurate process documentation and data integrity assurance.
  • Lead or participate in business process reengineering (BPR) and operational efficiency initiatives.
  • Promote continuous improvement through feedback loops, metric- driven decision making, and proactive issue resolution.
  • Perform any other tasks required to support the Association’s Mission, Values, and Strategic Objectives.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent preferred.
  • Experience with Homeowners and Catastrophe (CAT) claims, particularly wind and fire events, preferred — with emphasis on understanding end-to-end claims workflows, dependencies, and process challenges.
  • Proven experience in process management or business process improvement.
  • Advanced knowledge and practical application of process improvement tools and methodologies such as Lean, Six Sigma, or Business Process Management (BPM).
  • Experience with the Duck Creek Claims platform (or similar claims management systems) preferred.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) with the ability to develop clear documentation, process visuals, and performance tracking templates.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to engage effectively with internal stakeholders, consultants, and leadership.

title: Development Assistant
location: The Met Fifth Avenue, New York, NY
description:
About the Metropolitan Museum of Art

The Met presents over 5,000 years of art from around the world for everyone to experience and enjoy. The Museum lives in two iconic sites in New York City—The Met Fifth Avenue and The Met Cloisters. Millions of people also take part in The Met experience online.

Since its founding in 1870, The Met has always aspired to be more than a treasury of rare and beautiful objects. We are committed to fostering a collaborative and respectful work environment with a staff as diverse as the audiences we engage. Our staff members are art lovers who are passionate about working toward a common goal: creating the most dynamic and inspiring art museum in the world.

At The Met, every staff member – from security officers to researchers to scientists and beyond – lives by our core values of respect, inclusivity, collaboration, excellence, and integrity.

Respect: Engage one another with collegiality, empathy, and kindness, always.

Inclusivity: Ensure that all are and feel welcome and valued.

Collaboration: Reach across boundaries to exchange ideas and work together toward our shared mission.

Excellence: Lead the cultural world in quality and expertise—and inspire curiosity and creativity.

Integrity: Hold ourselves to the highest moral standards, admit when we fall short, and then evolve.

GENERAL STATEMENT OF RESPONSIBILITES & DUTIES:

As the Development Assistant for Events, you will provide administrative support for the Development events team which oversees approximately 60–80 events annually. You will assist with managing guests lists, responses, RSVP, and guest data. You will process benefit ticket sales, gift acknowledgements and reporting. You will provide floor level event support before, during, and after events.


Please submit a cover letter with your application.


PRIMARY RESPONSIBILIES & DUTIES:

  • Provide administrative support to the Deputy Chief Development Officer for Events and the entire team with event invitation list management, electronic and printed invitation mailings (mail merges, list clean up, etc.), guest response tracking and follow-ups, monitoring shared email and phone inboxes, and other tasks as needed
  • Import, update, and extract data for Development event mail/email outreach through segmentation, list building, and reporting
  • Assist with benefit ticket sales, gift acknowledgements, and record-keeping
  • Manage internal calendars on multiple platforms (i.e., Outlook, Airtable, Artifax, etc.)
  • Follow best practices for the management, use, and governance of the enterprise system, ensuring quality assurance and data integrity, and work with Institutional Advancement Operations team to oversee integration of external event invitation and database system (Launchmetrics) with Tessitura database
  • Provide general assistance with event logistics before, during, and after events (includes some nights and weekends)
  • Provide procurement support, including ensuring compliance with all Museum policies and procedures related to purchasing goods and services and submitting requisitions, supplier invoice requests, and other forms for payment, for the Administrator of the Development Office with regard to their role as the Procurement Ambassador for Development
  • Plan and execute smaller-scale events and program as needed
  • Other duties as assigned

REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred
  • Thorough knowledge of and experience with Tessitura (or comparable donor database), including list management, constituent updating, and reporting
  • Candidate should be a self-starter and feel comfortable working independently, with the ability to multitask several projects at once
  • Outstanding ability to work well under pressure on a variety of projects; candidate should be comfortable working in a very fast-paced, deadline-oriented environment
  • Due to significant top-level donor contact, excellent interpersonal skills are essential (professional, discrete, and diplomatic)
  • Previous events and/or Development experience required
  • Meticulous attention to detail required
  • Must be able to lift 50 pounds (some physical work will be required.)
  • Computer literacy (Microsoft Office) required; previous experience with Photoshop preferred

COMPENSATION

  • Pay Rate: $32 - $34 / Hourly

The advertised pay scale reflects the good faith minimum and maximum salary range for this role. The advertised pay scale is not a promise of a particular wage for any specific employee. The specific compensation offered to a candidate may be dependent on a variety of factors including, but not limited to, the candidate’s experience, education, special licensing or qualifications, and other factors.

Visa Sponsorship

Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Location Requirements

At time of employment, employees are expected to be located within commuting distance of the Museum. “Commuting distance” means that they are located in one of following states: New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, or Pennsylvania (the “Tri-state and PA” areas), and be able to commute to and from the Museum in a single day.

Benefits Offerings

The Museum provides competitive compensation, and generous benefits and perks for all eligible employees. Note: Benefits Offering may differ based on Employee Status.

  • Medical, dental, vision and life insurance
  • 403(b) basic retirement plan and optional matching retirement plan with an outstanding employer match
  • Considerable paid time off, including annual leave, sick leave, and 13 Museum holidays
  • Long-term disability coverage
  • Flexible Spending Accounts & Health Savings Account (pre-tax income for eligible health care expenses)
  • Commuter benefits (pre-tax income for parking or mass transit expenses)
  • Free financial-planning services
  • Financial assistance for relevant coursework, seminars, and training programs
  • 25% discount for staff in Museum shops
  • A subsidized staff cafeteria
  • Access to the Museums Council pass, which grants free admission to various museums and cultural institutions

We recognize that it is highly unlikely that someone meets 100% of the desired attributes for a role. If much of this job description describes you, then please apply for this role.

The Met is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, The Met will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed in this process, please contact benefits@metmuseum.org.

The Metropolitan Museum of Art provides equal opportunity to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, age, mental or physical disability, pregnancy, alienage or citizenship status, marital status or domestic partner status, genetic information, genetic predisposition or carrier status, gender identity, HIV status, military status and any other category protected by law in all employment decisions, including but not limited to recruitment, hiring, compensation, training and apprenticeship, promotion, upgrading, demotion, downgrading, transfer, lay-off and termination, and all other terms and conditions of employment.

title: Senior Databricks Data Analyst
description:
Description

Who We Are

Stitch is the global leader in helping brands drive marketing performance through Braze and Databricks. We work with Fortune 1000 brands to design and execute martech-driven solutions and lifecycle marketing strategies that drive meaningful outcomes. Our fast-growing team spans the US, UK, and Canada.

We’re actively building the best martech & CRM consultancy in the world. Not the biggest—the best. We’re looking for teammates who are energized by this challenge.

The Role

As a Databricks Analyst, you work at every layer between the data and the decision. You write the queries, make the basic data connections you need to get to the right data, and build the reporting clients run on. Then you figure out what the data is telling us about the client’s business, make the recommendation, and drive it through to action. You work with enterprise marketing, data, and IT leaders to turn their Databricks investment into measurable business outcomes.

We are looking for an analyst who is hands-on and proactive. You are not just interpreting and storytelling. You are in the workspace, in the SQL editor, and in the client conversation. Our clients are handing us the keys to their data, and the Databricks team has to drive: you spot what needs doing, build momentum, and make sure every engagement has traction and keeps moving forward. You partner closely with Stitch’s Databricks project managers, architects, and data engineers, and you help shape how Stitch delivers analytics on Databricks.

Who You Are

First and foremost, you’re motivated by impact. To be the best CRM consultancy in the world, we have to be motivated by performance—both in how our work drives outcomes for our customers, and for how our work drives outcomes for Stitch.

This means you’re not content with status quo—you’re always looking towards what’s next and seeking opportunities to grow yourself, grow our customers, and grow Stitch. You have relentless standards and uphold them unapologetically. You move nimbly, take ownership, drive things forward, and make the people around you better. You’re driven and can’t sit still. You don’t wait for momentum, you create it. When a client hands you the keys to their data, you start driving. If this sounds like you, you will thrive here.

What You’ll Do

  • Query and analyze client data in Databricks using SQL (and Python where needed) across silver and gold layers to answer business questions quickly and accurately.
  • Make the basic data connections you need to get to the work: connect sources and set up simple ingestion, and partner with data engineers on more complex pipeline builds.
  • Build and maintain dashboards, reporting, and Genie spaces that let client marketers self-serve on governed data.
  • Interpret data and present clear, prioritized recommendations to marketing and data stakeholders. Examples include: customer behavior, audience performance, lifecycle health, and revenue drivers
  • Drive recommendations through to action. Build the case, align stakeholders, and stay with the work until it is implemented and measured.
  • Design KPI frameworks, segmentation and lifecycle strategy, identity and customer 360 support, audits, methodology contributions, and QBR/EBR participation.
  • Support customer identity and customer 360 work by profiling sources, validating data quality, and testing outputs, partnering with data engineers on the build.
  • Reconcile audiences and data between Databricks and activation platforms such as Braze, and find and fix the root cause when counts don’t match.
  • Develop audience segmentation strategies and lifecycle stage definitions using first-party, behavioral, and CRM data in the lakehouse.
  • Run data audits and readiness assessments that give clients a clear, recommendation-driven view of where their data stands and what to do next.
  • Present findings and recommendations to client marketing, data, and IT leaders, and participate in QBRs and EBRs alongside Client Partners.
  • Partner with Databricks project managers, architects, and data engineers to keep engagements on track and surface risks and opportunities early.
  • Use AI tools (e.g., Genie, Gemini, Claude) to speed up analysis, documentation, and QA.
  • Contribute to Stitch’s Databricks methodology: reusable queries, dashboard templates, assessment tools, and analytics accelerators that raise the standard of every client engagement.
  • Manage your time to meet billable targets of 36+ hours per week.
  • Obtain DBX accreditations and DBX Data Analyst certification.
  • Travel up to 20% for client meetings, workshops, and onsite engagements.

What Success Looks Like

  • Clients see you as the person who knows their data and their business—not just someone who pulls reports. They come to you for what to do next.
  • You get to the data yourself. Queries, connections, and dashboards don’t sit waiting on other teams.
  • Your recommendations get implemented, and you can point to the business results they drove.
  • The engagements you’re on keep moving. Leadership sees momentum and traction, not stalled work.
  • Your queries, dashboards, and frameworks are reusable, and they help Stitch scale its Databricks practice.

Requirements

What You Bring

  • Strong, hands-on SQL. You write your own queries against large datasets and don’t wait for someone else to pull the data.
  • Working experience in Databricks (strongly preferred) or a comparable cloud data platform such as Snowflake or BigQuery—experience with SQL warehouses, Unity Catalog, and notebooks or equivalent.
  • Enough data engineering knowledge to be self-sufficient: comfortable connecting data sources, setting up basic ingestion, and working with bronze, silver, and gold data layers, without needing to be a data engineer.
  • Experience building dashboards and reporting in Databricks AI/BI, Power BI, Tableau, or equivalent.
  • Experienced with analytics data design patterns such as star schema. Experience designing and building datasets following a similar design pattern is a plus.
  • Independently interprets data in the context of the client’s business, makes recommendations without guidance, and drives them to completion.
  • Exceptional communicator who can explain technical findings to marketers and executives, and business priorities to technical teams.
  • Python (PySpark or pandas) is a plus. Marketing analytics experience with CRM, lifecycle, or customer data is a strong plus.

How You Consult

  • At Senior level, you’re managing outcomes, not tasks. How you communicate and build trust determines whether clients see Stitch as a vendor or a partner.
  • Translate delivery complexity into business language. Lead meetings that drive decisions, not just updates.
  • Build relationships at multiple levels. Communicate effectively with C-suite, project leads, and technical teams, especially client and IT data leaders.
  • Lead with the “why”. Connect the business outcome to the technical work so IT teams have a reason to prioritize and change course.
  • Present risks with recommendations and tradeoffs, not just alerts.
  • Navigate scope boundaries with confidence — knowing when to hold firm and when to adapt
  • Own outcomes. Lead without being asked. Identify what needs doing and do it.
  • Stay persistent and constructive through slow-moving IT processes. Keep momentum without burning trust.

Tools You’ll Use

  • Databricks: SQL Editor, SQL Warehouses, Unity Catalog, Notebooks, basic ingestion and Jobs, AI/BI Dashboards, Genie
  • SQL, Python (PySpark), GitHub
  • BI platforms such as Power BI or Tableau
  • Stitch’s internal AI tooling

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in data analytics, analytics engineering, or business intelligence, with hands-on SQL as a core part of the role.
  • 1+ years of hands-on experience with Databricks or a comparable cloud data platform (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift).
  • Demonstrated track record of turning analysis into recommendations that changed a business decision.
  • Client-facing experience within an agency or consultancy required.
  • Marketing, CRM, or customer data experience preferred. Databricks certification (e.g., Data Analyst Associate) is a plus.
  • Must be eligible to work in the United States without visa sponsorship.

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance
  • 401k with company match
  • Flexible PTO policy
  • Monthly tech stipend
  • Paid parental leave
  • In-person onboarding experience at our HQ in Indianapolis, Indiana
  • Mental well-being support

BSCC enables the secure sharing of vital healthcare information to improve the speed, quality, safety, coordination, and cost of patient care. Preferred Experience

  • Exposure to InterSystems HealthShare, HealthInsight, EMPI, semantic interoperability, identity management, or related HIE technologies.
  • Exposure to Agile/Scrum or other structured project delivery methods.

Development Expectations

This junior-level position is intended to build progressively deeper capability in healthcare data integration and HIE technology. The successful candidate will initially work under the guidance of experienced technical staff and progressively take ownership of more complex configuration, testing, troubleshooting, participant communication, and implementation tasks.

Working Conditions and Physical Demands

Position works remotely within the United States and requires the ability to effectively use office equipment and technology.

Requires the ability to travel nationally by commercial air to attend meetings, conferences, and partner engagements on an occasional basis.

The position requires the ability to communicate effectively, participate in meetings, and perform work in a professional office or virtual environment. Qualified candidates can perform the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

Work Authorization & Location Requirements: Incumbent must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. BSCC does not sponsor employment visas. This position is remote within the United States; candidates must reside and perform work within the U.S.

  • Conduct market pricing and compensation analysis using salary survey data, industry benchmarks, internal pay data, and other relevant sources to support competitive and equitable pay recommendations.
  • Review job descriptions and evaluate new or revised positions to support appropriate job classification, level alignment, exemption status, and salary range placement.
  • Partner with Human Resources, Talent Acquisition, and business leaders to provide guidance on pay decisions, offer recommendations, promotions, transfers, equity adjustments, and other compensation-related matters.
  • Assist with annual compensation planning processes, including merit review, salary adjustments, incentive or bonus administration, budget tracking, data validation, reporting, and communication support.
  • Maintain accurate compensation data in HR systems, spreadsheets, and related files; audit compensation information regularly to ensure completeness, consistency, and data integrity.
  • Assist with preparation of compensation reports, analyses, and summaries to identify trends, pay compression concerns, internal equity considerations, market competitiveness, and potential risk areas.
  • Participate in compensation surveys and assist with gathering, submitting, and validating survey data to support market competitiveness reviews.
  • Ensure and support compliance with applicable federal, state, and Puerto Rico wage and hour laws, pay transparency requirements, FLSA guidelines, and internal compensation policies.
  • Research and respond to compensation-related questions or discrepancies by reviewing applicable data, policies, and procedures and escalating complex or sensitive matters as appropriate.
  • Assist with the development, maintenance, and revision of job descriptions, compensation documentation, process guides, templates, and communication materials.
  • Identify opportunities to improve compensation processes, reporting, workflows, and tools to support efficiency, accuracy, and a positive employee and manager experience.
  • Develop and maintain effective working relationships with HR partners, managers, and internal stakeholders to understand business needs and provide timely, practical compensation support.
  • Maintain a positive, results-oriented work environment, build partnerships within the team and across the organization, and model professionalism and teamwork.
  • Handle compensation information with discretion, confidentiality, accuracy, professionalism, and sound judgment.
  • Participate, lead, and/or present in team, department, management, or other meetings as needed.
  • May also support broader HR projects and initiatives.
  • Perform all other duties that may be requested or assigned.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

Minimum Qualifications: A bachelor’s degree and 2+ years of compensation, finance, or related analytical experience, OR an equivalent combination of education and experience is required. 1+ years of direct compensation experience, including compensation analysis, pay equity, market pricing, job evaluation, salary structure administration, or pay-related data analysis, is required. Working knowledge of federal, state, and Puerto Rico wage and hour requirements, FLSA classification guidelines, pay transparency requirements, and compensation compliance practices is required. Experience in healthcare, clinical research, multi-state employers, and with remote workforce environments is preferred. A professional HR or compensation certification, such as CCP, PHR, SHRM-CP, or equivalent, is preferred.

Required Skills:
  • Proficiency with computer applications such as Microsoft applications (Word, Excel, PP, Teams, Sharepoint), web applications, and the ability to type proficiently (40+ wpm)
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including formulas, lookups, pivot tables, data validation, filtering, sorting, and analysis of large data sets.
  • Strong analytical and mathematical skills with the ability to interpret compensation data, identify trends, evaluate pay practices, and prepare accurate, actionable recommendations.
  • High attention to detail and accuracy when handling salary data, job information, employee records, calculations, reports, and compensation recommendations.
  • Strong organizational, time management, problem-solving, and project coordination skills, with the ability to meet deadlines and manage competing priorities.
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain compensation data, policies, and recommendations clearly to HR partners, managers, and business leaders.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and handle highly sensitive compensation and employee information with discretion and professionalism.
  • Well-developed interpersonal and listening skills and the ability to work well independently and collaboratively within a team environment, building trusted relationships with team, co-workers, managers, and external customers.
  • Must possess a high degree of professionalism, integrity, dependability, respect for others, self-motivation, and a strong work ethic.
  • Ability to work under minimal supervision, identify problems and implement solutions.
  • Ability to handle highly sensitive information in a confidential and professional manner, and in compliance with privacy and company guidelines.

Benefits

  • Full-time employees regularly scheduled to work at least 30 hours per week are benefits-eligible, with coverage starting on the first day of the month following date of hire.
  • Medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short and long-term disability insurance, health savings accounts, supplemental insurances, and a 401k plan with a safe harbor match are offered.

Position Title:

Natural Hazards Planner Floods (Limited Duration)

Job Description:

Join the Oregon Department of Land Conservation and Development (DLCD) as a Natural Hazards Planner – Floods to reduce the risk of flooding by helping the Oregon coordinator for the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP).

A day in the life

As the new Natural Hazards Planner - Floods you will:

  • Help cities and counties participate in the NFIP
  • Review cities and counties for compliance with the requirements of the NFIP
  • Draft amendments to development regulations to reduce risk and comply with NFIP requirements.
  • Do outreach to broad audiences about flood hazards generally and specifically about flood insurance
  • Give technical advice on reducing flood risk
  • If a natural disaster occurs, help cities and counties recover
  • Depending on workload and funding, plan for reducing the risk from other natural hazards

For the full position description, please email Jan.Guerrero@dlcd.oregon.gov.

Limited Duration

This position is primarily funded by a grant from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). The current grant runs through June 30, 2027. DLCD intends to apply to FEMA to renew the annual grant and continue the position, but we cannot guarantee future funding.

DLCD Vision and Mission

Vision: An Oregon where everyone can live, work, and thrive.

Mission: The Department of Land Conservation and Development (DLCD) leads Oregon’s land use planning program for the benefit of current and future generations. DLCD partners with communities as they cultivate places where everyone can live, work, and thrive.

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

One of DLCD’s foundational goals is to become a diverse, equitable, and inclusive agency that implements an equitable and inclusive planning program for Oregon. Efforts are supported by the State of Oregon Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Action Plan and an agency Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) Committee and Work Plan.

At DLCD, all employees are expected to recognize value in individual and cultural differences; lead activities in their division to promote and foster a diverse workforce; actively engage in implementing the DEI Work Plan and associated activities including achieving the agency’s affirmative action objectives and goals.

We recognize that to successfully meet our mission and agency values, our commitment to racial equity, diversity, equity, and inclusion must be at the center of our work. DLCD values the lived and professional experiences of individuals from historically and currently underserved and under-resourced communities and honor our Government-to-Government relations responsibilities with Oregon’s federally recognized Native American Tribes. We are committed to building and sustaining an inclusive, belonging, and equitable working environment for all employees. Candidates with diverse racial, ethnic, and cultural backgrounds, language fluencies, lived experiences, and skillsets are encouraged to apply.

What’s in it for you:

  • Opportunity to collaborate with a team of talented professionals who are passionate about the agency’s mission and priorities.
  • Flexible work location, with a mix of remote and in-office work.
  • 11 paid holidays per year and additional personal business time off.
  • Comprehensive benefit package options.

The Benefits

The State of Oregon offers a competitive and affordable health and benefits package, including excellent medical, vision and dental coverage, paid holidays off, personal business leave, paid vacation, and paid sick leave. In addition to standard medical benefits and employee leave, the state also provides additional optional benefits, such as basic life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, and flexible spending accounts for health care and childcare expenses.

After a qualifying period, new employees are enrolled in the Oregon Public Service Retirement Plan (OPSRP). State employees also have access to benefits like deferred compensation plans through the Oregon Savings Growth Plan and the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program.

Join thousands of state employees who came for a job and stayed for a career!

Minimum Qualifications

This position in classified as a Planner 2. The minimum qualifications for a Planner 2 position:

A master's degree in Community, Urban or Regional Planning, Public Administration, Social Science, Civil Engineering, Architecture, Economics, Geography or a related field;

OR

A bachelor's degree in urban or Regional Planning, Public Administration, Social Science, Civil Engineering, Architecture, Economics, Geography or a related field AND one year of progressively responsible planning experience related to the job;

OR

Four years of progressively responsible planning experience related to the job;

OR

An equivalent combination of relevant education, training, and experience.

We’re Also Looking for:

  • Experience in or knowledge of regulating development in flood hazard areas
  • Certification as a floodplain manager by the Association of State Floodplain Managers
  • Experience in or knowledge of local government planning, especially land use planning in Oregon
  • Lived or professional experience serving individuals from historically and currently underserved and under-resourced communities
  • Fluency in languages other than English, especially Spanish

You do not need to have all these qualities to be eligible for this position, but be sure to let us know which you do have in your cover letter and resume. We use that information to choose whom we will interview.

Your candidate profile, cover letter, and resume are the perfect place to display your interest in the position and highlight the skills and experience you will bring, making you the best candidate for the position. Overview

Iovance is seeking a Compensation Analyst reporting directly to the Sr. Director, Total Rewards & HR Operations. The Compensation Analyst serves as a key front‑ and back‑end partner to the business, providing advanced analytical expertise and strategic support across the organization. This role is responsible for balancing compensation best practices with practical flexibility, ensuring solutions are both compliant and business‑aligned. title: Program Manager
description:
The Program Manager is responsible for the operational success of VOAPA’s Master Leasing and Brian’s Place programming, ensuring seamless staff and volunteer team management, program development, implementation, delivery, quality control, and outcome evaluation. Master Leasing serves individuals who are experiencing housing instability along with severe and persistent mental health concerns. The program provides housing to participants across 20+ scattered-site units within Luzerne County as well as VOAPA’s owned Academy Street Apartments. Brian’s Place offers the Respite Center, a daytime recuperative care program for individuals experiencing homelessness coupled with complex healthcare challenges, as well as five units of permanent, affordable housing. The tenants residing in Brian’s Place often have dual enrollment under Master Leasing. The Program Manager oversees the day-to-day operations of both programs, splitting their time evenly between the two. The Program Manager fosters healthy team dynamics between Case Managers, Community Health Workers, Resident Advisors, and Housing Specialists who operate within the programs and under the manager’s supervision. The Program Manager develops and maintains essential community partnerships and serves as a key representative for VOAPA programs in the community.

Scope of Duties:

Interact with all participants, staff, and community members with respect and courtesy.

Build knowledge of respite and recuperative care programming and strengthen the programming within the Respite Center at Brian’s Place.

Raise community awareness and support around Brian’s Place and Master Leasing to increase volunteers, donations, and services.

Provide daily supervision to employees, volunteers, and interns assigned to programs within the purview. Create employee schedules weekly.

Oversee staff development by coordinating regularly scheduled one-on-one supervision opportunities, monthly team meetings and/or team-building activities, and cultivating and hosting relevant trainings for the group.

Ensure client confidentiality is maintained through HIPAA standards through all aspects of daily business.

Develop collaborative relationships with outside agencies and housing resources to increase referral options.

Assume scheduled on-call duties outside of business hours to support 24/7 programming staff in crises. Collaborate with the on-call staff to respond to critical incidents which may occur at any time of day since some programming is open 24 hours a day and 7 days a week. Alternative coverage will be coordinated when after-hours on-call availability is limited (vacations, personal emergencies, etc.).

Attend community-based meetings, as needed, and act as liaison between VOAPA programs in purview and external social service agencies and partners. Attend weekly Treatment Court meetings relevant to Master Leasing participants at the Luzerne County Courthouse and serve as a liaison between Master Leasing case management and the directives of the treatment court group.

Be knowledgeable about the programs’ intake, referral, and documentation processes and general policies and procedures to orient and offer guidance to team members in their day-to-day. This includes understanding organizational processes related to human resources and financial management.

Maintain statistical data on demographics and trends via VOAPA’s electronic health record system. Track outcomes based on funding source requirements. Ensure case documents and notes are accurately input promptly.

Enter participant data for individuals served via the Respite Center at Brian’s Place into PA HMIS daily.

Frequently monitor the work environment of teams (including within the Brian’s Place complex, Academy Street Apartments, and scattered-site units) to ensure fire and general property safety, upkeep of building maintenance, and supply management. Alert the Senior Director, Property or a Property Manager of concerns or necessary repairs immediately.

Manage site safety through regular staff trainings and drills on responding to an overdose, mental health crisis, domestic violence, outside threats, and emergencies.

Conduct regular supervision and annual performance reviews for direct reports.

Demonstrate a positive and professional image toward participants and agency representatives. Conduct self to promote dignity and respect for all staff, residents, volunteers, and the general public. Collaborate with local colleges and universities to support internship and research opportunities for students. Develop and implement policies and procedures in coordination with the Programs Director.

Conduct weekly participant case reviews. Coordinate weekly progress check meetings to ensure participants are completing goals outlined in the goal plan and that staff have the tools and resources necessary to assist those participants in achieving their goals.

Clock in and out daily and ensure that the correct working hours are submitted to the supervisor.

Review and approve, if appropriate, the timecards and paid time off of direct employee reports.

In situations where policy is questioned or in case of emergency, the supervisor is to be contacted.

Perform other duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Required Skills:

Integrity, discretion, and respect for confidentiality and privacy.

Critical thinking skills and an ability to work autonomously.

Excellent oral communication skills and the ability to de-escalate misunderstandings, errors, or conflicts in a diplomatic manner.

Willingness to learn and self-improve for professional growth.

Typing, computing, and data entry skills.

Strong empathy and interpersonal skills.

Good communication and customer service skills.

Ability to use verbal and nonverbal communication skills to build rapport.

Analytical skills.

Ability to foresee and mitigate inequities.

Ability to prioritize and work under pressure.

Ability to provide trauma-informed care.

Time management skills.

Personal organization skills.

Attention to detail.

Strong spelling, math, and financial skills.

Documentation skills.

Work Environment:

The individual will report to Brian’s Place daily unless scheduled projects require them to begin their day at a different site. The individual may report to housing facilities central to Wilkes-Barre such as the Academy Apartments or scattered sublet apartments throughout Luzerne County, including those located in Wilkes-Barre and Plymouth. The individual will have access to an agency vehicle for travel, a shared workspace at Brian’s Place, and a private workspace within the Academy Street Apartments. The individual can expect to share bathrooms and kitchen access with other employees and tenants. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, and filing cabinets. The role relies heavily on the use of the internet and technology for documentation and communication. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate but can become loud depending on the participant activities that occur. They may encounter the public or crises involving people served on occasion.

ADA Essential Functions:

Regularly required to stand, walk, sit, use hands to handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, climb stairs, talk, hear, and smell

Regularly lift and move up to 50 lbs.

Ability to see clearly at 20 inches or less.

Ability to identify and/or distinguish colors.

Ability to observe an area that can be seen up and down or to the left and right while remain fixed on a given point.

Credentials/Abilities:

The employee in this position must possess a minimum of an Associate’s Degree related to the human services field or at least (3) years of experience in the field of human services. Prior supervisory experience is preferred. The employee must possess a strong ability to make immediate decisions when faced with crisis or unusual situations. The employee must have a working knowledge of PA HMIS, PUPS, computer software, specifically Microsoft Office, including Outlook, Excel, and Word, as well as effective written and verbal communication skills. The employee must possess a strong ability to make immediate decisions when faced with a crisis or unusual situation.

Pennsylvania State Police clearances are required annually. A valid Pennsylvania driver’s license is required along with a good Driver’s History Report conducted annually; the employee will drive for meetings, community events, etc. Valid insurance on a personal vehicle is required.

Why Wells Fargo:

Are you looking for more? Find it here. At Wells Fargo, we're more than a financial services leader – we’re a global trailblazer committed to driving innovation, empowering communities, and helping our customers succeed. We believe that a meaningful career is much more than just a job – it’s about finding all of the elements to help you thrive, in one place. And we’re recognized for it – Wells Fargo once again ranked in the top three – making us the #1 financial services employer – on the 2026 LinkedIn Top Companies list of best workplaces “to grow your career” in the U.S. Join us!


About this role:

Wells Fargo is seeking a Senior Branch Premier Banker (SAFE) to play a pivotal role within our National Branch Network. This role grows, deepens, and manages relationships with affluent customers and those with more complex financial needs, serving as their primary point of contact for banking products and services through scheduled appointments, lobby engagement, and proactive outreach. This role is designed for growth-oriented professionals who lead with advice to acquire and deepen relationships through meaningful discovery and translate customer goals into comprehensive financial strategies. You will own and actively grow a defined book of business, leveraging goals based planning, and prudent risk oversight to deliver integrated solutions across deposits, investments, credit, home lending, and business banking. In addition, you’ll help customers with everyday banking needs-opening accounts, handling service requests, and ensuring a seamless experience making it easier for them to manage their banking with confidence. Success in this role is driven by strong relationship acumen, proactive customer engagement, and seamless collaboration with internal partners across Wealth, Home Lending, and Business Banking to deliver a differentiated customer experience.


Wells Fargo rewards behaviors that consistently create long term customer value and support customers in making informed financial decisions. You’ll be supported with digital tools, industry leading training, ongoing coaching, and backed by one of the most recognized brands in banking. This role offers a clear platform for career growth for experienced professionals who excel at building trust, managing a portfolio, and delivering holistic, multi product solutions.


In this role you will:

  • Proactively acquire new affluent consumer and business customers while deepening existing relationships through strategic outreach, referrals, and pre-planned customer appointments
  • Lead discovery‑driven conversations to understand customer goals and deliver tailored banking and credit strategies that strengthen relationships, increase retention, and drive balanced growth across deposits, lending, and investments
  • Serve as the primary financial partner delivering comprehensive, multi‑product guidance and ongoing reviews across life stages and evolving financial needs
  • Partner with a team of professionals across Wealth, Home Lending, and Business Banking to deliver integrated solutions by coordinating warm introductions, setting clear expectations, and taking personal ownership to convert qualified opportunities into closed outcomes
  • Champion digital adoption by educating customers on self-service and mobile banking options to elevate satisfaction, engagement, and service efficiency
  • Serve as an active member of the branch team by advising colleagues on relationship development and the management of complex client needs
  • Demonstrate risk excellence through accurate documentation, sound judgment, timely issue escalation, and adherence to policies and regulations to support strong control outcomes
  • The Senior Branch Premier Banker LP (license pending) role is a temporary position until employee has successfully completed licensing requirements and SAFE registration. Upon successful completion, employees will transition to the Senior Branch Premier Banker (SAFE) role. Employees hired into the Senior Branch Premier Banker LP role who are not fully licensed will participate in the Branch Network Licensed Banker program

Required Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of customer service experience, or equivalent demonstrated through one or a combination of the following: work experience, training, military experience, education
  • 3+ years of experience building and maintaining effective relationships with customers and partners
  • 3+ years of experience recommending products and services

Desired Qualifications:

  • Experience recommending financial products and translating customer goals into clear, actionable recommendations
  • Demonstrated ability to proactively source, acquire, and deepen relationships through proactive outreach and building strong internal partnership to support the customer experience
  • Proven experience managing a book-of-business, documentation of planning conversations, and consistent follow-through to drive retention and growth across deposits, lending, and investments
  • Experience coaching or supporting peers to strengthen team performance and customer impact
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly and confidently, listen with empathy, and build credibility and trust quickly with others

For any FINRA qualification exams earned after Sept. 30, 2018, the Securities Industry Essentials (SIE) exam is also required

  • SAFE registration is required at the time of employment and Wells Fargo will initiate the process after your start date. Loan Originators must meet LO/CFPB requirements and comply with Wells Fargo policies, including standards related to financial responsibility, character, fitness, and criminal background. A credit report may be reviewed (credit score not included) and additional ongoing screening may apply

  • Collaborate with stakeholders, users, technical teams, and software engineers to translate operational needs into actionable data and technical requirements
  • Engage with users and customers to identify and understand underlying business and technical needs
  • Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams to solve complex problems involving interrelated and interdependent objectives
  • Support the complete AI product development lifecycle, including conceptualization, design, implementation, testing, and evaluation
  • Stay current with emerging AI/ML technologies, research, tools, and industry practices and apply relevant advancements to ongoing initiatives

  • Demonstrated experience developing software using multiple programming languages and statistical packages
  • Knowledge of dataset management and analysis tools and AI/ML technologies
  • Demonstrated experience working with databases
  • Experience working with structured and unstructured data
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to use data and metrics to drive technical and product decisions
  • Experience analyzing and assessing data quality for AI/ML applications
  • Strong critical-thinking skills and demonstrated ability to collaboratively solve complex problems in a team environment
  • Agile/Scrum experience and familiarity with Agile methodologies
  • Demonstrated ability and willingness to continuously learn and adapt to rapidly evolving AI technologies
  • Familiarity with current AI research, technologies, and industry developments
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively with technical teams, users, and stakeholders

title: Enterprise Network Administrator - 24x7 Ops & Security
description:

Operational Support & Service Reliability: Monitor and maintain performance, capacity, availability, and health of network infrastructure and services. Provide 2nd/3rd level support for incidents and service requests, including connectivity, performance, wireless, routing, switching, firewalls and VPNs; document root causes and escalate as needed. Monitor security platforms and logs; maintain evidence for reviews and audits. Change, Documentation & Continuous Improvement: Prepare and execute change requests with implementation, testing, validation and back-out plans. Maintain accurate network diagrams, inventories, configurations and knowledge articles. Improve scripts, templates, monitoring, and processes to strengthen reliability and reduce manual effort. Collaboration & Service Delivery: Build relationships with business departments, vendors and service providers; provide guidance and knowledge sharing. Support other network initiatives and comply with policies and regulatory requirements. 3+ years hands-on experience administering and supporting network infrastructure in a multi-site or enterprise environment. Strong practical knowledge of multi-site routing and switching (TCP/IP, VLANs, STP, OSPF, BGP, DHCP, DNS, NAT, QoS). CCNA or equivalent practical experience required or expected within development period. CCNP or Palo Alto certifications are assets. Strong analytical, documentation, communication skills.

title: GRC & Privacy Analyst
description:
Founded by Arianna Huffington in 2016, Thrive Global is a leading behavior change technology company with the mission to improve productivity and health outcomes – one Microstep at a time. Thrive helps individuals and organizations improve well-being, performance and mental resilience with its AI-powered behavior change technology platform. Thrive’s Microsteps – small, science-backed steps to improve health and productivity – have been adopted by employees at more than 230 organizations in over 160 countries, from frontline and call center workers to executives at multinational companies. For more information, visit www.thriveglobal.com.

Thrive Global is seeking a detail-oriented GRC (Governance, Risk, and Compliance) and Privacy Analyst to strengthen our security, compliance, and data privacy posture. In this role, you will own and operationalize compliance programs, manage audit cycles, and help embed privacy-by-design principles across a health-focused, data-sensitive organization. This is an ideal position for someone who thrives at the intersection of security frameworks, privacy regulation, and modern automation tooling.

How You’ll Contribute

  • Administer and optimize compliance automation platforms such as Vanta, maintaining continuous control monitoring and evidence collection.
  • Lead and support audits across multiple frameworks, coordinating with internal stakeholders and external assessors.
  • Maintain and mature compliance programs mapped to SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27701, ISO 42001, HITRUST, HIPAA, NIST 800-53, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF).
  • Interpret and apply privacy standards including HIPAA and GDPR, ensuring data handling practices meet regulatory obligations.
  • Conduct risk assessments, track remediation efforts, and manage evidence and control documentation.
  • Apply project management discipline to compliance initiatives — setting timelines, coordinating cross-functional owners, and driving deliverables to completion.
  • Leverage AI tools to improve efficiency in evidence review, policy drafting, risk analysis, and reporting workflows.

Qualifications & Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university required.
  • Demonstrated experience with GRC and compliance automation applications, particularly Vanta.
  • Working knowledge of key security and privacy frameworks: SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27701, ISO 42001, HITRUST, HIPAA, NIST 800-53, and NIST AI RMF.
  • Strong understanding of privacy regulations, including HIPAA and GDPR.
  • Proven experience managing or supporting audits and applying structured project management practices.
  • Comfort and fluency with AI tools and a willingness to integrate them into daily workflows.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with strong attention to detail.
  • Relevant certifications (e.g., CISA, CIPP, ISO 27001 Implementer).
  • Experience in a healthcare, wellness, or otherwise regulated data environment.
  • Familiarity with AI governance and emerging AI compliance requirements.

✨ What We Offer:

  • Mission-Driven Impact: Be part of a company that’s truly making a difference in people’s lives around the world.
  • Career Growth: Develop within the company and help shape our growth strategy.
  • Human-Centric Culture: Thrive in a supportive environment with a range of wellness perks and benefits.
  • Competitive Compensation: Enjoy a comprehensive and rewarding total compensation package.
  • Health & Financial Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision coverage plus a 401(k) program with company match.
  • Time to Recharge: Generous paid time-off programs designed to help you rest, reset, and recharge — including Thrive Time, a benefit unique to Thrive that gives employees additional paid time off after major projects or intense periods of work to truly recharge and recover.

Compensation:

Total target compensation for this role will be $115,000 – $125,000.

  • Please note: We provide a competitive mix of salary, performance bonus, and equity. The final offer amount will depend on factors like experience, expertise, and may differ from the range above. This range also excludes additional benefits, such as 401(k), and medical, dental, or vision insurance.

title: O&M Sr. Origination Manager - Capital Projects and DevCo
description:

Sedentary work involves sitting most of the time, limited walking, and standing. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand, walk, use hands to finger, handle, or feel, and reach with hands and arms

Qualified Aquatech projects include a credible O&M offer early in development. Measure results by the share of qualified projects pursued with O&M, the value and margin of O&M awards, and forecast accuracy.

description:
Maersk is a global leader in integrated logistics and have been industry pioneers for over a century. Through innovation and transformation, we are redefining the boundaries of possibility, continuously setting new standards for efficiency, sustainability, and excellence.

At Maersk, we believe in the power of diversity, collaboration, and continuous learning and we work hard to ensure that the people in our organization reflect and understand the customers we exist to serve.

Join us as we harness cutting-edge technologies and unlock opportunities on a global scale. Together, let's sail towards a brighter, more sustainable future with Maersk.

We Offer

You will be interacting daily with colleagues internationally, giving you the opportunity to develop your professional skills in a global environment. We provide support for you to shape your own career by achieving expertise and learning on the job.

About the role

As an Ocean Customer Experience Senior Specialist - Spanish, you will own the overall customer experience for a portfolio of Direct Transport customers shipping with our Ocean and Intermodal products. You will be the team's go-to operational expert - managing escalations, building contingency plans, leading business reviews with customers, and driving initiatives that deliver tangible value for our customers and for Maersk.

What you will do

  • Onboard new customers onto our standard processes and digital platforms, building a strong foundation for a long-term partnership.
  • Promote digital and self-service solutions so customers get reliable, consistent service at scale.
  • Manage day-to-day customer communication, responding promptly and coordinating with your team - and reaching out proactively to your customers during major service disruptions.
  • Handle transactional activities including calls in line with agreed customer operating procedures and internal standards.
  • Coordinate the end-to-end shipment journey, working with teams across operations, sales, finance and product to deliver a seamless customer experience.
  • Resolve routine exceptions independently, either directly or by working through our global network.
  • Manage operational escalations and non-routine exceptions, putting contingency plans in place to minimize customer impact.
  • Lead regular business reviews with customers (where applicable) to review performance and align on future plans and priorities.
  • Drive continuous improvement to make it easier and more efficient for customers to do business with us.
  • Identify growth opportunities by offering customers additional products and solutions that match their needs.
  • Improve contract fulfilment (where applicable) through regular customer check-ins and collaboration with Sales and Product teams.
  • Drive value-creating initiatives with internal stakeholders or customers that deliver near-term, measurable business outcomes.

How your impact will be measured

You will be measured on customer outcomes and operational performance, including:

  • Customer satisfaction (e.g., NPS, CSAT)
  • Responsiveness and issue resolution turnaround time
  • Quality of issue handling and adoption of self-service tools
  • Adherence to agreed service standards
  • Productivity
  • Upselling / cross-selling and contract fulfilment
  • Business impact of improvement initiatives
  • Actively engage and contribute towards continuous improvement

Who you will work with

  • Customers - primarily day-to-day logistics contacts and team leads
  • Internal teams including our Global Service Centre, Sales, Operations, Finance, Product and Ocean Fulfilment
  • External partners such as terminals, depots, customs brokers, transport agents and truckers
  • Senior customer stakeholders and decision makers
  • Global product and customer experience teams

What we are looking for

Essential

  • Proven ownership - you go beyond your own scope to drive improvements and help others take accountability
  • Strong customer partnership - you anticipate risks, plan for disruptions and work with customers on solutions that support their business goals
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management, including with senior audiences
  • Strong data skills - you can turn data into clear insights and recommendations
  • Structured problem solving and a continuous improvement mindset
  • Solid knowledge of ocean and/or intermodal freight products and processes

Desirable

  • Understanding of end-to-end supply chain management
  • Project management experience

Qualifications & experience

  • Qualification: Bachelors Graduate, College Undergraduate maybe considered.
  • Experience: Minimum 4-5 years of experience in the logistics, shipping, call center or service industry.
  • Language proficiency: Proficient in Spanish and English, additional language such as German or French, is an advantage.
  • AI proficiency and upskilling: Working proficiency in AI-enabled tools, with a demonstrated commitment to continuous learning, upskilling, and the adoption of new digital technologies.


Don't rule yourself out if you don't tick every box. Depending on the role, transferable skills such as customer focus, communication, analytical thinking, problem-solving, accuracy and process discipline can be just as important as previous logistics experience.

Why join GSC?


Global work. Local teams. Real impact.

A career in GSC can take you in many directions. You can deepen your specialist expertise, move into people leadership, work in process excellence or transformation, build capability in training, or explore opportunities across the wider Maersk organization.

You'll have the opportunity to:

  • Work with colleagues and stakeholders across countries, functions and markets.
  • Build valuable expertise in a global logistics environment.
  • Learn through meaningful, hands-on experience.
  • Contribute to customer outcomes and better ways of working.
  • Develop your career through specialist, leadership, project and transformation pathways.

Ready to make your move?

If you're looking for a role where you can grow your skills, collaborate internationally and contribute to work with global impact, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and discover where a career with Maersk GSC could take you.
