title: Senior / Staff Threat Intelligence Analyst, Hacks
description:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM’s platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

About the Role

When a protocol is drained, or an exchange is compromised, our customers need to know within minutes or hours which addresses to block and where the funds are going. You will own TRM’s answer to that, end-to-end.

As a Senior / Staff Threat Intelligence Analyst, you will lead TRM’s hacks category: the metrics, the system that hits them, and the contractor team that keeps it running around the clock. You will size that team and make the case for the coverage it requires. We align on the outcome; the approach is yours.

The impact you will have

  • Take command when a big hack breaks and act as a leader. Run TRM’s response: triage, coordination across teams, internal and customer communications, and the incident report afterwards. Victim-engaged recovery work is typically led by our Global Investigations team.

  • Build the machine with AI. Build the tools and agents that automate intake and first attribution, so hacks of every size reach TRM fast, with human quality control over every output.

  • Get every major hack into TRM fast. Make sure every major hack is visible to customers within hours of the first credible public report, around the clock.

  • Keep TRM’s hack data complete and accurate. Every hack, at any size, is recorded with its entity, theft addresses, date, amount, and hack type.

  • Follow the money at scale. Design the system, with our Data Science and engineering teams, that carries hack-specific attribution downstream as stolen funds move.

  • Explain how it happened. Root-cause the most important hacks and publish best-in-industry technical analysis that makes TRM the first source cited.

  • See the next one coming. Build approaches that spot vulnerable contracts before they are exploited, and get them into our product.

What we’re looking for

  • 5+ years of professional experience in blockchain intelligence, crypto investigations, cyber threat intelligence, incident response, or a closely related field.

  • Has owned incident response in a high-stakes environment (exchange, security firm, incident response, or CTI team): war rooms, incident reports, communications under pressure.

  • Strong on-chain tracing, deep on EVM, and at least one of: BTC, TRON, or Solana, including bridges, cross-chain swaps, and mixers.

  • Understands how DeFi, bridge, and exchange exploits work, and how attackers behave after the theft.

  • Applied AI fluency. We expect you to already be building AI-assisted or agentic workflows in your daily analytical work, to be able to show how you validate their outputs and where they fail, and to treat AI as a force multiplier.

  • Experience managing contractors or leading a small team.

  • Writes and briefs clearly, from technical deep-dives to executive summaries.

  • Hands-on and highly accountable: does the hardest work, not only coordinates it.

Nice to have

  • Smart-contract reverse-engineering (Solidity).

  • Experience at a security auditor or blockchain analytics firm.

  • Experience following specific well-known hacker groups.

About the Team

The hacks function sits within TRM’s Primary Intelligence organization, alongside the Facilitation & Money Laundering (F&ML) pod. You will work closely with the Nation States, Cyber Threat Intelligence, and Global Investigations teams, as well as with Data Science and Engineering on automation, and with Marketing on publications.

Team Operating Rhythms

  • Monthly metrics review with your manager.

  • Weekly operating sync with your team.

  • Regular syncs with your team across time zones.

  • A war room, run by you, whenever a major hack breaks.

  • On-call responsibilities

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We’re excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

title: NASA Missions Schedule Analyst- Remote (Spacecraft Exp. Desired)
description:
CTS seeks a Schedule Analyst Subject Matter Expert to provide technical expertise to the Evaluations, Assessments, Studies, Services, and Support (EASSS) contract. This contract supports NASA Headquarters Science Mission Directorate (SMD) and facilitates NASA’s pursuit of the most noteworthy approaches for missions, payloads, spacecraft, instruments, and research that help answer the big questions in Earth and Space science. Located at LaRC, the NASA’s Science Office for Mission Assessments (SOMA) helps SMD select and manage missions, spacecraft, and instruments. To accomplish this, SOMA manages and provides oversight of evaluations, assessments, and studies for SMD and other NASA organizations. These include evaluation of proposals received in response to NASA Announcements of Opportunity, NASA Research Announcements, Cooperative Agreement Notices, and Broad Agency Announcements, as well as highly specialized studies and assessments, such as life cycle and independent cost estimates, schedule assessments, and risk analyses. CTS supports SOMA via the EASSS contract by providing subject matter experts who will apply their expertise to complex proposal evaluations, management and technical assessments, and advanced studies through the EASSS contract.

CTS’s subject matter experts need not be local to the program office near NASA Langley Research Center in Hampton, VA. We seek individuals who bring significant Technical, Management and Cost expertise in missions, payloads, spacecraft and instruments relevant to NASA’s mission. The work is performed remotely with less than 10% travel occurring periodically for some during the assignment to bring the geographically distributed teams together for workshops to finalize results.

The Schedule Analysis evaluators shall have demonstrated knowledge and proficiency in generating and maintaining NASA spaceflight mission schedules through all development phases. Evaluators shall be proficient in utilizing Microsoft Project to analyze schedule metrics such as critical path, secondary critical paths, and schedule margin. Evaluators shall be familiar with the NASA Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) Handbook and have experience assessing schedule completeness across WBS elements.

Education: Must have a Bachelor’s Degree in Mathematics, Finance, Engineering, or other directly related field.

We thank you for your time and consideration of our current opening. If you choose to apply please be sure to upload your most recent and detailed resume for our review.

title: Academic Success Coordinator
description:
Job Description

Position Summary:

The Department of Fish, Wildlife, and Conservation Biology (FWCB) seeks an Academic Success Coordinator to serve as a key member of its advising success team, providing high-quality academic advising, student success and career development instruction, outreach, communication, and student success assessment support for undergraduate students. This full-time, 12-month Administrative Professional position reports to the FWCB Undergraduate Program Coordinator and collaborates closely with the FWCB Advising Team, Curriculum Committee, faculty, and the Warner College Academic Success Collaborative. The position requires regular in-person work during business hours, with occasional evening and weekend responsibilities.

The Academic Success Coordinator supports undergraduate success by helping students transition to the university, build community, navigate degree requirements, connect with faculty and career opportunities, and progress toward timely graduation. Key responsibilities include academic advising, maintaining student records, analyzing student success data, serving on advising-related committees, leading the "New to the Major Seminar," providing pre-departure instruction for students participating in the Japan Education Abroad program, supporting Ram Orientation, assisting with student success initiatives and communications, and fostering strong collaborative relationships across the department, college, and university.


For full consideration, apply by Thursday, December 24, 2026, 11:59 PM (MT).


Essential Duties:

Academic Advising:

  • Advise FWCB undergraduate students on curriculum, course offerings, degree progress, and graduation planning; assist with overload requests, graduation contracts, substitutions, and other student success processes. Collaborate with the Undergraduate Coordinator, Advising Team, and faculty on career-specific and experiential learning opportunities, and develop knowledge of careers in wildlife biology, conservation biology, fisheries biology, ecology, and natural resources.
  • Provide individualized advising that recognizes each student’s path to degree completion and responds to the needs of diverse populations, including non-traditional, first-generation, veteran, underrepresented, and transfer students. Maintain accessible virtual and in-person office hours, regular email access, reliable responsiveness, and accurate advising records. Help implement support plans for students on academic probation and address the causes of their difficulties.
  • Assist with developing, coordinating, and delivering programming that supports student outcomes, graduation progress, and overall success. Advise students during Ram Orientation and Ram Welcome; meet with high school students, parents, guests, and prospective transfer students; support student clubs and organizations; and provide recommendation letters and references when appropriate.
  • Develop and update informational documents, flyers, advising publications, manuals, curriculum check sheets, and targeted student outreach through Canvas, Navigate, and other channels. Pursue professional development in advising best practices, introduce innovative ideas, share resources, and collaborate with Department, College, University, and external partners to improve advising and student support.

Instruction:

  • Coordinate and teach the “New to the Major Seminar” and preparatory lectures for students studying abroad in Japan. Update student success content, develop engaging and interactive learning opportunities, maintain the Canvas learning portal, build partnerships and arrange guest speakers from across the University and employers, and work with Peer Advisors on assignment grading.

Campus Collaboration/Service Administration:

  • Assist with designing and delivering interventions that address barriers to student success identified through student performance data. Collaborate with the FWCB Advising Team and faculty to develop a comprehensive, supportive undergraduate experience.
  • Attend meetings and trainings, build partnerships, and serve on committees with the Career Center, academic advisors, other Academic Success Coordinators, faculty, Collaborative for Student Achievement, Health Center, Case Management, Housing and Dining Services, University Honors Program, Cultural Centers, and other campus offices. Serve as the Advising Team’s liaison and a contributing member of the College and University Academic Success Coordinator Network to share best practices and support student success.

Assessment:

  • Assist with collecting, tracking, summarizing, and analyzing student success data and indicators; measure progress for individual students and groups, including concentrations; and contribute to annual reporting and assessment of student success and advising impact. Use assessment findings to respond to FWCB, WCNR, and CSU student needs and continually improve advising, programming, and outreach.

Conditions of Employment:

  • Pre-employment Criminal Background Check (required for all new hires).
  • The successful candidate must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. by the proposed start date.

Supervision:

  • Assist with duty delegation of Peer Advisors who are undergraduate students.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Master's degree with at least one year of higher education advising experience OR a Bachelor's degree with three years of higher education experience focused on advising and/or supporting students.
  • Experience working directly with students in a college/university setting, providing academic advising and/or conducting student development activities such as orientation, diversity support services, or career services.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in counseling, higher education, student affairs, wildlife biology/ecology, fisheries biology/ecology, conservation, or other natural resources related field.
  • Experience mentoring and advising college students.
  • Personal and professional commitment to diversity and inclusion as demonstrated by persistent effort, active planning, allocation of time and/or accountability for diversity outcome.
  • Excellent communication skills, including interpersonal, presentation, writing and technical/computer skills.
  • Experience teaching, presenting to, and/or leading large groups, and/or public speaking experience.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple projects in a timely and highly organized manner.

title: Manager, Quality (Night Shift)
description:
This is where your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your Role at Baxter

The Manager I, Quality Operations leads the Quality Line Operations organization and is accountable for compliant, timely, and effective Quality support across manufacturing operations. This role manages Quality Assurance II, Operations leaders and their teams, owns departmental results, and provides the next level of escalation for product, process, documentation, staffing, and compliance issues. The Manager ensures decisions and activities align with Baxter procedures, current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP), Good Documentation Practices (cGDocP), regulatory requirements, and patient and customer expectations.


Your Team

Baxter is focused on saving and sustaining lives by manufacturing high-quality products. Quality and Manufacturing leaders collaborate to manage risk, maintain reliable operations, resolve complex issues, and continuously improve performance.


Position Overview

This role leads Quality Line Operations across day and night shifts through Quality Assurance II, Operations leaders. The Manager establishes strategy, priorities, staffing, and performance expectations; develops leaders and succession plans; and partners with Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality Systems, and site leadership.


What You’ll Be Doing

  • Manage Quality Line Operations across assigned manufacturing areas and shifts, with accountability for compliance, product quality, service, safety, staffing, and departmental performance.
  • Directly supervise Quality Assurance II, Operations leaders and manage the broader Technician and Lead organization through subordinate leaders.
  • Establish departmental objectives, operating rhythms, staffing models, schedules, workload priorities, performance measures, and resource plans for day- and night-shift coverage.
  • Provide the next level of Quality escalation for significant or complex manufacturing-floor issues; direct risk assessment, containment, investigation, decision-making, communication, and escalation to site Quality leadership as required.
  • Ensure timely and compliant execution of floor oversight, in-process inspections, batch and critical-system record review, process-compliance audits, sample management, controlled-material activities, and other Line Operations responsibilities.
  • Oversee and approve deviations, investigations, CAPAs, risk assessments, nonconformances, corrective actions, and recurring-event reduction within the department’s scope; ensure actions are appropriate, sustainable, and completed on time.
  • Approve or provide governance for Quality decisions, batch-related documentation, controlled documents, procedures, protocols, qualifications, and validation activities within assigned authority.
  • Develop, coach, and evaluate direct reports; oversee hiring, onboarding, training, qualification, recognition, performance management, succession planning, and corrective action across the organization.
  • Analyze quality, compliance, service, and workforce metrics; identify trends and systemic risks; and sponsor continuous-improvement initiatives that improve reliability, efficiency, and right-first-time performance.
  • Partner with Manufacturing and cross-functional leaders to balance production priorities with independent Quality oversight and ensure issues are resolved without compromising compliance or product quality.
  • Maintain inspection readiness and support regulatory, customer, and internal inspections and audits; present departmental processes, records, decisions, and remediation plans to auditors and site leadership.
  • Develop and manage the department budget, labor plan, overtime, and other resources within approved targets.
  • Perform other quality-related duties, tasks, or projects as assigned.


What You’ll Bring

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in science, engineering, quality, manufacturing, business, or a related discipline.
  • At least 5 years of progressive experience in Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, or a related function in a regulated pharmaceutical, biologics, or medical-device environment.
  • At least 2 years of formal supervisory or people-management experience, including experience leading leaders or multiple teams, shifts, or work groups.
  • Thorough knowledge of cGMP, cGDocP, FDA requirements, applicable procedures and specifications, and quality-system expectations for regulated manufacturing.
  • Demonstrated ability to assess complex product, process, documentation, and compliance risks; make timely Quality decisions; and direct investigations, containment, corrective action, and escalation.
  • Demonstrated success managing departmental performance, staffing, priorities, employee development, and accountability through direct reports and subordinate leaders.
  • Strong leadership, coaching, communication, influencing, negotiation, collaboration, conflict-resolution, and change-management skills.
  • Strong analytical, critical-thinking, problem-solving, technical-writing, organizational, and project-management skills.
  • Experience using quality metrics and operational data to identify trends, establish priorities, manage risk, and improve performance.
  • Ability to communicate clearly with employees, peer managers, senior leaders, regulators, and auditors and to present complex Quality matters with sound rationale.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and applicable electronic quality, batch-release, training, and enterprise systems.
  • Ability to work flexible hours, provide off-shift leadership support, and work overtime or weekends as business needs require.
  • Must not be allergic to penicillin or cephalosporin drugs.
  • Must not be colorblind.
  • Near visual acuity of 20/20, with or without corrective vision.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience managing a floor-based Quality Operations organization supporting multiple manufacturing areas or shifts.
  • Experience with batch disposition support, investigations, CAPAs, internal and external audits, regulatory inspections, validation, and quality-system governance.
  • Experience managing departmental budgets, workforce plans, performance metrics, succession planning, and complex continuous-improvement initiatives.


Work Schedule and Environment

  • This position provides leadership across night shift supporting Line Operations
  • Work is performed in office and regulated manufacturing-floor environments.
  • Flexible hours, overtime, weekends, and off-shift availability may be required based on business, staffing, production, and escalation needs.

description:
Kinaxis in Canada is seeking a Staff Cloud Platform Engineer to lead the design and delivery of our cloud platform, enabling self-service deployments and robust automation. You will shape cloud reference architectures and guide teams across development and operations.

Solve complex challenges as a trusted technical lead. Drive a DevOps mindset and collaboration within the Cloud Platform Engineering Team. Develop and enhance cloud reference architectures and guide teams on implementation. Influence architectural decisions, improve CI/CD pipelines, and build secure, high-performing, resilient, and efficient cloud infrastructure. Demonstrated ability to lead complex cloud platform initiatives. Strong collaboration with development and operations teams. Experience in automation and platform tooling.

description:
Join Kindred People AB as a Senior Software Engineer where you will develop high-quality code and work on innovative solutions that meet business and technical requirements. description:

Reporting to your team manager, you will collaborate with developers, the product team and Rainbow Six Siege engineers. You will shape technical choices, improve platforms used by fans, organizers and players, and explore new tools to boost performance.

Design, develop and maintain our web platforms with a focus on application performance and reliability. Define technical choices and front-end architecture for our applications. Develop features from design through release and maintenance. Contribute to product design and maintain the quality of technical solutions. Diagnose, debug and resolve technical issues. Document technical choices and features to support maintenance. Collaborate with the product team to shape and improve our esports platforms. Explore tools and practices that could benefit the team. Experience in modern web application development. Strong skills in TypeScript, React and Next.js. Experience with micro-frontends, WebSocket and Web Components. Familiar with Node.js, npm and Vite. Able to communicate in English and collaborate with cross-functional teams.

title: Data Insights Analyst: Dashboards & SQL
description:
Triunity Software, Inc. in Ottawa, ON seeks a Data Analyst to turn complex data into actionable insights in a fast-paced tech setting. You will build dashboards, perform analyses, and collaborate across teams to deliver data-driven solutions.

The role emphasizes SQL, Python or R, and experience with Tableau/Power BI/Looker. A strong statistical foundation and communication skills are essential for presenting findings across stakeholders.

Collect, clean, and interpret large datasets to support business decision-making. Develop and maintain dashboards, reports, and data visualizations using BI tools. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify data needs and deliver analytical solutions. Perform statistical analysis and predictive modeling to uncover trends and patterns. Write and optimize SQL queries to extract and manipulate data from relational databases. Present findings and recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Monitor data quality and integrity, implementing improvements where necessary. Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, CS, or related field. Strong SQL, Python or R for data analysis. Experience with Tableau, Power BI, or Looker. Solid understanding of statistics and data modeling. Excellent problem-solving and attention to detail. Strong communication to present insights clearly. Experience in Agile or collaborative software teams is a plus. Bonus based on performance Health insurance Training & development

title: Dev Ops Senior Engineer
description:
Acuity Brands, Inc. in Cork, Ireland seeks a DevOps Architect to design, develop, and implement robust DevOps practices using Azure technologies. You’ll work with software and firmware engineers on the Q-SYS platform, supporting remote monitoring and AI-driven management.

Based in Cork, this role centers on scalable build/test infra and deployment automation. Key tasks include improving deployment workflows, staying current with DevOps trends, and coordinating releases with cross-functional

Assist in development of automated build and test infrastructure with emphasis on scalability, performance, and reliability. Improve and streamline the deployment workflow for software Dev and SQA teams. Continuous improvements to the deployment process to increase efficiency and reduce downtime. Stay up to date with emerging DevOps trends and automation technologies. Collaborate with development teams to ensure smooth integration of new features and releases. Develop and maintain documentation for deployment processes and procedures. Coordinate release decisions with the broader release team. BS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or equivalent. Automation-focused DevOps perspective. Background in Linux development workflow and tools. Background in Linux administration and deployment. Strong background in Azure cloud platform.

description:
Ookla is seeking a Site Reliability Engineer to join our Platform and SRE team. You will build, operate, and optimize a massive-scale infrastructure used by hundreds of millions of users worldwide.

You’ll focus on performance, reliability, observability, and security, while supporting a fast-moving development environment and participating in on-call rotations. Ookla emphasizes flexibility and a collaborative culture.

description:

Log, manage, and prioritize support tickets in line with service levels and customer expectations. Liaise with third-party vendors where necessary to ensure timely issue resolution. 2+ years in a customer-facing IT support or helpdesk role. Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving abilities. Experience supporting Microsoft Windows environments. Knowledge of Microsoft 365 administration. Familiarity with Active Directory and Group Policy. Experience with remote support tools and remote troubleshooting. Excellent communication and customer service skills. Ability to take ownership of issues and work towards resolution.

Demonstrated ability to remain actively involved in hands-on development. For senior lead opportunities, experience mentoring and guiding team members. Ability to balance technical leadership with individual contribution.

You will act as the Quality Point person for systems, review investigations, collaborate with other departments to close actions, and contribute to continuous improvement while maintaining safety practices.

Participate in the preparation and review of batch documentation Review and approval of deviation, CAPA’s, quality events and tasks Ensure the quality system effectively implemented and maintained Acts as Quality Point person for systems / processes providing guidance / feedback on quality issues Perform timely review of documentation / investigations / reports highlighting and assisting in the resolution of concerns commensurate with the risk Work with relevant departments to ensure timely closure of quality actions / findings Actively contribute to continuous improvement initiatives Conduct duties in a safe manner and report all safety issues or concerns Bachelor's degree in science or related field. description:

You will install, configure, test servers, storage, and networks, and work with virtualization and integration platforms to meet customer requirements.

description:
Michael Page (Canada) in Winnipeg seeks a Data Engineer to design and maintain scalable data pipelines, build data models and ensure reliable data delivery across Azure data platforms.

The successful candidate will have 5+ years of experience, strong Python/PySpark, SQL, and data integration skills, plus familiarity with Power BI and DevOps practices. This role offers collaboration with engineering and operations teams on large-scale data initiatives.

Monitor data workflows, investigate failures and resolve issues to maintain reliable data delivery. Work with technology colleagues to understand data needs and deliver fit-for-purpose solutions. Experience with Power BI or other BI tools. Familiarity with DevOps practices. CI/CD experience. Strong understanding of data pipeline engineering and big data design principles.

Success in this role is driven by strong relationship acumen, proactive customer engagement, and seamless collaboration with internal partners across Wealth, Home Lending, and Business Banking to deliver a differentiated customer experience.

Wells Fargo rewards behaviors that consistently create long term customer value and support customers in making informed financial decisions. You’ll be supported with digital tools, industry leading training, ongoing coaching, and backed by one of the most recognized brands in banking. At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Job Description

Your Role at Baxter

As a Technical Support Specialist, you will provide front-line support for Baxter's infusion systems, software applications, and connected technologies used in healthcare environments. This is where you can make an impact by helping hospitals, clinicians, biomedical technicians, and IT teams quickly resolve technical issues involving equipment that supports patient care. In this role, you'll balance technical support activities with case management and ticket processing while partnering with customers to maintain system performance and uptime.

  • Experience supporting customers via phone, email, or other service channels.

title: Principal Engineer, R&D
description:
This is where your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

You Role at Baxter


As a Principal Engineer, you will lead the design and development of critical product components from concept through production, owning technical solutions that directly impact both patient care and caregiver experience. This role offers the opportunity to take full ownership of a product subsystem, driving requirements, analytical modeling, CAD design, prototyping, testing, and optimization while collaborating across multidisciplinary teams. You will play a key role in developing innovative solutions that improve safety, ergonomics, and workflow efficiency for healthcare professionals, helping reduce caregiver strain while enhancing outcomes for the patients they serve.


What You'll Do:

  • Lead the planning and execution of complex engineering initiatives, delivering solutions that meet technical, quality, cost, and schedule objectives.
  • Drive product and system development from concept through design, analysis, prototyping, verification, and release.
  • Serve as the technical authority for critical decisions, risk assessment, and problem resolution with minimal guidance.
  • Lead cross-functional engineering efforts, ensuring alignment across stakeholders, requirements, and deliverables.
  • Translate customer, business, and regulatory needs into scalable, practical engineering solutions.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to engineers, fostering strong engineering practices and professional growth.
  • Communicate technical recommendations, tradeoffs, and project risks to engineering and business leaders.
  • Identify opportunities for innovation, continuous improvement, and technology advancement that strengthen product performance and business outcomes.

What You'll Bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or another relevant technical discipline.
  • 5+ years of engineering experience in product development, systems engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Strong foundation in engineering principles, first-principles thinking, and data-driven problem solving.
  • Proven ability to independently design, build, test, troubleshoot, and refine complex engineering solutions.
  • Demonstrated success managing multiple priorities and delivering high-quality technical results with minimal supervision.
  • Experience leading technical workstreams, projects, or small engineering teams within larger development programs.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders, challenge assumptions constructively, and mentor developing engineers.
  • Experience with numerical modeling, simulation tools, and finite element analysis (FEA) is preferred.

Baxter is committed to supporting the needs for flexibility in the workplace. We do so through our flexible workplace policy which includes a required minimum number of days a week onsite. This policy provides the benefits of connecting and collaborating in-person in support of our Mission. The flexible workplace policy is subject to local laws and legal requirements. At its discretion, Baxter may decide to adjust, suspend, or discontinue as business needs change.


We understand compensation is an important factor as you consider the next step in your career. At Baxter, we are committed to equitable pay for all employees, and we strive to be more transparent with our pay practices. The estimated base salary for this position is $112,000-$154,000 annually. The estimated range is meant to reflect an anticipated salary range for the position. We may pay more or less than of the anticipated range based upon market data and other factors, all of which are subject to change. Individual pay is based on upon location, skills and expertise, experience, and other relevant factors. This position may also be eligible for discretionary bonuses. For questions about this, our pay philosophy, and available benefits, please speak to the recruiter if you decide to apply and are selected for an interview.


Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

#LI-TV1

This is where your well-being matters. Baxter offers comprehensive compensation and benefits packages for eligible roles. Our health and well-being benefits include medical and dental coverage that start on day one, as well as insurance coverage for basic life, accident, short-term and long-term disability, and business travel accident insurance. Financial and retirement benefits include the Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), with the ability to purchase company stock at a discount, and the 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan (RSP), with options for employee contributions and company matching. We also offer Flexible Spending Accounts, educational assistance programs, and time-off benefits such as paid holidays, paid time off ranging from 20 to 35 days based on length of service, family and medical leaves of absence, and paid parental leave. Additional benefits include commuting benefits, the Employee Discount Program, the Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and childcare benefits. Join us and enjoy the competitive compensation and benefits we offer to our employees. 07

title: Clinical Project Manager - RWE FSP
description:
Job Title: Clinical Project Manager - RWE FSP

Job Location: Durham, North Carolina, United States of America

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Locations: US East Coast

Job Title: Clinical Project Manager, Real World Evidence


About the role

IQVIA is hiring a Clinical Project Manager to join our dedicated Real World Evidence (RWE) FSP team, working fully embedded within a leading pharmaceutical company. In this role, the Clinical Project Manager will lead the end-to-end delivery of real-world observational virology studies.

We are looking for an experienced study leader who can independently manage primary data collection studies, including studies incorporating patient-reported outcomes (PROs), and who brings a strong understanding of observational research across both primary and secondary data study designs.

Who you’ll work with

  • Epidemiologists, data analysts, Study Management Team, and clinical partners to deliver study-specific goals and timelines
  • Vendors to manage deliverables, timelines, and workflows
  • Operational oversight and business leads to support delivery across a portfolio of studies

What you’ll bring

  • Experience independently leading complex observational and real-world studies from planning through closeout
  • Ability to provide clear direction to global, cross-functional study teams
  • Proven ability to anticipate study risks and drive practical mitigation strategies
  • Sound judgement balancing quality, timelines, scope, and cost when making operational decisions
  • Strong communication skills across study teams, vendors, and senior leadership
  • Experience managing vendors across in-house, hybrid, and outsourced delivery models
  • Strong understanding of project financials, contractual commitments, forecasting, and change control
  • Ability to operate effectively in a matrixed, fast-paced environment

· Commitment to operational excellence and strategic client partnership

What you’ll do

  • Lead global, cross-functional observational studies and own delivery against scope, timelines, budget, and quality expectations, including large primary data collection studies requiring patient reported outcome (PRO) implementation
  • Identify and anticipate operational and quality risks, proactively escalate issues, and drive timely resolution with the Study Management Team
  • Conduct regular check-ins with Study Management Team Chair to align on study progress, priorities, risks, and emerging issues
  • Develop and maintain study management plans, timelines, risk assessments, and operational documentation
  • Ensure consistent use of study tools, training materials, and compliance with SOPs, policies, and procedures
  • Monitor study progress, financial performance, forecasting, and change control
  • Oversee vendor performance and deliverables across applicable sourcing models
  • Partner across functions to support milestone achievement, resolve issues, remove obstacles, and accelerate study delivery
  • Capture lessons learned and contribute to process improvement and best practices

Required qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in life sciences or related field
  • Minimum 4 years of experience in clinical study management, clinical operations, or clinical project management within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or CRO environment or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Demonstrated experience independently leading primary data collection observational studies from startup through closeout
  • Experience implementing patient-reported outcomes within primary data collection studies
  • Strong knowledge of observational research and RWE study execution, including the operational differences between clinical trials and observational studies
  • Experience working across both primary and secondary data real-world study designs
  • Virology experience strongly preferred
  • Knowledge of ICH GCP and relevant local laws, regulations, and guidelines applicable to clinical and observational research
  • Strong written and verbal communication, presentation, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills
  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to handle conflicting priorities
  • Ability to work effectively across geographies and cultures
  • Ability to demonstrate all IQVIA core competencies (Ownership, Innovation, Collaboration, Growth)

IQVIA is a leading global provider of clinical research services, commercial insights and healthcare intelligence to the life sciences and healthcare industries. We create intelligent connections to accelerate the development and commercialization of innovative medical treatments to help improve patient outcomes and population health worldwide. Learn more at

title: Benefits Analyst
description:
Melita is an HR, Benefits, and Payroll outsourcing company, serving and building lasting relationships with small and mid-sized employers in the U.S. and abroad. We were founded over 30 years ago on a simple principle: to help our clients succeed by innovating, serving, and supporting their Human Resources, Employee Benefits, and Payroll needs. As a results-driven organization, we hold ourselves accountable for our promises and we celebrate the successes of our clients. We live by a set of shared values that drive everything we do, and we are known for our high-integrity approach to building relationships with our clients and partners.

Position Summary:

The Benefits Analyst is a hybrid role on Melita’s Benefits Analysis (Benefits Marketing) team that combines hands-on client advisory work with the financial and underwriting analysis behind it. You are the person who both builds the numbers and explains them: projecting renewal costs, evaluating carrier proposals, modeling plan and contribution changes, benchmarking against the market, and then presenting clear, well-reasoned recommendations to small and mid-sized business clients.

This is not a sales role. It is, however, a critical position in the client relationship, so the ideal candidate pairs strong analytical ability and deep employee benefits knowledge with the interpersonal and relationship-building skills to advise decision-makers with confidence. You will report to the Director of Benefits Analysis.

Core Responsibilities:

Client Advisory and Presentation

  • Analyze and present proposals for a full range of benefit plans and options, including medical, dental, vision, disability, group life, and voluntary benefits, to small and mid-sized business clients.
  • Advise and guide clients on benefits package design and employee contribution strategy, aligning recommendations with competitive benchmarks and each company’s goals, culture, and budget.
  • Lead client renewal presentations and plan-change discussions, translating complex financial and benefits concepts into clear, actionable guidance for non-technical audiences.

Benefits Analysis and Underwriting

  • Own the analysis behind each client’s renewal: budget and renewal projections, rate development, rate-tier and contribution analysis, and plan-change modeling and pricing.
  • Benchmark plan designs, contributions, and costs against market data to support your recommendations.
  • Produce disruption, network-discount, administration-fee, and fully insured rate analyses when evaluating alternatives.
  • For level-funded and self-funded arrangements where applicable, develop claim projections and IBNR reserve estimates and interpret experience reporting.
  • Maintain clean, well-documented analytical files that another analyst can pick up and understand.

RFP and Carrier Marketing

  • Build and run RFPs to insurance carriers and general agency partners, soliciting renewal and alternative quotes for each line of coverage.
  • Review and validate the quotes that come back, then assemble the annual renewal proposal that the client decision rests on.
  • Manage relationships with carrier and GA partners to ensure Melita is well-supported, well-informed, and receiving competitive options for our clients.

Renewal-to-Open-Enrollment Handoff

  • Work closely with the internal Benefits Support team to drive timely annual renewal decisions and deliver a clean handoff, giving the support team ample time to execute a flawless Open Enrollment for every client.

Tools and Continuous Improvement

  • Work fluently in Microsoft Excel, Salesforce, and Melita’s proprietary proposal and analytical tools.
  • Contribute to file-documentation standards, process improvements, and the firm’s growing use of AI-enabled automation in analytical work.

Qualifications:

Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years in a role that involves small group benefits analysis and/or support.
  • Bachelor’s degree.
  • Active Life, Accident and Health Producer License, or the willingness and ability to obtain licensing in the relevant states within a defined onboarding period.
  • Solid grounding in benefits financial analysis: budget and claim projection, rate development, contribution analysis, and disruption and discount analysis.
  • Strong proficiency with Microsoft Excel and comfort working in a CRM (Salesforce) and AI-enabled workflows.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships with client decision-makers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a brokerage or consulting environment supporting small and mid-sized groups.
  • Hands-on experience across fully insured and level-funded (and ideally self-funded) programs.
  • Established relationships with carriers and general agency partners.
  • Familiarity with ancillary and voluntary benefit product lines.
  • Experience leading, mentoring, or coordinating the work of others, including offshore staff.

title: Compliance Data & Reporting Analyst
description:
Quick Summary

You’ll build the reports Kin sends regulators, hunt down data breaks, and keep compliance reporting reliable as we scale into new states. SQL required.

Who we are

Kin makes life simpler, more affordable, and better for homeowners — especially in the places where climate risks, rising costs, and outdated systems make it hardest. We start with smarter homeowners insurance and expand to everything homeowners need to thrive.

Using data, technology, and thoughtful human support, we’re building products that are clear, fair, and help homeowners feel confident — so homeowners aren’t left behind when they need help most.

Founded in 2016, Kin is a remote-first employer with Kinfolk across more than 35 states. We serve customers in 14 states (and counting). Our disciplined growth, strong customer satisfaction, and focus on long-term sustainability fosters outstanding growth, attracts marquee investors, and earns recognition and accolades, including:

  • Built In Chicago’s Best Places to Work, Midsize Companies (2021-2026)

  • Forbes’ America’s Best Startup Employers (2026)

  • Inc. 5000 Fastest-Growing Private Companies

  • Forbes’ Fintech 50 (2023-2026)

  • Great Places to Work Certified (2024-2026)

Most importantly, we’re building Kin to be a place where people do meaningful work with real impact — for our customers, our communities, and each other. We’re excited to tell you more about how you can contribute to our rapid growth, strong unit economics, profitability, and excellent customer ratings. To learn more about how we work and what we’re building, visit kin.com and see how we work.

The opportunity

We’re looking for a Compliance Reporting & Data Analyst to help us build the reporting muscle Kin needs as we scale. As we expand into new states and roll out new products, our regulatory, financial, and audit reporting obligations grow in both volume and complexity — and the stakes for getting them right grow with them.

This is a newly created role, added as we expand our Compliance Reporting & Data function to keep pace with that growth. Reporting to the Compliance Reporting & Data Lead, you’ll partner across Compliance, Finance, Product, and Data Engineering to make sure the numbers we send to regulators, auditors, and finance leaders are accurate, complete, and defensible. Your work will directly protect Kin’s ability to operate in every state we serve today — and every state we’re preparing to enter next.

Your responsibilities

  • Translate regulatory and financial reporting requirements into report logic and data definitions, in partnership with the Compliance Reporting & Data Lead

  • Develop, maintain, and update regulatory and compliance reports for state filings, market conduct exams, audits, and other reporting obligations

  • Validate data used in compliance submissions against agreed checks, document the procedure and results, and escalate exceptions for resolution

  • Own reporting readiness for new products and state launches, including post-launch data validation

  • Investigate reporting discrepancies and data anomalies, isolate root causes, and drive remediation with Data Engineering, Finance, and Product

  • Write and execute validation tests that confirm data pipelines produce reporting-accurate output, and close gaps with Data Engineering before reporting depends on them

  • Build and maintain automated reporting processes, data-quality checks, reconciliations, and alerts, and propose additional checks where recurring exceptions surface

  • Create and maintain clear documentation of report logic, data definitions, controls, validation procedures, and reporting processes to keep Kin audit-ready

  • Produce and reconcile the data feeds Finance relies on for month-end close, and resolve variances identified during reconciliations

  • Research data and assemble supporting documentation for responses to regulators, auditors, and internal stakeholders, and recommend process, control, and automation improvements to the Compliance Reporting & Data Lead

Success in this role

In your first 6–12 months at Kin, success is less about checking boxes and more about the impact you create. You’ll use your skills and judgment to take ownership of meaningful work, improve how we operate, and help move Kin’s mission forward. Along the way, you’ll deliver outcomes that make a real difference for both Kinfolk and the homeowners we serve.

By the end of your first year, you should feel confident in your role, trusted as an owner, and proud of the progress you’ve helped make.

  • Regulatory filings, market conduct exam responses, and audit requests go out on time, accurately, and backed by documentation an examiner can follow without a call.

  • New product launches and state expansions have clear compliance reporting requirements, with validated data feeds and documented controls.

  • Recurring reporting exceptions have dropped meaningfully as automated data-quality checks and alerts catch issues before they reach a filing

  • There is clear documentation in place for the reports you are responsible for, including step-by-step instructions.

What you’ll bring

  • 2+ years of experience in data analysis, compliance reporting, insurance regulatory reporting, financial reporting, audit, or a similar analytical role

  • Working proficiency in SQL, including joins, aggregation, and queries that test for completeness, duplicates, and reconciliation breaks

  • Experience translating business and regulatory reporting requirements into structured data needs

  • A track record of investigating data discrepancies, isolating root causes, and driving remediation to completion

  • Precise, detail-oriented working style with well-organized documentation that a colleague can pick up and follow without a walkthrough

  • Ability to manage multiple recurring reporting deadlines without sacrificing accuracy

  • Clear written and verbal communication with both technical partners (Data Engineering) and non-technical partners (Compliance, Finance)

Bonus if you have

  • Experience working in the P&C insurance industry

  • Familiarity with Looker or a comparable BI tool

  • Familiarity with data pipeline and data-platform tools such as Databricks, Airflow, or AWS tools

  • Experience with JIRA or similar work-management tools

  • Accounting, finance, or audit experience

  • Experience developing automated data-quality checks, reconciliations, or reporting processes

How we hire

We believe a great hiring experience should be clear, respectful, and human. We will accept applications for this position until November 24, 2026. While our recruiting team uses AI tools for efficiency, resumes are still screened by Kin’s in-house recruiters, and candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are made by recruiters and hiring teams. Rest assured, real people make real decisions.

The hiring process and timeline for each role will vary, depending on the position. However, here are some things you can expect from us:

  • Prompt updates and feedback following interviews

  • Interviews with recruiters, hiring managers, and members of teams

  • Skills assessment relevant to the position, if applicable

  • Genuine, thoughtful human interaction at every step

How we support you

We offer a comprehensive, competitive benefits program, allowing you to choose the benefits that are best for you and your family, starting on the first day of the month following your start date.

Core Benefits

  • Competitive salary and company equity through Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), granted as part of our standard compensation package and based on role and level

  • 401(k) with company match up to 4% of eligible earnings

  • Multiple medical plan options, plus dental and vision coverage

  • Company-funded HSA contributions (based on medical plan selection)

  • Company-paid life insurance and short-term disability

Health & Wellbeing

  • A variety of supplemental benefit options, including long-term disability, critical illness, accident, legal, and pet insurance

  • Access to mental health support and confidential counseling resources

  • Flexible PTO for exempt employees (most employees take 15–20 days per year), plus 8 company-observed holidays

  • Paid parental leave, including up to 14 weeks at 100% pay for birthing parents and 8 weeks at 100% pay for non-birthing parents

Growth & Development

  • Career mobility and internal growth opportunities across the organization

  • Professional development budgets for certifications, conferences, and learning available, subject to management approval

How we work

We don’t just hire for skills. We hire for alignment. Kinfolk bring diverse perspectives, but we’re united by a shared set of values that shape how we work and how we show up for each other and our customers.

Run through walls, together – Every one of us is responsible for creating the culture we want to work in. High performance. Low drama. Always respectful. We assume the best in each other and challenge ideas, not intentions. We show up, work hard, and play to each other’s strengths — because that’s how great teams win.

Raise the bar. Drop the ego – Attitudes are contagious. Every one of us is responsible for creating the culture we want to work in. High performance. Low drama. Always respectful. Like professional sports teams, we win by working in sync. We show up, work hard, and play to each other’s strengths.

Act like an owner – We are owners, fully accountable for achieving Kin’s mission. That requires positive, proactive, big-picture thinking well beyond our job descriptions. Ask questions, Take ownership. Do the right thing, even when it‘s hard. Because when Kin thrives, so do you. And so do our customers.

Operate lean. Deliver more – We build efficiency into everything we do. Each dollar we save gets reinvested to deliver more to our customers: better pricing, more products, and new innovations. We work smarter by relentlessly prioritizing and using technology, including AI, to multiply our impact. Lean is about focus, not deprivation. Lean isn’t a limitation — it’s our competitive advantage.

Keep asking ‘What if?’ – We value curiosity. To make insurance better for our customers, we experiment. We embrace insights. And we base decisions on data rather than assumptions. We see setbacks as opportunities for growth and are always learning and improving. Both individually and as a company.

Where we work

We are a remote-first company with offices in Chicago, IL and St. Petersburg, FL where teams can come together for collaboration.

For Sales Agents and Customer Service Agents: These roles sit in any of the following 32 states: AL, AZ, CO, FL, ID, IL, IN, KS, KY, LA, MA, MD, ME, MI, MO, MT, NC, NE, NM, NV, NY, OH, OK, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VT, VA, WA, and WI.

For all other positions, these roles can sit in any of the following 41 states: AL, AR, AZ, CA (exempt only), CO, CT, FL, GA, ID, IL, IN, IA, KS, KY, LA, MA, ME, MD, MI, MN, MO, MT, NC, NE, NJ, NM, NV, NY, OH, OK, OR, PA, SC, SD, TN, TX, UT, VT, VA, WA, and WI. Please only apply if you are able to live and work full-time in one of the states listed above.

For remote technical positions located in Canada, we are only able to hire individuals who reside in Ontario. Applicants must be able to live and work full-time in Ontario to be considered.

State locations and specifics are subject to change as our hiring requirements shift.

title: Senior Incident Response Analyst
description:
About OpenLoop

OpenLoop was co-founded by CEO, Dr. Jon Lensing, and COO, Christian Williams, with the vision to bring care anywhere. Our telehealth support solutions are thoughtfully designed to streamline and simplify go-to-market care delivery for companies offering meaningful virtual support to patients across an expansive array of specialties, in all 50 states.

About the Role

OpenLoop’s mission is to bring care anywhere by powering telehealth solutions at scale. Our Security Operations team protects the clinical and operational systems that OpenLoop and our partners run patient care on. As a Senior Incident Response Analyst, you’ll be a dedicated responder on our DFIR function — owning incidents end to end, deepening our forensic capability, and making sure containment happens fast when PHI and clinical operations are on the line.

What You’ll Do

  • Own tier-1 and tier-2 incidents end to end: detection validation, triage, scoping, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review.

  • Run host, memory, network, cloud, and identity forensic investigations independently, with evidence handling that holds up to legal, regulatory, and client scrutiny.

  • Investigate from EDR and SIEM telemetry — write and refine queries, build correlation logic, and reconstruct incident timelines from log data.

  • Share the IR on-call rotation with the Lead Incident Responder and Senior Staff Security Analyst, and exercise named containment authority (host isolation, session revocation) within a defined threshold.

  • Author and rewrite IR playbooks based on incidents you personally work, and run post-incident reviews with findings tracked to closure.

  • Automate or AI-assist repetitive triage and evidence-collection steps so the team’s time goes to investigation rather than toil.

  • Write for two audiences — a defensible technical timeline and an executive summary of the same incident.

Who You Are

You’re a hands-on responder who has led real incidents under real ambiguity, and you’re straight about what you got wrong. We hire for the discipline, not the tool SKU or the credential: no specific degree is required, and strong responders from Defender, SentinelOne, Splunk, or Sentinel environments are fully in scope. This is an individual contributor role.

Required Qualifications

  • 6–8 years of hands-on security experience, with the majority in incident response and/or digital forensics.

  • Demonstrated ownership of the full incident lifecycle, from detection validation through post-incident review.

  • Digital forensics breadth across host/disk, memory, network, cloud, and identity — from real casework, not coursework.

  • Working depth in EDR/EPP: investigating from endpoint telemetry, running response actions, and tuning what the tool surfaces.

  • Working depth in SIEM: query authoring, correlation logic, and timeline reconstruction from log data.

  • Hands-on fluency with a forensic toolchain (e.g., Velociraptor, KAPE, Volatility, Autopsy/EnCase/FTK/X-Ways, plaso, Zeek, Wireshark).

  • Evidence handling discipline — chain of custody, sound acquisition, and documentation that survives legal, regulatory, and client scrutiny.

  • MITRE ATT&CK fluency applied to real investigations.

  • Scripting for investigation and automation (Python, PowerShell, or similar).

  • Demonstrated, hands-on use of AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, or equivalent) in security work, with specific examples of their impact on speed or quality — and sound judgment about AI and sensitive data (PHI, credentials, telemetry).

  • Clear incident writing: able to produce both a technical timeline and an executive summary of the same incident.

  • Willingness to participate in a shared IR on-call rotation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • CrowdStrike Falcon EDR — hands-on investigation and response in the console.

  • CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM — CQL query authoring, correlation rules, and dashboards.

  • CrowdStrike Falcon Shield — SaaS app, identity, and third-party integration risk.

  • Cloud incident response in AWS (CloudTrail, GuardDuty, IAM abuse patterns).

  • Identity-centric investigation, particularly Okta (session hijacking, MFA fatigue, token theft, SSO abuse).

  • Healthcare, fintech, or other regulated-industry experience with sensitive data.

  • HIPAA, HITRUST, or SOC 2 from the operator side, including breach determination workflow.

  • GCFA, GCFE, GCIH, GNFA, GCIA, GREM, or equivalent demonstrated expertise.

  • Malware triage and reverse engineering fundamentals.

  • SOAR / automation platform experience, or AI-assisted IR workflows built on LLM APIs.

  • Multi-entity or M&A environment experience — we operate across several subsidiaries.

  • Open-source contributions to DFIR or security tooling; CTF history, conference talks, or other community engagement.

  • Experience maturing an IR program from a lower baseline.

  • Threat intelligence consumption applied to active investigations.

What Success Looks Like

  • In your first 6 months: fully onboarded and taking primary responder duty on a defined rotation, independently owning tier-1 and tier-2 incidents without escalation for routine cases.

  • Forensic capability is genuinely two-deep — you can run a host, memory, cloud, or identity investigation without the Lead Incident Responder in the room.

  • At least three IR playbooks rewritten or newly authored from incidents you worked, with post-incident reviews running on a consistent cadence and findings tracked to closure.

  • In your first 12 months: measurable reduction in MTTD and MTTR against baseline, with repetitive triage and evidence collection automated or AI-assisted rather than manual.

Our Benefits

In addition, for salaried positions you would also be eligible for:

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision plans

  • Flexible Spending/Health Savings Accounts

  • Flexible PTO

  • 401(k) + Company Match

  • Life Insurance, Pet insurance, and more

Our Company

We have a relatively flat organizational structure here at OpenLoop. Everyone is encouraged to bring ideas to the table and make things happen. This fits in well with our core values of Autonomy, Competence and Belonging, as we want everyone to feel empowered and supported to do their best work.

Sound like a good fit? We’d love to meet you.

title: Assistant Manager- Access Management
description:
Job Title: Assistant Manager | Access Management

Job Location: Bangalore, India

About Unilever:


Be part of the world’s most successful, purpose-led business. Work with brands that are well-loved around the world, that improve the lives of our consumers and the communities around us. We promote innovation, big and small, to make our business win and grow; and we believe in business as a force for good. Unleash your curiosity, challenge ideas and disrupt processes; use your energy to make this happen. Our brilliant business leaders and colleagues provide mentorship and inspiration, so you can be at your best. Every day, nine out of ten Indian households use our products to feel good, look good and get more out of life – giving us a unique opportunity to build a brighter future.

Every individual here can bring their purpose to life through their work. Join us and you’ll be surrounded by inspiring leaders and supportive peers. Among them, you’ll channel your purpose, bring fresh ideas to the table, and simply be you. As you work to make a real impact on the business and the world, we’ll work to help you become a better you.


PURPOSE OF THE ROLE


The Access Management product team delivers the privileged access controls that protect Unilever’s most critical technology platforms, identities and business services. The PAM capability enables secure, governed and auditable access for administrators, engineers, suppliers, service accounts and other privileged identities across on-premises, cloud and SaaS environments.

As the Privileged Access Management Product SME, you will be part of internal technical authority for PAM. You will oversee the design, engineering, integration, support and operational health of CyberArk, Beyond Trust and Cloud console capabilities, while shaping and leading the technical delivery of Unilever’s PAM modernization programme. The role requires strong hands-on expertise, strategic thinking and the ability to translate emerging security capabilities into scalable, resilient and user-centered services. Additionally, you will strive to continuously improve our services, ensuring they meet the evolving needs of our users and customers, and provide robust support to maintain secure, efficient and frictionless access.


WHAT WILL YOUR MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES BE


  • Serve as the internal technical authority for Privileged Access Management, including CyberArk, BeyondTrust and associated identity, directory, endpoint, cloud and security integrations.
  • evolve the PAM technical strategy, target architecture, standards and roadmap, aligned to Zero Trust, least privilege, identity-first security and Unilever technology strategy.
  • Lead the technical workstreams of the PAM modernization programme, including discovery, platform rationalization, migration planning, solution design, proof of concept, implementation and transition to operations.
  • Design secure, scalable and resilient solutions for credential vaulting, password rotation, privileged session management, remote privileged access, endpoint privilege management, secrets management and just-in-time access.
  • Define onboarding patterns for human, service, application, machine and cloud privileged identities, ensuring appropriate controls, approvals, ownership, monitoring and lifecycle governance.
  • Provide clear technical direction and oversight to strategic suppliers and delivery partners; assure designs, engineering practices, operational procedures and contracted outcomes against Unilever standards.
  • Act as the escalation point for complex PAM incidents and problems, leading advanced troubleshooting, root cause analysis, service restoration and permanent remediation across integrated platforms.
  • Improve 24x7 operational readiness through effective monitoring, alerting, capacity management, disaster recovery, resilience testing, patching, vulnerability management and service continuity controls.
  • Partner with IAM, Active Directory, Entra ID, cloud, endpoint, SOC, application, infrastructure and risk teams to embed PAM controls across hybrid and multi-cloud technology environments.
  • Establish measurable technical and service outcomes, including privileged account coverage, credential rotation compliance, session control adoption, onboarding throughput, platform health and reduction of standing privilege.
  • Support audits, control testing, risk assessments and remediation, ensuring evidence is accurate, repeatable and traceable and that suppliers remain accountable for agreed actions.
  • Monitor market and technology developments, evaluate new PAM and identity security capabilities, and recommend forward-looking improvements such as identity threat detection, password less administration, workload identity protection and policy-driven automation.
  • Coach engineers and operational teams, create reusable engineering patterns and documentation, and build sustainable internal capability for PAM design and support.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS


Necessary experience


  • 5-7+ years of hands-on experience in PAM, IAM, cyber security engineering or a related technical role within a large, complex and regulated enterprise.
  • Demonstrable engineering and operational experience with CyberArk PAM and strong working knowledge of BeyondTrust capabilities; experience across both platforms is highly desirable.
  • Proven delivery of PAM transformation or modernisation initiatives, including current-state assessment, target-state design, migration, platform consolidation and adoption planning.
  • Experience designing and operating highly available PAM services across global, hybrid and multi-cloud environments, including disaster recovery and cyber recovery considerations.
  • Deep understanding of privileged account discovery, vaulting, rotation, Just In Time, Zero Standing Privilege, session isolation and recording, remote access, endpoint privilege management, secrets management and non-human identity controls.
  • Experience integrating PAM with Active Directory, Entra ID, GCP, MFA, ITSM, SIEM/SOC, cloud platforms, databases, network devices, applications.
  • Advanced troubleshooting capability across complex identity, network, authentication, certificate, API and platform dependencies, with experience providing L3/L4 engineering support.
  • Experience governing third-party service providers, assuring technical designs and procedures, managing escalations and driving measurable service improvement.
  • Strong knowledge of cyber security risk, audit and control frameworks, with the ability to convert requirements into practical engineering standards and evidence.

Qualifications and desirable certifications
