However, we encourage candidates who may fall outside of this range to apply as well.


About the role

We are seeking an experienced development leader to manage the team responsible for designing, delivering, and operating the platforms that enable Intact’s GenAI strategy.


This role will lead the engineering and operational evolution of platforms such as Agentic AI Platform, which enables teams to build, govern, and run trustworthy AI agents at scale and IntactGPT, Intact’s secure conversational-AI workspace.


This role is accountable for enabling engineering teams to move quickly while maintaining strong controls for security, compliance, cost efficiency, and operational stability.

The successful candidate will combine strong people leadership, product management capability, engineering and operations experience to in a large, complex, and highly regulated insurance environment.


What you’ll do here:


Lead and develop a high-performing engineering team

  • Lead, mentor, and develop a team of engineers responsible for GenAI platforms and shared services.
  • Foster a culture of ownership, accountability, innovation, operational discipline, and continuous improvement.
  • Establish clear engineering practices, delivery expectations, and operational responsibilities.
  • Promote knowledge sharing, documentation, and the development of reusable patterns and standards.

Own GenAI platform architecture, delivery and operations

  • Be accountable for outcomes including reliability, cost, security, engineering velocity, and customer experience—not simply the completion of individual tasks or tickets.
  • Establish effective monitoring, alerting, capacity planning, incident response, problem management, and disaster recovery practices.
  • Lead platform lifecycle management, upgrades, vulnerability remediation, and technology modernization.
  • Ensure support models and operational readiness evolve as GenAI adoption expands.

Establish a product-oriented platform strategy

  • Translate enterprise needs into platform capabilities, reusable services, engineering standards, and prioritized delivery plans.
  • Develop and socialize the roadmap across a complex enterprise organization; build alignment among diverse stakeholder groups.
  • Track and communicate product value through measures such as adoption, time to production, DevX, delivery velocity, reliability, risk reduction, and cost efficiency.
  • Use customer feedback, operational data, and adoption insights to continuously improve the platform experience.

Enable secure, compliant, and responsible AI adoption

  • Embed cybersecurity, privacy, regulatory, and governance controls directly into the platforms so that compliance acts as a guardrail rather than a delivery bottleneck.
  • Partner with cybersecurity, privacy, risk, legal, compliance, audit, and architecture teams to ensure GenAI platforms align with enterprise policies and applicable Canadian regulatory expectations.

Manage financial, vendor, and service performance

  • Own or contribute to the operating and capital budget for GenAI platforms, cloud services, software, tooling, and related infrastructure.
  • Establish cost-management practices for model usage, platform consumption, cloud infrastructure, licensing, and third-party services.
  • Define, document, and report operational KPIs, SLAs, service health, adoption, customer experience, risk, and financial metrics.
  • Provide clear reporting to senior technology leaders and other stakeholders as required.

Navigate a complex enterprise environment

  • Build effective relationships across technology, architecture, infrastructure, cybersecurity, data, privacy, legal, risk, audit, finance and procurement.
  • Communicate complex technical, regulatory, and risk considerations clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Facilitate decisions and resolve competing priorities across multiple stakeholder groups.
  • Act as a trusted advisor to engineering teams adopting GenAI capabilities.

Core principles of the team you’ll be joining

The successful candidate will help establish and reinforce the following ways of working:

  • Engineer for the customer journey - Design every solution with the end-to-end software delivery lifecycle in mind, including onboarding, development, testing, deployment, operations, support, and retirement.
  • Automate everything, expose everything - Build API-accessible services and enable self-service consumption. Provisioning and operations should be code-driven, repeatable, and observable.
  • Compliance is a guardrail, not a gate - Encode security, privacy, and governance into the platforms so teams can move quickly without trading off safety or regulatory obligations.
  • Optimize for scale, not the exception - Design for broad enterprise adoption, efficient consumption, and sustainable operations. Prioritize simple, reusable patterns over one-off solutions.
  • Own the outcome, not the ticket - Be accountable for reliability, cost, security, engineering velocity, adoption, and customer experience—not only task completion.

What you bring to the table:


  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, information technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.
  • Experience operating cloud-based platforms and enterprise technology services.
  • Strong understanding of software development lifecycle practices, DevOps, CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, APIs, observability, automation, and platform engineering.
  • Knowledge of cybersecurity principles, including identity and access management, data protection, threat modelling, vulnerability management, secure design, and security operations.
  • Understanding of responsible AI, model risk, privacy, data governance, and regulatory controls.
  • Understanding of responsible AI, privacy, data governance, and regulatory controls.
  • Understanding of GenAI concepts, LLMs, AI agents, model gateways, RAG, or related technologies; experience with Azure Foundry, AWS Bedrock, GCP Gemini is an asset
  • Experience working within Canadian regulatory, privacy, risk, or compliance requirements; experience in financial services or insurance is an asset.
  • Demonstrated product management capabilities
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English; French is an asset - For candidates located in Quebec, bilingualism is required considering the necessity to interact on a regular basis with English-speaking colleagues across the country.
  • Demonstrated ability to build trust and influence across a large, matrixed organization.
  • Ability to participate in or support urgent production incidents and critical escalations outside normal business hours when required.
  • No Canadian work experience required however must be eligible to work in Canada.

How success will be measured:


  • Increased adoption and effective use of Intact’s GenAI platforms.
  • Faster delivery of secure GenAI-enabled solutions into production.
  • Improved developer and engineering team experience.
  • Strong platform availability, reliability, observability, and operational readiness.
  • Demonstrable security, privacy, governance, and regulatory compliance.
  • Effective management of model, cloud, infrastructure, and vendor costs.
  • Reduction in shadow AI and unmanaged technology adoption.
  • Reusable, API-accessible, automated platform capabilities.
  • Clear value realization and measurable business outcomes.

title: Senior Product Analyst
description:

Monarch is a powerful, all-in-one personal finance platform designed to help make the complexity of finances feel simple again. Since launching in 2021, we’ve become the top-recommended personal finance app by users and experts. Our goal? To take the stress out of finances so our members can focus on what truly matters.

We are a team of do-ers led by experienced entrepreneurs who are passionate about helping our members reach their financial goals. We’re hyper focused on building a product people love, and on finding every edge that helps us do that better. AI is core to how we operate: every person on the team uses it as a partner to sharpen judgment, move faster, and expand what’s possible. We’re not looking for tool mastery, we’re looking for fluency and curiosity. What matters is that AI is part of how you work today and that you’re actively raising your own bar on how to use it well.

As a fully remote company (even before COVID!), we welcome applicants from almost anywhere. Our team collaborates synchronously mostly from 9 AM – 2 PM PT and embraces asynchronous work to stay connected across time zones.

Join us on our mission to transform lives by simplifying money, together.

The Role:

Monarch is looking for a senior product analyst to join our data team. In this role, you’ll own how we measure the product and how we learn from it by setting the bar for experimental rigor, investigating user behavior to find what actually drives conversion and retention, and running our experimentation loop end to end. You will partner closely with peers on the data team and work with growth, product, and engineering teams, playing a crucial role in enabling us to make data-driven decisions.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own A/B test design and analysis and partner with product managers on conclusions and recommendations

  • Partner with the growth team across the full experimentation loop from generating and prioritizing ideas, sizing the opportunity, designing and analyzing the experiment, and folding learnings into the next round

  • Analyze user behavior and dive into anomalies to understand changes in the business

  • Partner with product and engineering teams on upcoming feature launches, defining the measurement approach and success metrics, and ensuring tracking events are in place

  • Provide data and insight into business decisions and share results with broader company and leadership team

  • Automate recurring workflows without sacrificing insight quality

  • Build new datasets and pipelines while also helping to maintain/update our existing data infrastructure

What You’ll Bring:

  • At least 4 years in a product analyst (or similar) role, preferably at a growth stage company

  • Advanced knowledge of statistical methodologies for A/B testing including designing experiments and analyzing their results

  • You are naturally curious and comfortable with ambiguity. You think through the tradeoffs of speed and accuracy and can make recommendations on the best approach to solving a problem

  • You can work with both technical and non-technical partners and translate requirements into actionable steps. You can comfortably explain technical topics and roadblocks to non-technical partners.

  • Expert level SQL – you are comfortable not just with selecting data but with creating new tables, advanced features like window functions, and writing clear and succinct code

  • Experience across a modern analytics stack. We use Amplitude and Statsig for product & experimentation and Snowflake, DBT, Hex, and Omni for BI.

  • AI fluency – you are actively pushing the boundaries of AI and know when to use it and when it might introduce errors

Nice to Haves:

  • Experience in consumer subscription analytics

  • Experience in an early stage, high growth startup

  • Competitive cash and equity compensation in a hyper growth, early stage company .

title: Cost Analyst- NASA Missions- Remote (Spacecraft Exp. Desired)
description:
CTS seeks a Cost Analyst Subject Matter Expert to provide technical expertise to the Evaluations, Assessments, Studies, Services, and Support (EASSS) contract. This contract supports NASA Headquarters Science Mission Directorate (SMD) and facilitates NASA’s pursuit of the most noteworthy approaches for missions, payloads, spacecraft, instruments, and research that help answer the big questions in Earth and Space science. Located at LaRC, the NASA’s Science Office for Mission Assessments (SOMA) helps SMD select and manage missions, spacecraft, and instruments. To accomplish this, SOMA manages and provides oversight of evaluations, assessments, and studies for SMD and other NASA organizations. These include evaluation of proposals received in response to NASA Announcements of Opportunity, NASA Research Announcements, Cooperative Agreement Notices, and Broad Agency Announcements, as well as highly specialized studies and assessments, such as life cycle and independent cost estimates, schedule assessments, and risk analyses. CTS supports SOMA via the EASSS contract by providing subject matter experts who will apply their expertise to complex proposal evaluations, management and technical assessments, and advanced studies through the EASSS contract.

CTS’s subject matter experts need not be local to the program office near NASA Langley Research Center in Hampton, VA. We seek individuals who bring significant Technical, Management and Cost expertise in missions, payloads, spacecraft and instruments relevant to NASA’s mission. The work is performed remotely with less than 10% travel occurring periodically for some during the assignment to bring the geographically distributed teams together for workshops to finalize results.

The Cost Analyst must have at least five (5) years of experience in estimating and analyzing space mission cost utilizing parametric models. Must be proficient in the use of aerospace industry standard cost analysis tools. Many cost estimating models exist, as is the case with the estimating methodologies, no single cost model can be used for all purposes. Estimating models can vary significantly in terms of data availability and automation. The knowledge of some of the following tools is greatly desired:


  • SEER (especially SEER-H)
  • Trueplanning
  • Project Cost Estimating Capability (PCEC)
  • NASA Air Force Cost Model (NAFCOM)
  • NASA Instrument Cost Model (NICM)
  • Technology Cost & Schedule Estimation (TCASE)
  • Schedule Management & Relationship Tool (SMART)
  • Phasing Model
  • One NASA Cost Engineering (ONCE) database
  • REDSTAR database
  • Polaris
  • Argo
  • Automated Cost Estimating Integrated Tools (ACEIT)
  • CO$TAT
  • Joint Analysis of Cost and Schedule (JACS)
  • PRICE cost models

Education: Must have a Bachelor’s Degree in Mathematics, Finance, Engineering, or other directly related field.

We thank you for your time and consideration of our current opening. If you choose to apply please be sure to upload your most recent and detailed resume for our review.

CTS is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate in our hiring or employment practices regardless of employment type.

title: Security Analyst – Tier 3 (West Coast)
description:
About 7AI

7AI is the foundational AI security company. Founded in 2024 by Cybereason co-founders Lior Div and Yonatan Striem-Amit, we came out of stealth in February 2025 to take on the non-human work of the SOC. Our platform pairs a federated SIEM with AI agents that detect, investigate, respond, and hunt, plus dedicated threat hunting and threat intelligence, with humans on the loop.

Backed by $166 million in total funding from investors including Index Ventures and Blackstone, we’re building the AI foundation for security operations in the agentic era, and we’re still early. That’s the appeal: you’ll join at a pivotal stage where your work shapes what 7AI becomes, alongside security veterans who’ve built this before. Our culture runs on respect, collaboration, and a shared bar for excellence, all pointed at one goal, delivering real outcomes for the customers who trust us to defend them.

Overview

7AI’s AI agents take on a lot of the SOC’s non-human work, but scaling that trust requires senior analysts who can validate the hardest cases and mentor the team doing it. As a Tier 3 Security Analyst, you’ll be the technical lead and escalation point for junior analysts reviewing 7AI’s AI agent investigations. You’ll validate the agents’ work, prove out the threats they stopped, and help customers understand the risk that was prevented. You’ll also hunt for malicious activity in customer environments using 7AI’s agents, and help build the processes that let this team scale without losing quality.

What You’ll Do

  • Review and validate the AI agents’ investigations for accuracy and completeness, assessing risk

  • Serve as the technical escalation point for junior analysts and mentor them

  • Correlate data across cloud, endpoint, identity, and network sources to build the full picture of an attack

  • Investigate malicious activity the AI agents responded to, and assess the risk that was prevented for customers

  • Use 7AI’s AI agents to hunt for emerging threats in customer environments, feeding new detections back into the product

  • Support customers with ongoing threat monitoring, triage, and alert prioritization, especially during active incidents

  • Proactively review logs and findings to catch potential threats and anomalies early

  • Communicate clearly with customers across technical levels, from SOC analysts to CISOs

  • Help design processes that let the team scale while keeping quality consistent

  • Work with Sales, Engineering, and Product to share customer feedback and help tune the platform

  • Stay current on emerging attack techniques and trends, including AI-driven attacks

What We’re Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience in security operations

  • Hands-on experience investigating alerts across endpoint, network, identity, email, and cloud sources

  • Strong understanding of security monitoring tools such as XDR, SIEM, IDS/IPS, and IDP

  • Familiarity with log and telemetry concepts

  • Strong knowledge of common attack techniques and frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, and incident triage methodologies

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to verify AI-driven analysis and make independent security decisions

  • Data querying experience with SIEM query languages such as SPL, KQL, FQL, or SQL

  • Strong knowledge of malware analysis methods

  • Strong interpersonal skills and a service-oriented mindset

  • A track record of collaborating well on a team, including mentoring others and teaching complex concepts

Nice to Have

  • Experience in a managed services environment

  • Incident handling experience

  • Relevant certifications such as Security+, GSEC, or GCIH

Executive Partner, CFO Advisory


About Gartner

Gartner is the world's leading research and advisory company, helping business leaders across every major industry make faster, smarter decisions and achieve their most critical priorities. Gartner's CFO & Finance Executive Programs provide finance leaders with objective insight, expert guidance, and a powerful peer network to accelerate business performance and transformation.


About the Role

Gartner is seeking accomplished current and former Chief Financial Officers from publicly traded organizations with at least $1 billion in annual revenue to join our CFO Executive Partner team.

As an Executive Partner, you will serve as a trusted advisor to a portfolio of CFOs and senior finance executives, helping them navigate complex business challenges, advance strategic priorities, and improve organizational performance. Leveraging your executive leadership experience, you will engage as a peer counselor, coach, and thought partner while helping clients maximize the value of Gartner's research, insights, and advisory resources.

This role provides a unique opportunity to remain engaged with senior business leaders, influence the future of the finance function, and share your expertise across multiple industries while enjoying the flexibility of a fully remote position.


What You'll Do

Trusted Advisor to CFOs

  • Serve as a strategic advisor to a portfolio of senior finance executives and CFOs.
  • Conduct regular executive consultations focused on leadership effectiveness, organizational transformation, financial performance, and strategic execution.
  • Help CFOs identify priorities, evaluate challenges, and develop practical action plans to achieve business outcomes.
  • Share insights, best practices, and lessons learned from your own executive leadership experience.

Executive Engagement & Thought Leadership

  • Facilitate executive workshops, peer discussions, and leadership sessions for CFO members.
  • Lead discussions and executive roundtables at Gartner conferences and client events.
  • Foster executive networking and knowledge sharing among senior finance leaders.
  • Contribute to the development and delivery of CFO-focused thought leadership and research initiatives.

Client Success & Business Growth

  • Partner closely with Gartner sales, service, and research teams to deliver exceptional client value.
  • Participate in account planning, renewal discussions, and prospective member conversations.
  • Help organizations understand how Gartner's research and advisory capabilities can accelerate business outcomes.
  • Support member retention by building trusted, long-term executive relationships.

Ideal Background

Successful candidates will bring:

  • Current or former Chief Financial Officer experience within a publicly traded company generating at least $1 billion in annual revenue.
  • Demonstrated success leading enterprise finance organizations through growth, transformation, restructuring, digital modernization, M&A activity, capital allocation decisions, or operational performance improvement.
  • Experience engaging Boards of Directors, Audit Committees, investors, analysts, and external stakeholders.
  • Broad expertise across core finance disciplines, including financial planning and analysis, accounting, treasury, investor relations, capital markets, risk management, and finance technology.
  • A proven ability to influence senior executives and drive enterprise-wide outcomes.

Highly Valued Qualifications

  • Fortune 500 leadership experience.
  • Multi-industry or multinational operating experience.
  • Public company governance and SEC reporting expertise.
  • Experience leading large-scale organizational transformation initiatives.
  • Prior consulting, advisory, board, executive coaching, or mentoring experience.

Location & Travel

  • Fully remote position.
  • Candidates may reside anywhere within the continental United States.
  • Domestic travel typically ranges from 20% to 25%, varying based on client engagement needs, conference participation, and business priorities.

Why Executive Leaders Join Gartner

Many Executive Partners join Gartner after distinguished operating careers because they want to continue making an impact while engaging with some of the world's most senior finance leaders. The role offers the opportunity to:

  • Influence and advise CFOs across diverse industries.
  • Remain connected to the most important trends shaping the future of finance.
  • Leverage decades of executive leadership experience in a highly strategic capacity.
  • Collaborate with an elite network of former and current business leaders.
  • Enjoy flexibility while continuing to operate at the highest levels of executive leadership.

Executive Partners are full-time Gartner employees with full benefits. The role can be based anywhere in the continental United States.

Performs the full range of Case Analyst investigative duties with the exception of Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) and Currency Transaction Report (CTR) filings, which are referred to and completed by BSA/AML Operations.   • Executes card actions (block, unblock, close, reissue) on Pathward Managed cards and submits Action Requests for Sponsorship cards through the established process, documenting the basis, date, and system used.
  • Documents all review activity, analysis, and dispositions in Actimize and applicable tracking spreadsheets, clearly and at the time the step is performed, to a standard understandable by a regulator, auditor, or QA reviewer.
  • Escalates SAR-eligible, immediate-attention, terrorist-financing, human-trafficking, or imminent-loss indicators same business day per the escalation procedures and prepares referral information for BSA/AML Operations.
  • Answers inbound and returns outbound calls related to fraud monitoring, card status, and cardholder verification, completing required after-call documentation.
  • Maintains service levels (SLAs), production, and quality standards for assigned workstreams in accordance with policies, procedures, and compliance requirements.
  • Other duties as assigned.

What You Will Need:

  • Attention to detail and accuracy in transaction analysis and documentation.
  • Ability to manage a daily workload and meet same-day and SLA-driven deadlines.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Self-sufficient and well organized with support; comfortable working across multiple systems and monitoring reports.
  • Foundational understanding of fraud red flags and typologies (e.g., account takeover, first-party fraud, card-not-present fraud) preferred.

description:
Persons in these roles are expected to work from our offices in Seattle. On-site requirements vary based on position and team. If you have questions about on-site work arrangements for this role, please ask your recruiter.

Research Intern, Undergrad: $94,320 (Annually)

Who You Are:

Are you interested in researching cutting-edge developments in AI applied to climate modeling? Do you have a passion for applying technology to do good in the world? If so, an Ai2 research internship in the Climate Modeling team may be the perfect opportunity. We will be offering 12-week internships during summer 2027. We will review applications and schedule virtual interviews for top candidates in January-February 2027.

Ai2 Research Internship Information:

  • Duration: 12 weeks
  • Start Date: Flexible
  • Candidates: A PhD student with a strong research background

Please apply by January 4, 2027, at 11:00pm Pacific Time to be considered for our Spring/Summer 2027 internships.

Who We Are:

Ai2’s Climate Modeling team (Ai2CM) has developed ACE, the world’s leading AI-based global atmosphere emulator for climate applications. ACE can be trained to replicate weather variability and climate change at 100 km horizontal resolution using historical observations or outputs from any physics-based climate model. It runs hundreds of times faster on a single GPU than such a model running on a supercomputer. For climate-planning applications, we have implemented diffusion-based super-resolution for downscaling ACE simulations to kilometer-scale local detail. We also recently began a collaboration with Google Research to advance NeuralGCM, a hybrid AI-physics model, for climate projection applications.

Your Next Challenge:

At Ai2, you will be working with world-class AI researchers and software engineers. We perform team-based, ambitious research, with a mandate to strive for big breakthroughs, not just incremental progress, in an exciting and interactive workplace.

Interns will develop and apply novel AI methodologies for projects such as: (1) account for the effects of disparate radiative forcing agents including aerosols within ACE; (2) improve representation of land processes or the stratosphere in ACE; (3) improve the generalization capabilities of NeuralGCM’s column-wise learned physics.

You will work closely with a technical mentor on project design, coding and testing. Your technical mentor will discuss project details with you before your start date.

Over the course of your time at Ai2, you will build your resume and leave an impact on Ai2 and the world. We have a beautiful office near a bike trail, the University of Washington and Lake Union; daily catered lunches; and great pay. Summer is the perfect season to explore Seattle and our great outdoors.

To see more about our current, future, and past interns at Ai2, check out the internship page on our website!

What You’ll Need:

  • Candidacy in a PhD program in computer or computational/data science, applied math/statistics, physical sciences (including atmospheric or ocean science) or engineering.
  • Strong skills in Python and collaborative software development in git; excellent communication skills.
  • Prior coursework and practical research experience in machine learning.
  • Graduate-level course work in atmospheric or climate science or some area of fluid dynamics is a plus.
  • Prior machine learning experience applied to autoregressive atmosphere or ocean modeling is a plus.
  • Eager to learn new skills and like to work in a challenging environment.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by a team member to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the functions.

  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position for long periods of time.
  • The ability to communicate information and ideas so others will understand. Must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations.
  • The ability to observe details at close range.
  • Can work under deadlines.

A Little More About Ai2:

Ai2 is a Seattle based non-profit AI research institute founded in 2014 by the late Paul Allen. Our mission is building breakthrough AI to solve the world’s biggest problems. We develop foundational AI research and innovation to deliver real-world impact through large-scale open models, data, robotics, conservation, and beyond.

In addition to Ai2’s core mission, we also aim to contribute to humanity through our treatment of each member of the Ai2 Team. Some highlights are:

  • We are a learning organization – because everything Ai2 does is ground-breaking, we are learning every day. With a wide variety of world-class AI experts as guest speakers, and our commitment to your personal on-going education, Ai2 is a place where you will have opportunities to continue learning alongside your coworkers.
  • We value diversity - We seek to hire, support, and promote people from all genders, ethnicities, and all levels of experience regardless of age. We particularly encourage applications from women, non-binary individuals, people of color, members of the LGBTQA+ community, and people with disabilities of any kind.
  • We value inclusion - We understand the value that people's individual experiences and perspectives can bring to an organization, and we are building a culture in which all voices are heard, respected and considered.
  • We emphasize a healthy work/life balance – we believe our team members are happiest and most productive when their work/life balance is optimized. While we value powerful research results which drive our mission forward, we also value dinner with family, weekend time, and vacation time. We offer generous paid vacation and sick leave as well as family leave.
  • We are collaborative and transparent – we consider ourselves a team, all moving with a common purpose. We are quick to cheer our successes, and even quicker to share and jointly problem solve our failures.
  • We are in Seattle – and our office is on the water! We have mountains, we have lakes, we have four seasons, we bike to work, we have a vibrant theater scene, and we have so much else. We welcome interest from applicants from outside of the United States.
  • We are friendly– chances are you will like every one of the 200+ (and growing) people who work here. We do.

MAKE A DIFFERENCE IN OREGON’S NATURAL RESOURCES!


Opportunity Awaits, Apply Today! We especially encourage students, early career professionals, and anyone interested in a career in fish, wildlife, and natural resources, to apply! Come learn and train with ODFW and help us fulfill our mission: To protect and enhance Oregon's fish and wildlife and their habitats for use and enjoyment by present and future generations.


As a Fisheries Assistant (Biological Science Assistant) in Enterprise, Oregon, you will conduct studies to investigate and compare juvenile life history and migration patterns of spring Chinook salmon and steelhead populations in the Grande Ronde and Imnaha basins. This position will directly support the operation of juvenile fish traps, assist with creel surveys, and participate in spawning ground surveys. Results of this study will improve our ability to develop adequate recovery programs for Chinook salmon and steelhead in Northeast Oregon. Duties include:

  • Operate incline plane and screw traps
  • Conduct angler surveys and spawning ground surveys
  • Survey juvenile fish populations
  • PIT tag juvenile Chinook salmon and steelhead
  • Collect and summarize scientific data

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. They are not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities and duties required.


During periods of intense monitoring activity, this position requires working long hours at irregular times, frequently on weekends, in adverse weather conditions and/or on slippery stream banks. Work requires driving long distances on gravel roads, possibly in adverse weather conditions. This position is physically demanding.


During sampling season from March-May, a large trap will be operated seven nights/days per week and will require working and camping at the remote field station near Asotin, WA. Onsite housing will be provided; however, facilities are rudimentary (camping).

title: Nattevakt, 40% stilling, turnus i ukedager og helger (over 18 + førerkort) - Circle K Ringdalskogen
description:
Job Description


Kjære fremtidige kollega,


La oss si det først som sist. Circle K er slett ikke jobben for alle, men den passer for mange. Og de menneskene elsker å jobbe her!


I tiden som nattevakt har vi sett kollegaer komme og gå. De som velger å kaste inn håndkleet sier ofte at jobben var for kompleks, at arbeidslista var for lang og at det rett og slett var for tøft å jobbe natten. De som står løpet ut har til felles at de tåler tempoet, og at de digger å kjenne på følelsen av å gjennomføre et godt stykke arbeid.


Det vi trenger nå, er en ålreit kollega og lagspiller som:


  • Trives med å jobbe natt og holder fokuset oppe selv om du styrer skuta alene hele vakten
  • En nattugle som elsker rutineoppgaver og sørger for å gjøre klar stasjonen til kollegaen som kommer på morgenen
  • Blir motivert av å levere topp service til alle som besøker stasjonen, og gjør sport i å bite tenna sammen og smile når kunden klager på rekesalaten for tredje gang
  • Holder hodet kaldt når det skjer uforutsette ting og løser disse med sunn fornuft
  • Er interessert i mat og motiveres av å steke den beste burger´n i mils omkrets
  • Stiller opp på kort varsel dersom noen har blitt syk, eller ved behov (og forventer det samme av andre)
  • Forstår at man må vaske toalett og gulv, selv om dette ikke alltid er favorittoppgaven
  • Er glad i mennesker, og tar ansvar for å holde stasjonsområdet like ryddig på utsiden som på innsiden
  • Ønsker å gjøre en innsats for et grønnere og mer bærekraftig samfunn langs veien


For deg som har ambisjoner om å bygge en karriere, får du gode muligheter til det i Circle K. Du får jobbe i et stort selskap der innsats og arbeidsmoral blir lagt merke til. Du får være med på selskapets endring for å møte kundens behov.


Høres dette interessant ut? Da foreslår vi at du tar kontakt med en gang!
Til denne stillingen vil du jobbe i en 40% nattvakt stilling. Turnus vil være i ukedagene og noe helg, og arbeidstiden er fra 23:00 - 07:00.

Det vil være mulighet for større stilling på sikt, eller å ta på seg flere vakter ved behov og ønske.


Vi ser etter deg som er selvstendig, ansvarsbevisst og pålitelig, og som trives med å jobbe natt. Du er serviceinnstilt, positiv og strukturert, tar initiativ og håndterer både travle perioder og uforutsette situasjoner på egen hånd. Du er fleksibel, har fokus på renhold, matsikkerhet og gode rutiner, og tar eierskap til arbeidsplassen. Erfaring fra butikk eller service er en fordel, men riktig innstilling og personlig egnethet vektlegges mest.


Man må være over 18 år og ha førerkort for å være aktuell for denne stillingen.
Oppstart og opplæring i Januar måned.


Vennlig hilsen oss på Circle K Ringdalskogen

title: NPD Development Technician Lead
description:

Working as one to help many.


POSITION SUMMARY

Supervising people/projects to assist with the creation and production of medical devices. The New Product Development (NPD) Technician Lead II supervises and works with Process Engineers to ensure manufacturing meets quality requirements and the project schedule, identifies process improvements for established products, determines equipment needs and protocols for optimal manufacturing, assists in the resolution of production problems as needed, and investigates and tests new, pilot, scale-up or revised production procedures. The NPD Technician Lead II also supports manufacturing, Sales & Marketing, and other lab departments as needed during product improvement stage. The New Product Development Technician Lead II ensures ProMed’s brand, philosophy, systems, policies, and procedures are properly implemented and observed.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Position duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

• Assists Engineers in the design, development, fabrication and assembly of products, equipment, and apparatus, creating work instructions and preparing test reports.

• Continuing responsibility for installation, modification, repair, and maintenance of the equipment in a laboratory.

• Coordinates daily schedules to assure department runs efficiently and customer needs are met.

• Assists NPD Manager with the planning and review of resources and training necessary to meeting department needs.

• Assists Engineers with process development and the associated documentation.

• Assists Engineers with writing/documenting processes.

• Implements and supports Research and Development initiatives related to new technology and release of new production components.

• Supports Tech Center projects and daily activities of the Tech Center department and other departments as requested and required.

• Thought partner to department for all process steps.

• Meets expectations of regular, reliable attendance.

• Other Duties As Needed: Any other duties and tasks as deemed necessary and appropriate.

QUALIFICATION, EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.


Required:

  • Associates degree or equivalent work experience.
  • At least 5 years of experience working with medical components development.
  • Ability to demonstrate increasing levels of responsibility within a silicone molding operation.
  • Ability to schedule, coordinate, track and document development projects statuses.
  • Must have Intermediate knowledge of Microsoft Office products to include, Word, Excel, Outlook.
  • Knowledge and/or training to ISO 13485 (current) standards, Medical Devices Quality Management System.
  • Commitment to continuous improvement company-wide.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills both written and verbal; professional, courteous and friendly personality; clearly conveys ideas and information and receives information effectively.
  • Excellent organizational, problem-solving and time-sensitive skills.
  • Ability to create positive working relationships with a diverse group of people including gender, ethnicity, age, and cultural and skill level differences.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to establish priorities and meet deadlines.


Preferred:

  • Bachelors degree in Process Engineering or equivilent


WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the principal roles and responsibilities of this job.

  • Exposure to heated/air conditioned, ventilated facilities with florescent lighting;
  • Exposure to building where a variety of chemical substances are used for cleaning, and/or operation of equipment;
  • The noise level in the work environment is usually minor;
  • Duties are performed indoors;
  • Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

PHYSICAL, SENSORY, COGNITIVE & NEUROLOGICAL DEMANDS

While performing the duties of this job:

  • The employee may be required to stoop, bend, squat, kneel, reach, stand, walk, lift, pull, push, grasp, talk, hear, see and use repetitive motions;
  • Specific vision abilities required include close vision such as to read handwritten or typed material and the ability to adjust focus;
  • The position requires the individual to meet multiple demands from several people and interact with internal and external people;
  • Employee moves about the building and be able to maneuver in tight spaces between desks, etc.;
  • Employee may have duties involving walking on even or uneven surfaces;
  • Employee occasionally to frequently use a whiteboard, which can require grasping whiteboard pens, reaching at, below, or above shoulder height and may require trunk or neck rotation to look back;
  • Employee may use computers, overhead projectors, TV, and other work-related equipment, which may require an approximately 25+ pound force to push or pull equipment;
  • It is necessary to grasp and manipulate pens, markers, scissors, staplers, etc. occasionally to frequently.
  • Employee must see and hear on a continuous basis as well as speak frequently;

Position varies from standing, sitting, walking, etc. On some occasions it may be necessary to move quickly, run, etc. over smooth or uneven surfaces.

  • Strong understanding of mobile application behavior, client-server communication and API-driven workflows
  • Experience with functional, regression, integration and exploratory testing
  • Strong defect analysis and troubleshooting skills, including the ability to review logs and isolate reproducible issues
  • Experience working with test management, issue tracking and source control tools
  • Familiarity with Agile software development and release processes
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to work collaboratively with Engineering, Product and QA teams
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple testing priorities
  • Ability and willingness to use AI-assisted tools effectively to support test development, analysis, troubleshooting and documentation
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience testing cybersecurity, identity, password management or other security-sensitive mobile applications
  • Familiarity with iOS automation frameworks such as XCUITest, Appium or similar tools
  • Experience testing authentication technologies such as biometrics, passkeys, MFA or SSO
  • Experience with API testing tools such as Postman
  • Familiarity with mobile performance, accessibility or network-condition testing
  • Experience validating mobile applications across both iOS and Android environments
  • Familiarity with TestFlight and App Store release workflows

Benefits

  • Medical, Dental & Vision (inclusive of domestic partnerships)
  • Employer Paid Life Insurance & Employee/Spouse/Child Supplemental life
  • Voluntary Short/Long Term Disability Insurance
  • 401K (Roth/Traditional)

Position Title:

Natural Hazard Planner (Limited Duration)

Job Description:

Join the Oregon Department of Land Conservation and Development (DLCD) as a Natural Hazards Mitigation Planner to update plans that reduce the risk from natural hazards.

A day in the life.

As the new Natural Hazards Planner you will:

  • Review existing natural hazard mitigation plans to identify appropriate methods and prioritize sections to update.
  • Engage the local community, technical experts, and elected officials in the planning process.
  • Obtain necessary information, data, and maps.
  • Assess risks from multiple natural hazards
  • Determine actions that would reduce the risks
  • Draft new or revised plan sections.
  • Ensure that the planning process and updated plan comply with requirements from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA)
  • Support local government staff during the local adoption process.

For the full position description, please email Jan.Guerrero@dlcd.oregon.gov.

Limited Duration

This position is primarily funded by grants from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). Currently DLCD has a grant to fund projects expected to run through January 31, 2028. DLCD may receive additional grants for additional projects to continue the position, but we cannot guarantee future funding.

DLCD Vision and Mission

Vision: An Oregon where everyone can live, work, and thrive.

Mission: The Department of Land Conservation and Development (DLCD) leads Oregon’s land use planning program for the benefit of current and future generations. DLCD partners with communities as they cultivate places where everyone can live, work, and thrive.

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

One of DLCD’s foundational goals is to become a diverse, equitable, and inclusive agency that implements an equitable and inclusive planning program for Oregon. Efforts are supported by the State of Oregon Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Action Plan and an agency Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) Committee and Work Plan.

At DLCD, all employees are expected to recognize value in individual and cultural differences; lead activities in their division to promote and foster a diverse workforce; actively engage in implementing the DEI Work Plan and associated activities including achieving the agency’s affirmative action objectives and goals.

We recognize that to successfully meet our mission and agency values, our commitment to racial equity, diversity, equity, and inclusion must be at the center of our work. DLCD values the lived and professional experiences of individuals from historically and currently underserved and under-resourced communities and honor our Government-to-Government relations responsibilities with Oregon’s federally recognized Native American Tribes. We are committed to building and sustaining an inclusive, belonging, and equitable working environment for all employees. Candidates with diverse racial, ethnic, and cultural backgrounds, language fluencies, lived experiences, and skillsets are encouraged to apply.

What’s in it for you:

  • Opportunity to collaborate with a team of talented professionals who are passionate about the agency’s mission and priorities.
  • Flexible work location, with a mix of remote and in-office work.
  • 11 paid holidays per year and additional personal business time off.
  • Comprehensive benefit package options.

The Benefits

The State of Oregon offers a competitive and affordable health and benefits package, including excellent medical, vision and dental coverage, paid holidays off, personal business leave, paid vacation, and paid sick leave. In addition to standard medical benefits and employee leave, the state also provides additional optional benefits, such as basic life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, and flexible spending accounts for health care and childcare expenses.

After a qualifying period, new employees are enrolled in the Oregon Public Service Retirement Plan (OPSRP). State employees also have access to benefits like deferred compensation plans through the Oregon Savings Growth Plan and the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program.

Join thousands of state employees who came for a job and stayed for a career!

Minimum Qualifications

This position in classified as a Planner 2. The minimum qualifications for a Planner 2 position:

A master's degree in Community, Urban or Regional Planning, Public Administration, Social Science, Civil Engineering, Architecture, Economics, Geography or a related field;

OR

A bachelor's degree in urban or Regional Planning, Public Administration, Social Science, Civil Engineering, Architecture, Economics, Geography or a related field AND one year of progressively responsible planning experience related to the job;

OR

Four years of progressively responsible planning experience related to the job;

OR

An equivalent combination of relevant education, training, and experience.

We’re Also Looking for:

• Experience in or knowledge of natural hazards, especially mitigation planning

• Experience in or knowledge of local government planning, especially land use planning in Oregon

• Strong writing skills

• Lived or professional experience serving individuals from historically and currently underserved and under-resourced communities

• Fluency in languages other than English, especially Spanish

You do not need to have all these qualities to be eligible for this position, but be sure to let us know which you do have in your cover letter and resume. We use that information to choose whom we will interview.

Tips for Interested Candidates

Your candidate profile, cover letter, and resume are the perfect place to display your interest in the position and highlight the skills and experience you will bring, making you the best candidate for the position. Failure to attach a cover letter and resume may result in a candidate’s disqualification. Successful candidates who are not yet a PERS participating member, will receive the 6.95% pay increase and begin the 6% employee contribution upon participating in PERS. DLCD employees are eligible for step increases on an annual basis, up to the top of the classification salary range.

title: Product Manager, HR Systems and AI Enablement
description:
About Marvell

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. Your Team, Your Impact

This role is an opportunity to join Marvell's HR organization as a product and program contributor driving high-impact, global initiatives. As part of the HR Product & AI Enablement team, you will own delivery of HR technologies, processes, and employee experiences across the HR ecosystem, and you will bring AI-enabled approaches to how Human Resources work. You will partner closely with Talent Acquisition, HRIS, People Services, Total Rewards, and other cross-functional HR groups to deliver scalable solutions that improve how employees and managers interact with HR products and services.

What You Can Expect


1. HR Product Delivery

  • Own end-to-end delivery of assigned HR technology and process initiatives, including scope, requirements, timelines, and release plans, under the direction of the HR Product & AI Enablement lead.
  • Write clear product requirements and user stories that guide HRIS and technical teams, and validate delivered functionality against them.
  • Maintain and groom the backlog for assigned workstreams, recommending priorities based on impact, feasibility, and alignment with HR's digital strategy.
  • Track milestones, dependencies, and success metrics for assigned initiatives, and report status to stakeholders and leadership.

2. AI Enablement

  • Identify and evaluate opportunities to apply AI tools and automation to HR and Talent Acquisition workflows, documenting use cases, expected value, and feasibility.
  • Build and maintain templates and guided workflows that help HR and TA teams use approved AI tools effectively.
  • Support pilots of AI-enabled features in Workday and other HR platforms, measuring adoption and business outcomes.
  • Partner with Legal, IT Security, and Privacy to develop and apply responsible-use guidelines for AI involving employee and candidate data.
  • Stay current on AI capabilities and HR technology trends, and share practical recommendations with the team.

3. Stakeholder Communication

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for product-related questions from assigned HR partners.
  • Provide regular updates to global stakeholders and gather feedback to ensure transparency and alignment.
  • Escalate priority conflicts or misalignment to the lead, and help ensure product work supports broader HR and Talent Acquisition strategies.

4. Risk & Issue Management

  • Identify risks across systems, processes, and timelines for assigned initiatives, and develop mitigation plans.
  • Monitor risks through the product lifecycle, escalating material risks early, and troubleshoot issues with HRIS and technical teams to root cause.

5. Systems Implementation & Integration

  • Define business requirements, goals, and success criteria for Workday ATS and related module enhancements, so the what and the why are clear before HRIS determines the how.
  • Partner with HRIS to prioritize and sequence system changes, and make scope trade-offs when delivery constraints arise.
  • Document data and process requirements for integrations with other HR systems, and confirm with HRIS that the integrated design meets the business need.
  • Coordinate user acceptance testing with HR and TA stakeholders, validating delivered functionality against requirements and confirming it achieves the intended business outcome.

6. Training, Change Management & Support

  • Develop training materials and deliver sessions for HR users on new tools, processes, and enhancements.

description:
Review Response Specialist

Position Title

Position summary

The Review Response Specialist writes the replies that local businesses across the United States put in front of their customers. You respond to online reviews and social comments on our clients’ behalf — thoughtfully, professionally, and with search visibility in mind — protecting and strengthening their reputation with every response.

This is a production seat with a craft standard: real volume, real deadlines, and no room for a careless sentence. You are writing in someone else’s voice, in public, about their business.

You are part of a team, but most of the day-to-day work is self-directed. You will also work directly with clients by email and phone on negative reviews and difficult situations. Standard working hours are 8:30-5 pm EST, with some rotating weekend coverage expected, not exceeding 40 hours per week.

Responsibilities

Accountable for:

  • Response quality: every reply must be accurate, on-brand, correctly toned, and free of grammar and spelling errors. It publishes under the client’s name, not ours.
  • Turnaround: responses delivered within the standard, every day, without a backlog building behind you.
  • Negative review handling: difficult feedback addressed in a way that resolves the situation for the customer and protects the client.

Lane 1: Response production

OWNS:

  • The quality and search-consciousness of every response you publish.
  • Your daily throughput against the turnaround standard.

RUNS:

  • Writing responses to reviews and social comments across Google, Facebook, DealerRater, Cars.com, Edmunds, Yelp, CarGurus, and other platforms.
  • Applying each client’s voice, guidelines, and content priorities.
  • Incorporating SEO best practices into response content.

Lane 2: Negative reviews and client partnership

OWNS:

  • The handling of negative reviews and comments, in direct partnership with the client.
  • The confidentiality of the client and customer information you handle, in line with Widewail’s data handling standards.

RUNS:

  • Email and phone communication with clients in support of their online reputation.
  • Recommending how a client could or should manage a difficult situation online.
  • Escalating situations that need a manager or a client decision before they escalate on their own.

Performance measures

The Review Response Specialist is evaluated primarily on:

  1. Response volume against the daily or shift standard.
  2. Quality and audit score, measured through review of published responses.
  3. Turnaround-time adherence and backlog age.
  4. Revision and correction rate.
  5. Handling of escalated negative reviews, measured through resolution and client feedback.

Specific standards and targets are set with your supervisor at hire and reviewed during the performance cycle.

First 90 days

By 30 days

  • You are writing publishable responses for a defined set of clients, with review before publication.
  • You know each of your clients’ voices, guidelines, and content priorities.

By 60 days

  • You are working independently at the turnaround standard for your assigned book.
  • You are handling routine negative reviews without escalation.

By 90 days

  • You are at full volume, replying to 4000-4500 reviews per month , working difficult reviews with direct client contact.
  • You have a point of view on what makes a response work, and you contribute it to the team.

Core competencies

  • Writing judgment — you know the difference between a reply that closes a situation and one that inflames it, and you can tell which one you have just written.
  • Voice discipline — you can hold someone else’s voice consistently across hundreds of responses, without letting your own leak through.
  • Composure — you can read hostile, unfair, or upsetting feedback all day and still write something measured.
  • Self-direction — you manage your own queue and your own deadlines without anyone checking on you.
  • Attention to detail — grammar and spelling are not negotiable, because the client’s name is on it.
  • Customer-service instinct — you default to resolving the problem rather than winning the argument.

Qualifications

Required

  • 1+ years of copywriting or content writing experience.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication. Proper use of grammar and spelling is an absolute must.
  • Familiarity with SEO and best practices for web content development.
  • Understanding of online reputation management and common review platforms.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and manage deadlines.

Preferred

  • Associate’s degree or higher in marketing, communications, business, or a similar field, or equivalent experience.
  • Automotive retail or dealer group experience.
  • Experience writing in a brand-governed or regulated environment.

Tools and systems

  • Slack, Google Business Profile, Facebook, DealerRater, Cars.com, Edmunds, and Cargurus, plus the Widewail platform.

Compensation and benefits

$19.50–$25.00 per hour, depending on experience. Widewail benefits include:

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage, with HSA, FSA, and dependent care account options
  • Company-funded Lifestyle Spending Account
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Paid parental leave
  • Combined time off and paid holidays
  • Remote-first working environment

  • Customer satisfaction (e.g., NPS, CSAT, DSAT)

Essential

  • AI proficiency and upskilling: Basic proficiency in AI-enabled tools, with a willingness to continuously learn, upskill, and adopt new digital technologies.

Don't rule yourself out if you don't tick every box. Depending on the role, transferable skills such as customer focus, communication, analytical thinking, problem-solving, accuracy and process discipline can be just as important as previous logistics experience.

Why join GSC?


Global work. Local teams. Real impact.

A career in GSC can take you in many directions. You can deepen your specialist expertise, move into people leadership, work in process excellence or transformation, build capability in training, or explore opportunities across the wider Maersk organization.

You'll have the opportunity to:

  • Learn through meaningful, hands-on experience.
  • Contribute to customer outcomes and better ways of working.
  • Develop your career through specialist, leadership, project and transformation pathways.

Ready to make your move?

If you're looking for a role where you can grow your skills, collaborate internationally and contribute to work with global impact, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and discover where a career with Maersk GSC could take you.

MAKE A DIFFERENCE IN OREGON’S NATURAL RESOURCES!


Opportunity Awaits, Apply Today! We especially encourage students, early career professionals, and anyone interested in a career in fish, wildlife, and natural resources, to apply! Come learn and train with ODFW and help us fulfill our mission: To protect and enhance Oregon's fish and wildlife and their habitats for use and enjoyment by present and future generations.


As a Smolt Monitoring Assistant (Biological Science Assistant)in Asotin, Washington, you will conduct field sampling activities needed to carry out smolt monitoring and/or comparative survival studies of salmon and steelhead in the lower Grande Ronde River. Duties include:

  • Conduct daily fish sampling and PIT tagging
  • Collect, record, and summarize biological data
  • Operate and maintain juvenile fish trap and small power boat

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. They are not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities and duties required.


During periods of intense monitoring activity, these positions require working long hours at irregular times, frequently on weekends, in adverse weather conditions and/or on slippery stream banks. Work requires driving long distances on gravel roads, possibly in adverse weather conditions. These positions are physically demanding.


The trap will be operated seven nights/days per week and will require working and living at the remote field station in adverse weather. Onsite housing will be provided; however, facilities are rudimentary (camping).


This position requires acquiring a Boater Education Certificate obtained through the Oregon State Marine Board within the first 30 days of appointment.

  • Assist in developing strategic communications, white papers, and briefing materials for senior DAF leadership on enterprise-level resilience topics.
  • Take ownership of specific project workstreams, developing work plans, tracking progress against milestones, and ensuring timely delivery of high-quality work.
  • Prepare for and actively participate in client meetings, including developing agendas, briefing on your areas of responsibility, and capturing key decisions and action items.
  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with mid-level government clients and stakeholders.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field such as Public Policy, Energy Policy, Water Policy, Political Science, Environmental Science, Engineering, Water Resource Management, or a related discipline.
  • 4-6 years of professional experience, with a significant portion in federal consulting, public policy analysis, or the energy/water/resilience sector.

  • Proven experience managing project tasks or workstreams, including tracking deadlines, coordinating with team members, and delivering a final product.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience drafting professional reports and briefings.
  • U.S. Citizenship is required. Ability to obtain and maintain a Department of Defense (DoD) Common Access Card (CAC).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in a relevant field.
  • Direct experience supporting the Department of War (DoW), Department of the Air Force, or another federal agency on energy, water, or installation resilience programs.
  • Water utility experience.
  • An active Secret security clearance.
  • Familiarity with DAF organizational structures (e.g., SAF/IEE, AFIMSC, AFCEC).

Role Overview:

Own the technical basis of Aquatech’s operations and maintenance (O&M) proposals for industrial water and wastewater treatment. The Technical Lead develops the operating scope, resource and consumption estimates, and technical qualifications that inform the commercial offer. Key responsibilities:

• Review RFPs, process flow diagrams, piping and instrumentation diagrams, design data, historical operating records and customer specifications. Participate in site assessments and technical discussions to resolve gaps before pricing.

• Define the O&M scope, including operating responsibilities, maintenance boundaries, customer interfaces, startup and steady-state requirements, and exclusions.

• Build and validate staffing by post and shift, including relief coverage, required skills, operator certifications and specialist support. Match coverage to plant workload and reliability requirements.

• Develop and document the technical inputs to the O&M cost model for chemicals, energy, water, consumables, membranes, maintenance, spare parts, subcontracted services and residuals handling. Validate the assumptions with Operations, Engineering, Performance Chemicals and Procurement as appropriate.

• Assess design capacity, influent variability, treatment limits, redundancy and existing equipment condition. Identify gaps that require additional scope, a technical qualification or a customer decision.

• Define the technical basis for performance guarantees, including operating limits, customer obligations and testing and acceptance criteria. Flag unresolved technical risks and quantify their cost and operating impact for internal bid reviews.

• Write the technical sections of proposals and support customer clarifications and negotiations. Maintain a clear record of assumptions, exclusions and commitments through award and handover.

Other duties as assigned.

title: Vulnerability & Attack Surface Management Analyst II
description:
About OpenLoop

OpenLoop was co-founded by CEO, Dr. Jon Lensing, and COO, Christian Williams, with the vision to bring care anywhere. Our telehealth support solutions are thoughtfully designed to streamline and simplify go-to-market care delivery for companies offering meaningful virtual support to patients across an expansive array of specialties, in all 50 states.

About the Role

OpenLoop’s mission is to bring care anywhere by powering telehealth solutions at scale. Security Operations at OpenLoop protects patient data, clinical operations, and the systems our partners build on. We handle PHI, we’re subject to HIPAA, and care delivery depends on our systems working.

We’re hiring a Vulnerability & Attack Surface Management Analyst II. Nobody at OpenLoop works on vulnerability management or attack surface management full-time today, so you’ll be the first. You’ll report to the Director of Information Security, who sets strategy and priorities for both programs. You’ll carry out that plan, and we expect you to tell us when the findings suggest the priorities should change.

Some context on where things stand. Our cloud inventory has grown about five times over this year and more than doubled in the last two months. We deployed Wiz eight months ago, and it’s finding far more risk than we currently have people to work. Vulnerability management gets squeezed in around other work, and attack surface management has barely started. We’re also rolling out a platform that lets internal teams publish their own applications, which will grow our external footprint faster than anything else this year.

The program is early. You’ll help build it, with a direction already set. You’ll take a very large set of findings and narrow it to what matters using the risk model we’re putting in place, get fixes shipped through engineering teams across the company, and run attack surface discovery on a regular schedule instead of only when a client asks.

What this role is not: forwarding scanner reports to engineering. You own the fix through verification. It’s also not incident response or forensics (you’ll work with our IR team, but your focus is exposure and remediation), not a GRC role (you’ll help with audits and client reviews, but the day-to-day work is operational), and not a tool evaluation role. The platforms are in place, and the job is getting results from them.

What You’ll Do

  • Run the vulnerability lifecycle day to day: discovery, validation, prioritization, remediation tracking, verification, and reporting across cloud workloads, containers, code repositories, and endpoints.

  • Prioritize by actual risk, not raw CVSS. Apply and improve our risk model, which weighs internet exposure, exploitability (CISA KEV, EPSS), asset criticality, and data sensitivity. When the model needs to change, bring the evidence. When something is being deprioritized, make that visible so the decision is made on purpose.

  • Build a reliable asset inventory. Combine cloud, endpoint, and SaaS inventory into one view, with a named owner for every asset that matters. Most assets don’t have an owner today, so this is your first and most important deliverable. After that, run external discovery on a set schedule to find what we have exposed to the internet, including things nobody told us about.

  • Drive remediation. Get fixes done through Engineering, IT, and Platform teams. Write tickets people can act on, agree on realistic timelines, escalate to the Director when you’re blocked, and confirm the fix is in place.

  • Fix problems at the source and automate repetitive work. Roll out hardened base images and dependency baselines so a single upstream change closes thousands of findings. We’ve piloted this and it works, and you’ll lead the broader rollout. Connect scanner and CNAPP APIs to ticketing and reporting. If you find yourself building the same report by hand twice, automate it.

  • Own web application security. Run dynamic scans of our web properties, work fixes through application teams, and use edge and WAF controls as temporary mitigation while the real fix ships. Keep track of which issues are mitigated and which are actually fixed.

  • Set up security checks for the new publishing platform. Make sure internally built, externally published applications are inventoried and scanned before they go live, and raise gaps early while the process is still being designed.

  • Manage vulnerability disclosure and bug bounty intake. Validate researcher reports, check them against known issues, respond promptly and professionally, and see valid reports through to a verified fix. Escalate disclosure and severity decisions to the Director.

  • Use AI tools in your daily work. Use Claude, coding assistants, and newer agent-based tools to triage at volume, correlate findings, draft remediation guidance, and produce reports. Use good judgment about what data goes into which tool, since we handle PHI. With this many findings and a small team, these tools are a core part of how the work gets done.

  • Track and report metrics. Report mean time to remediate, backlog burn-down, and SLA coverage. Prepare the reporting the Director presents to leadership, and pull together evidence for client, partner, and auditor requests in our HIPAA-regulated environment.

Who You Are

You own your work from start to finish. A finding is done when the fix is verified, not when the ticket is filed. You’re comfortable working a backlog that will never reach zero. You’re direct: you state your view, explain your reasoning, and welcome disagreement, including from engineers who push back on a severity rating. You’re willing to argue that something shouldn’t be worked, and you’re fine being overruled. When thousands of findings share one root cause, you go after the root cause. You treat patient safety and data integrity as requirements. You already use AI tools in your work, you have opinions about where they help and where they don’t, and you’re careful about what goes into them.

REQUIRED

  • 3 to 6 years in security, with significant hands-on experience in vulnerability management, attack surface management, or cloud security posture management.

  • Hands-on experience running and tuning a vulnerability scanning or CNAPP platform.

  • Experience prioritizing a large set of findings with a risk-based model, and the ability to explain how you made those calls. Working knowledge of CVSS, EPSS, and the CISA KEV catalog, and a view on how to use them together.

  • Cloud security fundamentals in at least one major provider (GCP or AWS preferred), including how workloads, identity, and network exposure fit together. Experience with container and image vulnerabilities and dependency (SCA) findings in code repositories.

  • Comfort starting with an incomplete inventory. Figuring out what exists and who owns it is a large part of this job.

  • Experience working directly with engineering teams to get fixes shipped.

  • Scripting skills (Python, PowerShell, or similar) sufficient to query APIs and automate reporting.

  • Regular, hands-on use of AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, or similar) in security work. Be ready to share specific examples of how they improved your speed or quality, and explain how you decide what’s safe to share with them when PHI, credentials, or sensitive data are involved.

  • Strong writing. You can write a ticket an engineer will act on and a risk summary an executive will understand, and you know those are different documents.

PREFERRED

  • VM and CNAPP platforms: Wiz especially, since it’s our primary platform and experience with it will shorten your ramp-up. Also useful: Orca, Prisma Cloud, Defender for Cloud, or Lacework; CrowdStrike Falcon Exposure Management or Spotlight; Tenable, Qualys, or Rapid7 for non-cloud assets.

  • Attack surface and asset inventory: external ASM tools and recon methods (DNS, certificate transparency, subdomain and shadow IT discovery), CAASM and inventory platforms such as Axonius or runZero, and SaaS discovery tools.

  • Application and edge security: DAST and edge/WAF platforms (Invicti, Burp Suite, Cloudflare, Akamai), and vulnerability disclosure or bug bounty programs (HackerOne, Bugcrowd), including researcher communication, report validation, and duplicate handling.

  • Platform and supply chain: hardened or minimal base images (Chainguard, distroless, or an in-house golden image program), Kubernetes and container security at scale (we run GKE and EKS), PaaS/edge hosting such as Vercel, Netlify, or Cloudflare Pages, SBOMs and software supply chain security, and automation connecting scanner APIs to Jira, Slack, or reporting pipelines.

  • Regulated environments: experience in healthcare, fintech, or another regulated industry, and hands-on HIPAA, HITRUST, or SOC 2 work, especially providing vulnerability management evidence to auditors and clients.

  • Certifications: GCLD, GCPN, GWEB, GSEC, AWS or GCP security specialty, OSCP, or equivalent experience.

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation

  • Medical, Dental & Vision

  • Flexible Spending / Health Savings Accounts

  • Generous PTO and hybrid-work flexibility

  • 401(k) with Company Match

  • Life Insurance, Pet Insurance, and more

Our Company

We have a relatively flat organizational structure here at OpenLoop. Everyone is encouraged to bring ideas to the table and make things happen. This fits in well with our core values of Autonomy, Competence and Belonging, as we want everyone to feel empowered and supported to do their best work.

Sound like a good fit? We’d love to meet you.
